translations.literal: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Gao Daoyue, Zhen Chen, Zhang Zuan, Gao Cong

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十八

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 28

sentences.zh: 韓麒麟程駿李彪孫昶高道悅甄琛高聰

translations.literal: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Sun Chang, Gao Daoyue, Zhen Chen, Gao Cong
translations.idiomatic: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Sun Chang, Gao Daoyue, Zhen Chen, and Gao Cong

sentences.zh: 孝文時，拜齊州刺史，假魏昌侯。

translations.literal: At the time of Emperor Xiaowen, he was appointed Inspector of Qizhou and provisionally made Marquis of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen he was appointed inspector of Qizhou and given the provisional title Marquis of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 在官寡於刑罰，從事劉普慶說麒麟曰：「明公仗節方夏，無所斬戮，何以示威？

translations.literal: In office he seldom applied punishments. His aide Liu Puqing said to Qilin, "Your Excellency holds your commission in midsummer yet have carried out no executions—how will you display your authority?"
translations.idiomatic: While in office he rarely imposed punishments. His aide Liu Puqing urged him, "Your Excellency has taken up your commission at the height of summer yet have not carried out a single execution—how will you make your authority felt?"

sentences.zh: 」麒麟曰：「人不犯法，何所戮乎？

translations.literal: Qilin said, "If the people do not break the law, whom should I execute?"
translations.idiomatic: Qilin replied, "If no one breaks the law, whom should I put to death?"

sentences.zh: 若必須斬斷以立威名，當以卿應之。

translations.literal: If executions are truly required to establish a reputation for severity, you yourself should supply the example.
translations.idiomatic: If heads truly must fall to establish a reputation for severity, you yourself ought to supply the example.

sentences.zh: 」普慶慚懼而退。

translations.literal: Puqing, ashamed and afraid, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Puqing withdrew, abashed and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 麒麟以親附之人，未階台官，士人沈抑，乃表請守宰有闕，宜推用豪望，增置吏員，廣延賢哲，則華族蒙榮，良才獲敘，懷德安土，庶或在茲。

translations.literal: Qilin, because men attached to the throne by kinship had not risen to court offices while scholars were suppressed, submitted a memorial requesting that when prefectural and district posts fell vacant, men of eminent local standing should be promoted, official posts increased, and worthy men widely recruited—then eminent clans would receive honor, able men obtain advancement, and cherishing virtue and settling the land might perhaps be achieved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin observed that men connected to the throne by kinship had not advanced to court office while scholars languished in obscurity. He therefore memorialized that when prefectural and county posts fell vacant, locally eminent men should be promoted, the roster of officials expanded, and worthy men recruited broadly—so that great clans might gain honor, able men secure advancement, and the people, cherishing virtue, settle peacefully on the land.

sentences.zh: 朝議從之。

translations.literal: The court deliberation adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 太和十一年，京都大饑，麒麟表陳時務曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe, when the capital suffered severe famine, Qilin submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Taihe era, when the capital was stricken by severe famine, Qilin submitted a memorial on affairs of the day, stating:

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，經國立政，積儲九稔，謂之太平。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity, in governing the state and establishing policy, stored grain for nine years and called that peace.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity, in governing the realm and establishing policy, laid up grain for nine harvests and called that true peace.

sentences.zh: 故躬藉千畝，以率百姓。

translations.literal: Therefore they personally plowed the thousand-mu field to lead the common people.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore personally plowed the sacred field to lead the common people by example.

sentences.zh: 用能衣食滋茂，禮教興行。

translations.literal: By this means clothing and food flourished and ritual instruction spread.
translations.idiomatic: Thus food and clothing flourished and ritual instruction took root.

sentences.zh: 逮於中代，亦崇斯業，入粟者與斬敵同爵，力田者與孝悌均賞。

translations.literal: Down to the middle dynasties they likewise honored this pursuit: those who contributed grain received the same rank as those who beheaded enemies, and those who labored in the fields received rewards equal to the filial and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the middle dynasties this pursuit was honored: men who contributed grain won the same honors as those who slew enemies in battle, and diligent farmers received rewards equal to those given for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 實百王之常軌，為政之所先。

translations.literal: This was truly the constant path of the hundred kings and the foremost concern of government.
translations.idiomatic: This was the constant practice of the hundred kings and the first priority of good government.

sentences.zh: 今京師人庶，不田者多；

translations.literal: Now among the population of the capital, many do not farm;
translations.idiomatic: Today in the capital, a great many people do not till the soil;

sentences.zh: 遊食之口，三分居二。

translations.literal: mouths that wander and consume—two parts in three.
translations.idiomatic: and of those who live by wandering and consumption, two-thirds have no fields at all.

sentences.zh: 蓋一夫不耕，或受其饑，況於今者，動以萬計？

translations.literal: For if one man does not plow, others may suffer hunger from it—how much more when today the numbers run to tens of thousands?
translations.idiomatic: When a single man fails to plow, others may go hungry because of it—how much worse when the idle now number in the tens of thousands?

sentences.zh: 故頃年山東遭水，而人有餒終，今秋京都遇旱，穀價踴貴，實由農人不勸，素無儲積故也。

translations.literal: Thus in recent years when Shandong suffered floods, people still starved to death; this autumn the capital met drought and grain prices soared—all truly because farmers were not encouraged and there were no stored reserves.
translations.idiomatic: That is why in recent years, though Shandong suffered floods, people still starved to death, and this autumn, when drought struck the capital, grain prices soared—all because farming was not encouraged and no reserves had been laid up.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下天縱欽明，道高三五，上垂覆載之澤，下有凍餒之人，皆由有司不為其制，長吏不恤其本。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, heaven-endowed and reverently wise, your Way surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, above extending the grace that covers and bears all, yet below are people frozen and starving—all because the responsible offices do not establish regulations and chief officials do not tend the root.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty, endowed by Heaven with surpassing wisdom, whose Way rises above even the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, extends from above the grace that shelters all beneath the sky—yet below, people freeze and starve, all because the responsible offices fail to set proper regulations and chief officials neglect the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 自承平日久，豐穰積年，競相矜誇，浸成侈俗。

translations.literal: Since peace has lasted long and harvests been abundant year after year, people vie in boasting and extravagance has gradually become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Peace has endured so long and harvests been so abundant year after year that people vie in ostentation until extravagance has become the norm.

sentences.zh: 故令耕者日少，田者日荒。

translations.literal: Hence plowmen grow fewer day by day and fields more desolate day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Hence those who plow grow fewer each day and fields lie more fallow each day.

sentences.zh: 谷帛罄於府庫，寶貨盈於市里，衣食匱於室，麗服溢于路。

translations.literal: Grain and silk are exhausted in the treasuries, precious goods overflow in the markets, food and clothing are wanting in the home, yet splendid dress floods the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and silk are exhausted in the government storehouses while precious goods overflow the markets; food and clothing are scarce within homes, yet splendid dress parades along every road.

sentences.zh: 饑寒之本，實在於斯。

translations.literal: The root of hunger and cold lies truly here.
translations.idiomatic: The root of hunger and cold lies here.

sentences.zh: 愚謂凡珍玩之物，皆宜禁斷。

translations.literal: I venture to say that all objects of precious play should be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that all luxury trinkets and curios should be banned outright.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之禮，備為格式，令貴賤有別，人歸樸素。

translations.literal: Rites for auspicious and inauspicious occasions should be fully set in prescribed forms, so that noble and humble are distinguished and people return to simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for joyous and mournful occasions should be codified in full, so that high and low are clearly distinguished and people return to plain living.

sentences.zh: 制天下男女，計口受田。

translations.literal: Regulate males and females throughout the realm, allotting fields by counted mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Register all men and women in the realm and allot fields according to household size.

sentences.zh: 宰司四時巡行，台使歲一案檢，勤相勸課，嚴加賞罰。

translations.literal: Chief officials should tour in the four seasons, capital envoys conduct yearly inspections, diligently encouraging cultivation with strict rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Chief officials should tour the countryside in all four seasons, capital inspectors conduct yearly reviews, and rewards and punishments should be applied strictly to encourage diligent farming.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，必有盈贍，雖遇凶災，免於流亡矣。

translations.literal: Within a few years there will surely be surplus; even if disaster strikes, exile may be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years there will surely be surplus grain; even if disaster strikes, the people may be spared mass flight.

sentences.zh: 往年校比戶貫，租賦輕少。

translations.literal: In past years, when household registers were checked and compared, rents and levies were light and few.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, when household registers were checked and compared, rents and levies were kept light.

sentences.zh: 臣所統齊州，租粟才可給俸，略無入倉。

translations.literal: In Qizhou, which I administer, grain rents barely suffice for salaries, with scarcely any entering the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Qizhou, which I administer, grain rents barely cover official salaries, with scarcely any surplus entering the granaries.

sentences.zh: 雖于人為利，而不可長久。

translations.literal: Though this benefits the people, it cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Though this benefits the people in the short term, it cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 脫有戎役，或遭天災，恐供給之方，無所取濟。

translations.literal: If military service arises or heaven sends disaster, I fear there will be no means to draw on for supply.
translations.idiomatic: Should war break out or heaven send disaster, I fear there will be no reserves from which to draw.

sentences.zh: 請減絹布，增益穀租，年豐多積，歲儉出振。

translations.literal: I request reducing silk and cloth levies and increasing grain rents, storing more in abundant years and releasing relief in lean years.
translations.idiomatic: I request that silk and cloth levies be reduced and grain rents increased, so that more is stored in abundant years and relief distributed in lean ones.

sentences.zh: 所謂私人之穀，寄積於官；

translations.literal: This is what is called the people's grain deposited in accumulation with the government;
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by the people's grain held in deposit with the state;

sentences.zh: 官有宿積，則人無荒年矣。

translations.literal: when the government has standing reserves, the people will have no years of famine.
translations.idiomatic: when the state maintains standing reserves, the people need never face famine.

sentences.zh: 卒官，遺敕其子，殯以素棺，事從儉約。

translations.literal: He died in office and left instructions to his son: bury in a plain coffin and keep the funeral frugal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, leaving instructions to his son to bury him in a plain coffin and keep the funeral simple.

sentences.zh: 麒麟立性恭慎，恆置律令於坐傍。

translations.literal: Qilin's nature was respectful and cautious; he always kept the statutes at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin was by nature respectful and cautious, always keeping the law codes at his side.

sentences.zh: 臨終之日，唯有俸絹數十疋，其清貧如此。

translations.literal: On the day of his death he had only several dozen bolts of salary silk—such was his integrity and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he possessed only several dozen bolts of salary silk—such was his integrity and poverty.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、燕郡公，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Regular Attendant at the Palace Library and Duke of Yan Commandery, with the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Yan Commandery, with the posthumous epithet Kang, meaning Peaceful.

sentences.zh: 長子興宗，字茂先。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingzong, style Maoxian.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingzong, courtesy name Maoxian.

sentences.zh: 好學有文才，位秘書中散。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had literary talent, and held the post of Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and possessed literary talent, rising to the post of Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈漁陽太守。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Governor of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed governor of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 子子熙，字元雍。

translations.literal: His son Zixi, style Yuanyong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixi, courtesy name Yuanyong.

sentences.zh: 少自修整，頗有學識，為清河王懌郎中令。

translations.literal: From youth he cultivated himself and had considerable learning, and served as Chamberlain for Prince Yi of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he cultivated himself diligently and acquired considerable learning, serving as chamberlain to Prince Yi of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 初，子熙父以爵讓弟顯宗，不受；

translations.literal: At first Zixi's father offered his noble rank to his younger brother Xianzong, who would not accept it;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zixi's father had offered his noble rank to his younger brother Xianzong, who refused to accept it;

sentences.zh: 子熙成父素懷，卒亦不襲。

translations.literal: Zixi fulfilled his father's lifelong intent and in the end did not inherit the rank either.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi honored his father's lifelong intent and likewise never inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 及顯宗卒，子熙別蒙賜爵，乃以先爵讓弟仲穆。

translations.literal: When Xianzong died, Zixi separately received a granted noble rank and then yielded the earlier rank to his younger brother Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzong died, Zixi received a separate grant of nobility and then yielded his original rank to his younger brother Zhongmu.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was the fraternal affection among the brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the mutual devotion among the brothers.

sentences.zh: 母亡，居喪有禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning with proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he observed mourning with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 子熙為懌所眷遇，遂闕位，待其畢喪後，復引用。

translations.literal: Because Zixi was favored by Prince Yi, his post was left vacant until mourning was complete, after which he was again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Yi favored Zixi, his post was left vacant until his mourning was complete, whereupon he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 及元叉害懌，久不得葬。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha killed Prince Yi, burial was long delayed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha murdered Prince Yi, burial was long delayed.

sentences.zh: 子熙為之憂悴，屏居田野。

translations.literal: Zixi grieved and wasted away over this and withdrew to live in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi grieved himself nearly to death over this and withdrew to live in seclusion in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 每言王若不得復封，以禮遷葬，誓以終身不仕。

translations.literal: He repeatedly said that if the prince were not restored to his fief and properly reburied, he swore never to take office for life.
translations.idiomatic: He declared repeatedly that unless the prince were restored to his fief and properly reburied, he would never take office again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 後靈太后反政，以叉為尚書令，解其領軍。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, made Yuan Cha Minister of the Masters of Writing, and relieved him of command of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Empress Dowager Ling restored her authority, she appointed Yuan Cha Minister of the Masters of Writing and stripped him of command of the guards.

sentences.zh: 子熙與懌中大夫劉定興、學官令傅靈舣、賓客張子慎伏闕上書，理懌之冤，極言元叉、劉騰誣誷。

translations.literal: Zixi, together with Prince Yi's Grand Master of the Palace Liu Dingxing, Director of the Academy Fu Lingyi, and Retainer Zhang Zishen, prostrated themselves before the palace gate and submitted a memorial vindicating Prince Yi's wrong and denouncing at length the slander by Yuan Cha and Liu Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi, together with Prince Yi's palace grandee Liu Dingxing, the director of the academy Fu Lingyi, and retainer Zhang Zishen, prostrated themselves at the palace gate and submitted a memorial vindicating Prince Yi, denouncing at length the false charges brought by Yuan Cha and Liu Teng.

sentences.zh: 書奏，靈太后義之，乃引子熙為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Dowager Ling approved their righteousness and thereupon appointed Zixi as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Dowager Ling was moved by their righteousness and appointed Zixi Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後遂剖騰棺，賜叉死。

translations.literal: Later Liu Teng's coffin was opened and Yuan Cha was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng's coffin was later opened for investigation, and Yuan Cha was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 尋修國史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was put to work on the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 建義初，兼黃門，尋為正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he served concurrently in the Yellow Gate and soon held the regular post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he served concurrently in the Yellow Gate Directorate and soon received the regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 子熙清白自守，不交人事。

translations.literal: Zixi kept himself pure and did not mingle in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi maintained his integrity and kept aloof from worldly entanglements.

sentences.zh: 又少孤，為叔顯宗所撫養。

translations.literal: Moreover, orphaned young, he was raised by his uncle Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he had been raised by his uncle Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 及顯宗卒，顯宗子伯華又幼，子熙愛友等於同生。

translations.literal: When Xianzong died, Xianzong's son Bohua was still young, and Zixi loved him as he would a brother of the same womb.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong died, leaving his young son Bohua, Zixi loved the boy as he would a brother born of the same mother.

sentences.zh: 長猶共居，車馬資財，隨其費用，未嘗見於言色。

translations.literal: Even when grown they still lived together; carriage, horses, and property were at his disposal, yet Zixi never showed it in word or expression.
translations.idiomatic: Even after they came of age they continued to live together; carriages, horses, and property were freely at Bohua's disposal, yet Zixi never so much as hinted at it in word or bearing.

sentences.zh: 又上書求析階與伯華，於是除伯華東太原太守。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial requesting to divide his rank with Bohua, whereupon Bohua was appointed Governor of Eastern Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting to share his official rank with Bohua, whereupon Bohua was appointed governor of Eastern Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及伯華在郡，為刺史元弼所辱。

translations.literal: When Bohua was in the commandery, he was insulted by the inspector Yuan Bi.
translations.idiomatic: While Bohua served in the commandery, he was humiliated by the inspector Yuan Bi.

sentences.zh: 子熙乃泣訴朝廷。

translations.literal: Zixi thereupon wept and appealed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi thereupon went weeping to appeal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔遣案檢，弼遂大見詰讓。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming issued an edict dispatching investigators, and Bi was severely reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered an investigation, and Bi was severely reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之禽葛榮，送至京師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 莊帝欲面數之，子熙以為榮既元凶，自知必死，恐或不遜，無宜見之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang wished to rebuke him to his face. Zixi thought that Rong, being the chief culprit, knew he must die and might not be submissive—there was no reason to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang wished to confront him in person. Zixi argued that Ge Rong, as the chief rebel, knew he faced certain death and might behave insolently—there was no good reason to receive him.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮聞而大怒，請罪子熙。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong heard of this and was greatly angered, demanding punishment for Zixi.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong heard of this and flew into a rage, demanding that Zixi be punished.

sentences.zh: 莊帝恕而不責。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang pardoned him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang pardoned him and imposed no penalty.

sentences.zh: 及邢杲起逆，詔子熙慰勞。

translations.literal: When Xing Gai rose in rebellion, an edict ordered Zixi to go comfort and reassure the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Gai rose in rebellion, an edict ordered Zixi to go and offer reassurance to the affected regions.

sentences.zh: 杲詐降，子熙信之。

translations.literal: Gai feigned surrender and Zixi believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gai feigned surrender, and Zixi believed him.

sentences.zh: 遷至樂陵，杲復反，子熙還。

translations.literal: When he reached Leling, Gai rebelled again and Zixi returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Leling, Gai rebelled again, and Zixi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 坐付廷尉，論以大辟，恕死免官。

translations.literal: He was handed over to the Minister of Justice, sentenced to death by the grand statute, but pardoned from death and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was handed over to the Minister of Justice and sentenced to death, but the sentence was commuted and he was merely dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，領著作，以奉冊勳，封曆城縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he headed the Bureau of Historiography and, for service in presenting the enfeoffment documents, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Licheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he headed the Bureau of Historiography and, for his service in presenting the enfeoffment documents, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Licheng.

sentences.zh: 天平初，為侍讀，除國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era he became Lecturer-in-Attendance and was appointed Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era he became lecturer-in-attendance and was appointed director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 子熙儉素安貧，常好退靜。

translations.literal: Zixi was frugal and content in poverty, always preferring withdrawal and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi lived frugally and was content in poverty, always preferring retirement and quiet.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴之始，百司並給兵力，時以祭酒閑務，止給二人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the move to Ye, all offices were allotted military retainers; because the director's post was considered a leisurely duty, he was given only two men.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first moved to Ye, every office was allotted military retainers; because the director's post was considered a light duty, he was assigned only two.

sentences.zh: 或有令其陳請者，子熙曰：「朝廷自不與祭酒兵，何關韓子熙事。

translations.literal: When some urged him to petition for more, Zixi said, "If the court itself does not grant retainers to the director, what has that to do with Han Zixi?"
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to petition for more, Zixi said, "If the court itself chooses not to grant retainers to the director, what business is that of Han Zixi?"

sentences.zh: 」論者高之。

translations.literal: Commentators held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators admired him greatly for this.

sentences.zh: 元象中，加衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was additionally made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was additionally appointed General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 先是，子熙與弟娉王氏為妻，姑之女也，生二子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zixi had married the Wang clan for his younger brother—a daughter of his aunt's—and she bore two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zixi had arranged for his younger brother to marry a woman of the Wang clan, a daughter of his aunt, who bore two sons.

sentences.zh: 子熙尚未婚，後遂與寡嫗李氏奸合而生三子。

translations.literal: Zixi himself had not yet married; later he had an illicit union with the widow Lady Li and she bore three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi himself had not yet married; later he entered an illicit liaison with the widow Lady Li, who bore him three sons.

sentences.zh: 王、李不穆，迭相告言。

translations.literal: Wang and Li were not harmonious and took turns denouncing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang and Lady Li could not abide each other and took turns lodging accusations.

sentences.zh: 子熙因此慚恨，遂以發疾。

translations.literal: Zixi, ashamed and resentful over this, thereupon fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and tormented by this, Zixi fell ill.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺戒不求贈諡，其子不能遵奉，遂至幹謁。

translations.literal: He died leaving instructions not to seek posthumous titles or epithets; his sons could not follow this and went so far as to lobby for them.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he left instructions not to seek posthumous honors, but his sons could not obey and went so far as to lobby the court for them.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wuding era he was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuding era he was posthumously appointed General of Agile Cavalry, with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 興宗弟顯宗，字茂親。

translations.literal: Xingzong's younger brother Xianzong, style Maoqin.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong's younger brother Xianzong, courtesy name Maoqin.

sentences.zh: 剛直，能面折廷諍，亦有才學。

translations.literal: He was upright and firm, able to rebuke face to face at court, and also had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and outspoken, able to speak bluntly in court debate, and possessed both talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 沙門法撫，三齊稱其聰悟。

translations.literal: The monk Fafu was acclaimed throughout the Three Qis for his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Fafu was renowned throughout the Three Qis for his quick wit.

sentences.zh: 嘗與顯宗校試，抄百餘人名，各讀一遍，隨即覆呼，法撫猶有一二舛謬，顯宗了無誤錯。

translations.literal: He once tested against Xianzong: copying out more than a hundred names, each read once through, then immediately called back in reverse—Fafu still had one or two errors, while Xianzong had not a single mistake.
translations.idiomatic: He once tested himself against Xianzong: they copied out more than a hundred names, each read the list once, then immediately recited it back in reverse order. Fafu still made one or two errors; Xianzong made none.

sentences.zh: 法撫歎曰：「貧道生平以來，唯服郎耳。」

translations.literal: Fafu sighed and said, "In all my life as a poor monk, I yield only to you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Fafu sighed and said, "In all my years as a monk, I have yielded to no one but you, sir."

sentences.zh: 太和初，舉秀才，對策甲科，除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was recommended as a xiucai, achieved first rank in the policy examination, and was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was recommended as a xiucai, achieved top rank in the policy examination, and was appointed assistant in the Bureau of Historiography.

sentences.zh: 後兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as vice director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既定遷都，顯宗上書：

translations.literal: After the capital relocation was decided, Xianzong submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: After the decision to move the capital, Xianzong submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 一曰：竊聞輿駕今夏若不巡三齊，當幸中山。

translations.literal: First: I have heard privately that if the imperial carriage does not tour the Three Qis this summer, it will visit Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: First: I have heard privately that if Your Majesty does not tour the Three Qis this summer, the imperial progress will visit Zhongshan instead.

sentences.zh: 竊以為非計也。

translations.literal: I venture to think this is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think this would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 當今徭役宜早息，洛京宜速成。

translations.literal: At present corvée labor should cease early, and the Luo capital should be completed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor ought to end soon, and the Luo capital ought to be finished quickly.

sentences.zh: 省費則徭役可簡，並功則洛京易就。

translations.literal: If expenses are reduced, corvée can be lightened; if efforts are combined, the Luo capital is easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce expenditures and corvée can be lightened; combine efforts and the Luo capital will be completed with ease.

sentences.zh: 願早還北京，以省諸州供帳之費，則南州免雜徭之煩，北都息分析之歎；

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty return early to the northern capital to save the provisioning costs of the provinces, so that the southern provinces are spared miscellaneous corvée troubles and the northern capital ceases the sighs of division;
translations.idiomatic: I urge an early return to the northern capital to spare the provinces the cost of provisioning the court, so that the southern provinces may be freed from miscellaneous corvée burdens and the northern capital relieved of the distress of being split apart;

sentences.zh: 洛京可以時就，遷者僉爾如歸。

translations.literal: the Luo capital can be completed in due time, and those who relocate will all return as if going home.
translations.idiomatic: the Luo capital can be completed in due time, and those who relocate will come as willingly as returning home.

sentences.zh: 二曰：自古聖帝必以儉約為美，亂主必以奢侈貽患。

translations.literal: Second: From antiquity sage emperors have taken frugality as beauty, while disorderly rulers have brought disaster through extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Second: From antiquity sage emperors have prized frugality, while disorderly rulers have brought disaster through extravagance.

sentences.zh: 仰惟先朝，皆卑宮室而致力於經略，故能基宇開廣，業祚隆泰。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider the former dynasty, all kept palaces humble and devoted effort to statecraft, and therefore could broaden the foundation and make the enterprise prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the former dynasty, our rulers kept their palaces humble and devoted themselves to statecraft, and thus broadened the foundation of the realm and secured a flourishing succession.

sentences.zh: 今洛陽基趾，魏明所營，取譏前代。

translations.literal: Now the foundations of Luoyang were built by Emperor Ming of Wei and drew mockery from earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: The foundations of Luoyang were laid by Emperor Ming of Wei and drew mockery even in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下損之又損之。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty should reduce them again and yet again.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to scale them back again and yet again.

sentences.zh: 頃來北都富室，競以第宅相尚，今因遷徙，宜申禁約，令貴賤有檢，無得逾制。

translations.literal: Recently in the northern capital wealthy households have vied in showing off their mansions; now with the relocation, prohibitions should be enforced so that noble and humble are restrained and none may exceed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Recently wealthy households in the northern capital have vied in ostentatious mansions; with the relocation now at hand, restrictions should be enforced so that high and low are held in check and none may exceed prescribed limits.

sentences.zh: 端廣衢路，通利溝洫，使寺署有別，士庶異居，永垂百世不刊之範。

translations.literal: Straighten and widen the thoroughfares, open and improve the canals, separate monasteries and offices, distinguish scholar and commoner dwellings, and establish a norm unalterable for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Straighten and widen the thoroughfares, open the canals to good use, separate monasteries from government offices, and keep scholars and commoners in distinct quarters—establishing a model that will endure unaltered for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 三曰：竊聞輿駕還洛陽，輕將數千騎，臣甚為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: Third: I have heard privately that when the imperial carriage returns to Luoyang, it will be lightly escorted by only several thousand horsemen—I greatly disapprove of this for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Third: I have heard privately that when the imperial carriage returns to Luoyang, it will travel with only a few thousand horsemen as escort—I cannot approve this for Your Majesty's safety.

sentences.zh: 夫千金之子，猶坐不垂堂，況萬乘之尊，富有四海乎。

translations.literal: A son worth a thousand in gold still will not sit with his feet overhanging the hall—how much more the sovereign of ten thousand chariots, possessing all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Even the son of a house worth a thousand in gold will not sit where a tile might fall upon him—how much more should the Son of Heaven, who possesses all within the four seas, take such precautions.

sentences.zh: 清道而行，尚恐銜橛之失，況履涉山河而不加三思哉。

translations.literal: Even when the road is cleared before travel, one still fears the mishap of a bit-strike; how much more when treading mountains and rivers without thrice considering?
translations.idiomatic: Even when the road is cleared beforehand, one still fears that a horse may bolt; how much more when crossing mountains and rivers without thinking thrice?

sentences.zh: 四曰：竊惟陛下耳聽法音，目玩墳典，口對百辟，心慮萬機，晷昃而食，夜分而寢。

translations.literal: Fourth: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's ears hear the sounds of the law, your eyes peruse the classics, your mouth addresses the hundred officials, your mind weighs ten thousand affairs—eating when the sun slants, sleeping when night is half spent.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: I reflect that Your Majesty's ears hear the teachings of the law, your eyes peruse the classical texts, your mouth addresses the hundred officials, and your mind weighs ten thousand affairs—eating only when the sun slants westward, sleeping only when night is half spent.

sentences.zh: 加以孝思之至，與時而深；

translations.literal: Added to this, filial thoughts reach their utmost and deepen with the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Added to this is the utmost depth of filial devotion, which grows deeper with the seasons;

sentences.zh: 文章之業，日成篇卷。

translations.literal: the work of literary composition daily completes scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: and the work of literary composition daily completes new scrolls.

sentences.zh: 雖睿明所用，未足為煩，然非所以嗇神養性，熙無疆之祚。

translations.literal: Though employed by sagely intelligence and not enough to be troublesome, this is not the way to conserve the spirit and nurture one's nature, nor to extend boundless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Though such exertions are well within Your Majesty's sagely powers, they are not the way to conserve the spirit, nurture one's nature, and extend boundless fortune.

sentences.zh: 莊周有言：「形有待而智無涯，以有待之形，役無涯之智，殆矣。

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou said, "The form has limits but wisdom has no bounds; to use a limited form to drive boundless wisdom is perilous."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Zhou said, "The body has its limits but the mind has none; to drive an unlimited mind with a limited body is perilous."

sentences.zh: 」此愚臣所不安也。

translations.literal: This is what your foolish servant finds unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: This is what your humble servant finds unsettling.

sentences.zh: 孝文頗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen largely accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen largely accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 顯宗又上言：

translations.literal: Xianzong again submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 前代取士，必先正名，故有賢良方正之稱。

translations.literal: Former ages in selecting scholars first rectified names, hence the titles Worthy and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In former ages, in selecting officials the court first rectified names, hence the titles Worthy and Upright.

sentences.zh: 今州郡貢察，徒有秀、孝之名，而無秀、孝之實。

translations.literal: Now when provinces and commanderies present candidates for inspection, there are only the names Excellent and Filial, without the reality of excellence and filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Today when provinces and commanderies present candidates, they bear only the labels Excellent and Filial, without the substance of excellence or filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷但檢其門望，不復彈坐。

translations.literal: Yet the court only examines their family standing and no longer impeaches and punishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court examines only their family standing and no longer holds anyone accountable.

sentences.zh: 如此則可令別貢門望以敘士人，何假冒秀、孝之名也？

translations.literal: If so, one might as well have a separate presentation of family standing to rank scholars—why falsely borrow the names Excellent and Filial?
translations.idiomatic: If so, the court might as well rank scholars solely by family standing—why maintain the false pretense of the Excellent and Filial labels?

sentences.zh: 夫門望者，是其父祖之遺烈，亦何益於皇家。

translations.literal: Family standing is the legacy of one's father and grandfather—what benefit does it bring the imperial house?
translations.idiomatic: Family standing is merely the legacy of one's forebears—what benefit does it bring the throne?

sentences.zh: 益于時者，賢才而已。

translations.literal: What benefits the age is talented men alone.
translations.idiomatic: What benefits the age is talent alone.

sentences.zh: 苟有其才，雖屠釣奴虜之賤，聖皇不恥以為臣；

translations.literal: If one has talent, though base as butcher, fisherman, slave, or captive, the sage emperor is not ashamed to make him a minister;
translations.idiomatic: If a man has talent, though he be as lowly as a butcher, fisherman, slave, or captive, the sage emperor will not disdain to make him a minister;

sentences.zh: 苟非其才，雖三後之胤，自墜於皁隸矣。

translations.literal: if one lacks talent, though a descendant of the three queens, he will cast himself down among the black-clad servants.
translations.idiomatic: if he lacks talent, though he be a descendant of the three queens, he will cast himself down among the common servants.

sentences.zh: 議者或云：今世等無奇才，不若取士於門。

translations.literal: Some who discuss the matter say: this age equally lacks extraordinary talent, so it is better to select scholars from eminent families.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that this age lacks extraordinary talent and that it is therefore better to select officials from eminent families.

sentences.zh: 此亦失矣。

translations.literal: This too is an error.
translations.idiomatic: This too is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 豈可以世無周、邵，便廢宰相而不置哉。

translations.literal: How can one say that because the age lacks a Duke of Zhou or Duke of Shao, one should abolish the office of chief minister and not appoint one?
translations.idiomatic: Surely one does not abolish the office of chief minister merely because the age lacks a Duke of Zhou or Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 但當校其有寸長銖重者，即先敘之，則賢才無遺矣。

translations.literal: One need only assess those who have even an inch of length or a grain of weight in merit and advance them first—then no worthy talent will be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: One need only assess whoever possesses even the smallest measure of merit and advance him first—then no worthy talent will be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 又曰：夫帝皇所以居尊以禦下者，威也；

translations.literal: He also said: The reason emperors dwell in exalted dignity to rule those below is authority;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: Emperors dwell in exalted dignity to rule those below through authority;

sentences.zh: 兆庶所以徙惡以從善者，法也。

translations.literal: the reason the myriad people turn from evil to follow good is law.
translations.idiomatic: the myriad people turn from evil to follow good through law.

sentences.zh: 是以有國有家，必以刑法為政，生人之命，於是而在。

translations.literal: Therefore those who have a state or a family must take penal law as government—the lives of the living depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore every state and every household must govern through penal law, for the lives of the people depend upon it.

sentences.zh: 有罪必罰，罰必當辜，則雖以捶撻薄刑，而人莫敢犯。

translations.literal: If the guilty are surely punished and punishments surely fit the crime, then even with light penalties of beating, no one dares offend.
translations.idiomatic: If the guilty are surely punished and punishments fit the crime, then even light penalties of beating will deter all offense.

sentences.zh: 有制不行，人得僥倖，則雖參夷之誅，不足以肅。

translations.literal: If regulations exist but are not enforced and people gain lucky escape, then even punishments of tearing apart the body are insufficient to bring awe.
translations.idiomatic: If regulations exist but are not enforced and people escape through luck, then even the most severe punishments are insufficient to inspire awe.

sentences.zh: 自太和以來，未多坐盜棄市，而遠近肅清。

translations.literal: Since the Taihe era, not many have been executed by market-display for theft, yet far and near are orderly and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taihe era, few thieves have been executed in the marketplace, yet far and near the realm has been orderly and pure.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，止奸在於防檢，不在嚴刑。

translations.literal: From this it is said: stopping wickedness lies in prevention and inspection, not in severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that stopping wickedness lies in prevention and inspection, not in severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 今州郡牧守，邀當時之名，行一切之法；

translations.literal: Now provincial and commandery governors and prefects seek the reputation of the moment and apply all-or-nothing methods;
translations.idiomatic: Today provincial and commandery governors seek momentary reputation and apply draconian methods;

sentences.zh: 台閣百官，亦咸以深酷為無私，以仁恕為容盜。

translations.literal: the central offices and hundred officials likewise all take deep severity as impartiality and kindness and forbearance as indulging thieves.
translations.idiomatic: while officials at court likewise regard deep severity as impartiality and kindness and forbearance as indulging thieves.

sentences.zh: 迭相敦厲，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: They urge one another on in turn and thus form custom.
translations.idiomatic: They urge one another on until this has become custom.

sentences.zh: 陛下居九重之內，視人如赤子；

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells within the ninefold palace and views people as newborn infants;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells within the ninefold palace and views the people as newborn infants;

sentences.zh: 百司分萬務之要，遇下如仇讎。

translations.literal: the hundred offices divide the essentials of ten thousand affairs and meet those below like mortal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: while the hundred offices, dividing among them the essentials of ten thousand affairs, treat those below like mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 是則堯、舜止一人，而桀、紂以千百，和氣不至，蓋由於此。

translations.literal: Thus there is only one Yao or Shun, while Jie and Zhou multiply by the hundreds and thousands—harmonious qi does not arrive, probably because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there is only one Yao or Shun above, while below Jie and Zhou multiply by the hundreds and thousands—harmonious qi never arrives, and the reason lies here.

sentences.zh: 宜敕示百官，以惠元元之命。

translations.literal: It is fitting to issue an edict showing the hundred officials, to show kindness to the lives of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict should instruct the hundred officials to show kindness to the lives of the common people.

sentences.zh: 又曰：昔周王為犬戎所逐，東遷河洛，鎬京猶稱宗周，以存本也。

translations.literal: He also said: Formerly the Zhou king was driven off by the Quanrong and migrated east to the He and Luo; Hao still was called Ancestral Zhou, to preserve the root.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: When the Zhou king was driven east by the Quanrong to the He and Luo region, Hao was still called Ancestral Zhou, to preserve the root of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 光武雖曰中興，實自草創，西京尚置京尹，亦不廢舊。

translations.literal: Guangwu though called Restoration in fact began from founding; the Western Capital still had a Capital Intendant appointed, and the old was not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Though Guangwu's reign is called a restoration, it was in fact a new founding; he still appointed a Capital Intendant for the Western Capital and did not abandon the old capital.

sentences.zh: 今陛下光隆先業，遷宅中土，稽古復禮，于斯為盛。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty gloriously uplifts the former enterprise, moves the residence to the central land, examines antiquity and restores ritual—at this it is most grand.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty gloriously uplifts the former enterprise, moves the capital to the central land, examines antiquity and restores ritual—never has this been grander.

sentences.zh: 按《春秋》之義，有宗廟謂之都，無謂之邑，此不刊之典也。

translations.literal: According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, where there are ancestral temples it is called a capital; where there are none, a town—this is an unalterable canon.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, where ancestral temples stand it is called a capital; where they do not, merely a town—this is an unalterable canon.

sentences.zh: 況北代，宗廟在焉，山陵托焉，王業所基，聖躬所載，其為神鄉福地，實亦遠矣。

translations.literal: How much more the northern capital of Dai, where ancestral temples stand, where imperial tombs rest, the foundation of royal enterprise and the burden of the sacred person—its being a divine homeland and blessed land is truly far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: How much more the northern capital of Dai, where the ancestral temples stand, where the imperial tombs rest, the foundation of the royal enterprise and the dwelling of the sacred person—its status as a divine homeland and blessed land is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 今便同之郡國，臣竊不安。

translations.literal: To make it now the same as other commanderies and states—I privately am uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: To reduce it now to the status of an ordinary commandery fills me with unease.

sentences.zh: 愚謂代京宜建畿置尹，一如故事。

translations.literal: I venture to say the capital of Dai should establish an inner domain and appoint an intendant, just as in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the capital of Dai should be established as an inner domain with an intendant appointed, following precedent.

sentences.zh: 崇本重舊，以光萬葉。

translations.literal: Honoring the root and valuing the old will glorify ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the root and valuing the old will glorify the dynasty for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「伏見洛京之制，居人以官位相從，不依族類。

translations.literal: He also said: "I humbly observe that in the regulations of the Luo capital, residents are grouped by official rank and follow one another, not by clan category.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I observe that in the regulations of the Luo capital, residents are grouped by official rank rather than by clan or occupation.

sentences.zh: 然官位非常，有朝榮而夕悴，則衣冠淪於廝豎之邑，臧獲顯於膏腴之裏，物之顛倒，或至於斯。

translations.literal: Yet official rank is not constant—honored in the morning and wretched by evening—then caps and gowns sink into neighborhoods of servants and lackeys, while slaves and attendants appear in rich districts; the inversion of things may reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet official rank is not constant—honored in the morning, ruined by evening—so that scholars sink into neighborhoods of servants while slaves and attendants appear in the finest districts; things may be inverted to this degree.

sentences.zh: 古之聖王，必令四人異居者，欲其業定而志專。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity surely made the four classes dwell apart, wishing their occupations settled and their wills focused.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity required the four classes to dwell apart, wishing their occupations settled and their wills focused.

sentences.zh: 業定則不偽，志專則不淫，故耳目所習，不督而就；

translations.literal: When occupation is settled there is no falsity; when the will is focused there is no dissipation—therefore what eyes and ears habitually learn is achieved without supervision;
translations.idiomatic: When occupation is settled there is no falsity; when the will is focused there is no dissipation—therefore what eyes and ears habitually learn is mastered without supervision;

sentences.zh: 父兄之教，不肅而成。

translations.literal: the teaching of fathers and elder brothers is accomplished without severity.
translations.idiomatic: and the teaching of fathers and elder brothers takes effect without severity.

sentences.zh: 仰惟太祖道武皇帝，創基撥亂，日不暇給，然猶分別士庶，不令雜居，伎作屠沽，各有攸處。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu, who founded the base and quelled disorder with no leisure even to eat, yet still distinguished scholar and commoner and did not allow mixed dwelling—performers, craftsmen, butchers, and vendors each had their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu, who founded the realm and quelled disorder without a moment's rest, yet still distinguished scholars from commoners and forbade mixed dwelling—performers, craftsmen, butchers, and vendors each had their proper place.

sentences.zh: 但不設科禁，買賣任情，販貴易賤，錯居渾雜。

translations.literal: But because no statutory prohibitions were set, buying and selling followed whim, the expensive was sold and the cheap bought, and mixed dwelling became confused and blended.
translations.idiomatic: But because no statutory prohibitions were established, buying and selling followed whim, the expensive was traded for the cheap, and quarters became confused and blended.

sentences.zh: 假令一處彈箏吹笛，緩舞長歌；

translations.literal: Suppose in one place zithers are plucked and flutes blown, slow dances and long songs performed;
translations.idiomatic: Suppose in one quarter zithers are plucked and flutes blown, with slow dances and long songs;

sentences.zh: 一處嚴師苦訓，誦《詩》講《禮》，宣令童齔，任意所從，其走赴舞堂者萬數，往就學館者無一。

translations.literal: in another place stern teachers train bitterly, reciting the Odes and lecturing on the Rites—if children are left to follow as they please, those who run to the dance hall number in the tens of thousands, while those who go to the schoolhouse are not one.
translations.idiomatic: in another stern teachers train diligently, reciting the Odes and lecturing on the Rites—if children are left free to choose, tens of thousands will run to the dance hall and not one to the schoolhouse.

sentences.zh: 此則伎作不可雜居，士人不宜異處之明驗也。

translations.literal: This is clear proof that performers must not dwell mixed together and scholars should not dwell in separate places.
translations.idiomatic: This is clear proof that performers must not dwell among scholars, and that scholars should not be scattered among other classes.

sentences.zh: 故孔父雲裏仁之美，孟母弘三徙之訓。

translations.literal: Therefore Master Kong spoke of the beauty of dwelling amid benevolence, and Mencius's mother magnified the lesson of thrice moving.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Confucius spoke of the beauty of dwelling amid benevolence, and Mencius's mother magnified the lesson of thrice moving house.

sentences.zh: 賢聖明誨，若此之重。

translations.literal: The bright teachings of sages and worthies are weighty as this.
translations.idiomatic: The teachings of sages and worthies carry such weight.

sentences.zh: 今令伎作之家習士人風禮，則百年難成；

translations.literal: Now if households of performers are made to learn the manners and ritual of scholars, a hundred years will hardly suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If households of performers are made to learn the manners and ritual of scholars, a hundred years will hardly suffice;

sentences.zh: 令士人兒童效伎作容態，則一朝可得。

translations.literal: if scholars' children are made to imitate the bearing of performers, it can be achieved in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: but if scholars' children are made to imitate the bearing of performers, it can be achieved in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 以士人同處，則禮教易興；

translations.literal: If scholars dwell together, ritual instruction is easily raised;
translations.idiomatic: When scholars dwell together, ritual instruction flourishes easily;

sentences.zh: 伎作雜居，則風俗難改。

translations.literal: if performers dwell mixed together, custom is hard to change.
translations.idiomatic: when performers dwell mixed among them, custom is hard to reform.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每選舉人士，則校其一婚一官，以為升降，何其密也。

translations.literal: Whenever the court selects scholars, it examines one marriage and one office for promotion or demotion—how meticulous!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court selects officials, it scrutinizes their marriage alliances and official posts for promotion or demotion—how meticulous!

sentences.zh: 至於伎作官塗，得與膏梁華望接閈連甍，何其略也。

translations.literal: Yet as for performers on the official path, they may join with noble grain and eminent standing, connecting gates and joining eaves—how lax!
translations.idiomatic: Yet performers on the official path may dwell door to door with the noblest families—how lax!

sentences.zh: 今稽古建極，光宅中區，凡所徙居，皆是公地。

translations.literal: Now in examining antiquity and establishing the pinnacle, gloriously dwelling in the central region, all who relocate dwell on public land.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as the court examines antiquity and establishes its pinnacle in the central region, all who relocate dwell on public land.

sentences.zh: 分別伎作，在於一言，有何為疑，而虧盛美？

translations.literal: Separating performers depends on a single word—what is there to doubt, that would diminish this great beauty?
translations.idiomatic: Separating performers requires only a single edict—what is there to hesitate over, that would diminish this great achievement?

sentences.zh: 又曰：自南偽相承，竊有淮北，欲擅中華之稱，且以招誘邊人，故僑置中州郡縣。

translations.literal: He also said: Since the false southern regime succeeded one another, usurping the Huai north, wishing to monopolize the title of Central States and also to entice border people, they therefore established expatriate Central Province commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: Since the southern regime succeeded one another, usurping the north of the Huai and claiming the title of Central States to entice border peoples, they established expatriate commanderies and counties of the Central Province.

sentences.zh: 自皇風南被，仍而不改，凡有重名，其數甚眾，非所以疆域物士，必也正名之謂也。

translations.literal: Since the imperial wind spread south, this has continued unchanged; wherever there are duplicate names, their number is very great—this is not the way to delimit territory and classify people; it is what is meant by rectifying names.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial influence spread south, this has continued unchanged; duplicate place names are now exceedingly numerous—this is no way to delimit territory and classify the people; the ancients called this failure to rectify names.

sentences.zh: 愚以為可依地理舊名，一皆厘革，小者併合，大者分置。

translations.literal: I venture to think one may follow the old geographical names and reform all at once—small ones merged, large ones divided and placed.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the old geographical names should be followed and all reorganized at once—small districts merged, large ones divided anew.

sentences.zh: 及中州郡縣，昔以戶少並省，今人口既多，亦可復舊。

translations.literal: As for Central Province commanderies and counties, formerly because households were few they were merged and reduced; now that population is great, the old may also be restored.
translations.idiomatic: As for Central Province commanderies and counties, formerly merged because households were few, they may now be restored as population has grown.

sentences.zh: 君人者，以天下為家，不得有所私也。

translations.literal: One who rules men takes the realm as home and may have nothing private.
translations.idiomatic: One who rules men takes the realm as his home and may keep nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 故倉庫儲貯，以俟水旱之災，供軍國之用。

translations.literal: Therefore granaries and storehouses are stocked to await flood and drought disasters and supply military and state use.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore granaries and storehouses are stocked to await flood and drought and to supply the army and the state.

sentences.zh: 至於有功德者，然後加賜。

translations.literal: Only when there is merit and virtue are additional grants then added.
translations.idiomatic: Additional grants should be made only to those who have earned merit.

sentences.zh: 爰及末代，乃寵之所隆，賜賚無限。

translations.literal: Down to the late age, favor became what was exalted and grants and gifts without limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the late age, favoritism had become the norm and grants knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 自比以來，亦為太過。

translations.literal: Since then this too has been excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Since then this too has been excessive.

sentences.zh: 在朝諸貴，受祿不輕，土本被綺羅，僕妾厭梁肉，而復厚賚屢加，動以千計。

translations.literal: The eminent at court receive salaries that are not light; their native soil is covered with brocade and gauze, servants and concubines sated with fine grain and meat—yet thick grants are repeatedly added, often reaching thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The eminent at court receive substantial salaries; their estates are draped in brocade, their servants and concubines sated with fine food—yet lavish grants are repeatedly added, often reaching into the thousands.

sentences.zh: 若分賜鰥寡，贍濟實多。

translations.literal: If distributed to widowers and widows, the relief would truly be great.
translations.idiomatic: If distributed to widows and orphans, the relief would be far greater.

sentences.zh: 如不悛革，豈「周急不繼富」之謂也？

translations.literal: If this is not reformed, is this not contrary to the saying "relieve urgency, do not aid the rich"?
translations.idiomatic: If this is not reformed, does it not violate the principle of relieving the urgent rather than enriching the wealthy?

sentences.zh: 又曰：諸宿衛內直者，宜令武官習弓矢，文官諷書傳。

translations.literal: He also said: All inner attendants on palace guard duty should have military officers practice bow and arrow, and civil officers recite the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: Palace guards on inner duty should have military officers practice archery and civil officers study the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 無令繕其蒲博之具，以成褻狎之容，徙損朝儀，無益事實。

translations.literal: Do not let them prepare their gambling equipment, forming an irreverent familiar bearing, vainly damaging court ritual without benefiting practical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They should not prepare gambling equipment and adopt irreverent familiar manners, vainly damaging court ritual without benefiting practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 如此之類，一宜禁止。

translations.literal: Matters of this kind should all be prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of this kind should all be prohibited.

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 孝文曾謂顯宗及程靈虯曰：「著作之任，國書是司。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once said to Xianzong and Cheng Lingbin: "The duty of the Historiography Office is to oversee the national records.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once said to Xianzong and Cheng Lingbin: "The Historiography Office oversees the national records.

sentences.zh: 卿等之文，朕自委悉；

translations.literal: Your writings, I myself entrust and know well;
translations.idiomatic: Your writings I know well myself;

sentences.zh: 中省之品，卿等所聞。

translations.literal: the rankings of the inner province, you have heard.
translations.idiomatic: the rankings at court you have heard discussed.

sentences.zh: 若欲取況古人，班、馬之徒，固自遼闊。

translations.literal: If you wish to compare with the ancients, Ban and Sima and their kind are naturally far beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to compare yourselves with the ancients, Ban Gu, Sima Qian, and their like are naturally far beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 若求之當世，文學之能，卿等應推崔孝伯。

translations.literal: If you seek among the present age for literary ability, you should rank Cui Xiaobo first.
translations.idiomatic: If you seek literary ability in the present age, you should rank Cui Xiaobo first.

sentences.zh: 」又謂顯宗曰：「校卿才能，可居中第。

translations.literal: " He also said to Xianzong: "Assessing your talent, you may rank in the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said to Xianzong: "Assessing your talent, you may rank in the middle grade.

sentences.zh: 」謂程靈虯曰：「卿與顯宗，復有差降，可居下上。

translations.literal: " To Cheng Lingbin he said: "Between you and Xianzong there is again a difference in rank; you may occupy lower-upper.
translations.idiomatic: " To Cheng Lingbin he said: "Between you and Xianzong there is again a difference; you may rank lower-upper.

sentences.zh: 」顯宗曰：「臣才第短淺，比于崔光，實為隆渥。

translations.literal: " Xianzong said: "Your servant's talent and rank are short and shallow; compared with Cui Guang, this is truly generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzong said: "Your servant's talent is modest and shallow; compared with Cui Guang, this ranking is truly generous favor.

sentences.zh: 然臣竊謂陛下貴古而賤今。

translations.literal: Yet your servant privately considers that Your Majesty honors antiquity and belittles the present.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I privately believe that Your Majesty values the past while undervaluing the present.

sentences.zh: 昔揚雄著《太玄經》，當時不免覆甕之譚，二百年外，則越諸子。

translations.literal: In the past Yang Xiong composed the *Classic of the Supreme Mystery*; at the time he could not avoid talk of "overturning the jar," yet after two hundred years it surpassed all the other masters.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Yang Xiong wrote the *Classic of the Supreme Mystery*; in his own day he could not escape mockery as one who had "overturned the jar," yet two centuries later his work surpassed that of all other masters.

sentences.zh: 今臣所撰，雖未足光述帝載，然萬祀之後，仰觀祖宗巍巍之功，上睹陛下明明之德，亦何謝欽明于《唐典》，慎徽于《虞書》。

translations.literal: What your servant has compiled today, though insufficient to gloriously set forth the imperial record, yet after ten thousand generations, looking up to behold the towering achievements of the ancestors and gazing upon Your Majesty's brilliant virtue, how would it defer to the reverent clarity in the *Documents of Tang* or the careful adherence in the *Documents of Yu*?
translations.idiomatic: What I have compiled today may not suffice to gloriously record the imperial reign, yet ten thousand generations hence, readers looking up to the towering achievements of your ancestors and beholding Your Majesty's luminous virtue will find nothing to envy in the reverent clarity of the *Documents of Tang* or the scrupulous virtue recorded in the *Documents of Yu*.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「假使朕無愧於虞舜，卿復何如堯臣？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Suppose I am not ashamed before Yu Shun—what then would you be compared with a minister of Yao?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Suppose I have nothing to be ashamed of before Yu Shun—what then would you compare to among Yao's ministers?

sentences.zh: 」顯宗曰：「陛下齊蹤堯、舜，公卿寧非二八之儔。

translations.literal: " Xianzong said: "Your Majesty tracks Yao and Shun together; are the ministers and grandees not surely the peers of the Eight Wise and the Two Worthies?
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzong said: "Your Majesty follows in the footsteps of Yao and Shun; surely the ministers and grandees are no less than the Eight Wise and the Two Worthies.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿為著作，僅名奉職，未是良史也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "You serve in the Historiography Office merely in name as one fulfilling duty—not yet a good historian.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "As historiographer you merely hold the title and perform the duty in name—you are not yet a fine historian.

sentences.zh: 」顯宗曰：「臣仰遭明時，直筆無懼，又不受金，安眠美食，此優於遷、固也。

translations.literal: " Xianzong said: "Your servant fortunately meets an enlightened age, writes with an upright brush without fear, and moreover accepts no gold—sleeping peacefully and eating well—this is superior to Sima Qian and Ban Gu.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzong said: "I am fortunate to live in an enlightened age, can write with an honest brush without fear, take no bribes, and enjoy peaceful sleep and good food—this is better than Sima Qian and Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 」帝哂之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor smiled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor smiled at this.

sentences.zh: 後與員外郎崔逸等參定朝儀。

translations.literal: Later he joined with Assistant Section Director Cui Yi and others to draft the court ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he worked with Vice-Director Cui Yi and others to finalize the court rituals.

sentences.zh: 帝曾詔諸官曰：「近代已來，高卑出身，恆有常分。

translations.literal: The Emperor once issued an edict to the officials, saying: "In recent times, high and low in origin have invariably had fixed distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once issued an edict to the officials saying: "In recent times officials of high and low status have invariably come from fixed backgrounds.

sentences.zh: 朕意所為可，復以為不可，宜校量之。

translations.literal: What We deem acceptable, others again deem unacceptable—this should be weighed and measured.
translations.idiomatic: What I consider acceptable, others deem unacceptable—this merits careful review.

sentences.zh: 」李沖曰：「未審上古已來，置官列位，為欲為膏梁兒地，為欲益政贊時？

translations.literal: " Li Chong said: "It is unclear—since high antiquity, in establishing offices and arranging ranks, was the intent to pave the way for sons of fine grain, or to improve governance and assist the age?
translations.idiomatic: " Li Chong said: "I wonder: since high antiquity, when offices were created and ranks assigned, was the purpose to carve out positions for the sons of the wealthy, or to improve governance and serve the times?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「俱欲為人。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Both are intended for people.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Both purposes serve people.

sentences.zh: 」沖曰：「若欲為人，陛下今日何為專崇門品，不有拔才之詔？

translations.literal: " Chong said: "If the intent is to serve people, why does Your Majesty today exclusively honor family status and lack an edict to promote talent?
translations.idiomatic: " Chong said: "If the aim is to serve people, why does Your Majesty today exclusively exalt family rank and issue no edict to elevate men of talent?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「苟有殊人之技，不患不知。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "If one has extraordinary human skill, one need not worry about going unnoticed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Anyone with exceptional ability need not fear being overlooked.

sentences.zh: 然君子之門，假使無當世之用者，要自德行純篤，朕是以用之。

translations.literal: Yet the gates of gentlemen—even if there is no one of use in the present age—must themselves be pure and steadfast in virtue, and We employ them for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even if a gentleman family produces no one useful to the present age, their character is inherently pure and steadfast, and that is why I employ them.

sentences.zh: 」沖曰：「傅岩、呂望，豈可以門見舉？

translations.literal: " Chong said: "Fu Yan and Lü Wang—could they have been recommended by family gate?
translations.idiomatic: " Chong said: "Could men like Fu Yue of Fu Rock and Lü Wang have been recommended on the basis of family standing?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如此濟世者希，曠代有一兩耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Such world-saving men are rare—an age may have but one or two.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Such rescuers of the age are rare—perhaps one or two in an entire era.

sentences.zh: 」沖謂諸卿士曰：「適欲請救諸賢。

translations.literal: " Chong said to the various ministers and scholars: "I was just about to ask the noble gentlemen for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong turned to the assembled ministers and said: "I had just meant to appeal to you gentlemen for support.

sentences.zh: 」秘書令李彪曰：「師旅寡少，未足為援，意有所懷，敢不盡言於聖日。

translations.literal: " Chief Secretary Li Biao said: "My troops and companions are few—not enough to serve as support; yet having something in mind, how dare I not speak fully on this sacred day?
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Secretary Li Biao said: "I have few allies here and cannot count on much support, but I have something on my mind and dare not withhold my full views on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 陛下若專以地望，不審魯之三卿，孰若四科？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty relies solely on territory and prestige, is it not unclear whether Lu's Three Ministers or the Four Categories were superior?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty selects men solely by land and family prestige, I ask: were the Three Ministers of Lu superior to Confucius's four categories of students?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「猶如向解。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "As with the explanation just now.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "The same answer as before applies.

sentences.zh: 」顯宗進曰：「陛下光宅洛邑，百禮惟新，國之興否，指此一選。

translations.literal: " Xianzong stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty has made Luoyang shine as the capital; a hundred rites are all renewed—the rise or fall of the state hinges on this one selection.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzong stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty has established glory at Luoyang; every ritual is being renewed—the nation's rise or fall turns on this single choice of officials.

sentences.zh: 且以國事論之，不審中秘監、令之子，必為秘書郎，頃來為監、令者，子皆可為不？

translations.literal: Moreover, speaking of state affairs—is it not unclear whether sons of the Central Secretariat Supervisor and Director must become Secretariat Gentlemen? Have all sons of recent Supervisors and Directors been qualified to serve?
translations.idiomatic: As a matter of state policy, must the sons of Central Secretariat supervisors and directors necessarily become secretariat attendants? Were all the sons of recent supervisors and directors truly qualified?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿何不論當世膏腴為監、令者？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Why do you not discuss the wealthy and fertile families serving as Supervisors and Directors in the present age?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Why not discuss the wealthy elite who currently serve as supervisors and directors?

sentences.zh: 」顯宗曰：「陛下以物不可類，不應以貴承貴，以賤襲賤。

translations.literal: " Xianzong said: "Your Majesty holds that things cannot be classified alike—nobility should not inherit nobility, nor baseness perpetuate baseness.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzong said: "Your Majesty holds that people cannot be lumped together—nobility should not simply inherit nobility, nor humble status perpetuate humble status.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「若有高明卓爾，才具俊出者，朕亦不拘此例。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "If there is one lofty, bright, and outstanding, with talent and excellence surpassing others, We too will not be bound by this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Where a man is eminent, brilliant, and outstanding in talent, I too will not be bound by this rule.

sentences.zh: 」後為本州中正。

translations.literal: " Later he served as the local Fairness Appraiser for his province.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was appointed provincial appraiser for his home province.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，車駕南征，以顯宗為右軍府長史、統軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the imperial carriage southward campaigned, Xianzong was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right Army Office and Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, during the southern campaign, Xianzong was made chief clerk of the Right Army Office and given command of troops.

sentences.zh: 次赭陽，齊戍主成公期遣其軍主胡松、高法援等並引蠻賊，來擊軍營。

translations.literal: Halting at Zheyang, Qi garrison commander Cheng Gongqi sent his army commanders Hu Song, Gao Fayuan, and others, jointly leading barbarian bandits to strike the army camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Zheyang, the Qi garrison commander Cheng Gongqi sent his subcommanders Hu Song, Gao Fayuan, and others to lead barbarian allies in an attack on the encampment.

sentences.zh: 顯宗拒戰，斬法援首。

translations.literal: Xianzong repelled the battle and beheaded Fayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong fought them off and took Gao Fayuan's head.

sentences.zh: 顯宗至新野，帝曰：「何不作露布也？

translations.literal: When Xianzong reached Xinye, the Emperor said: "Why not issue a victory proclamation?
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong reached Xinye, the Emperor asked: "Why haven't you issued a victory bulletin?

sentences.zh: 」顯宗曰：「臣頃見鎮南將軍王肅獲賊二三，驢馬數匹，皆為露布。

translations.literal: " Xianzong said: "Your servant recently saw the Pacifier-General of the South Wang Su capture two or three bandits and several donkeys and horses—yet he still issued victory proclamations for all of them.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzong said: "I recently saw Pacifier-General of the South Wang Su issue victory bulletins for capturing just two or three enemy soldiers and a few donkeys and horses.

sentences.zh: 臣在東觀，私每哂之。

translations.literal: Your servant at the Eastern Pavilion privately always smiled at this.
translations.idiomatic: When I was at the Eastern Pavilion, I used to laugh at that privately.

sentences.zh: 近雖仰憑威靈，得摧醜虜，兵寡力弱，禽斬不多。

translations.literal: Recently, though relying on Your Majesty's awe-inspiring power to crush the ugly enemy, our troops are few and strength weak—the captures and beheadings are not many.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, though I have relied on your martial authority to defeat the enemy, my forces are few and weak, and the prisoners killed and captured are not many.

sentences.zh: 脫復高曳長縑，虛張功捷，尤而效之，其罪彌甚。

translations.literal: If I again hoist long silk high and falsely magnify merit and victory, following the example of what is blameworthy, the offense would be all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: If I were now to hoist long banners and inflate my achievements, imitating what I once mocked, my offense would be all the worse.

sentences.zh: 所以斂毫卷帛，解上而已。

translations.literal: Therefore I put away the brush and roll up the silk, and submit a simple report—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have merely rolled up my brush and silk and submitted a brief report.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「如卿此勳，誠合茅社，須赭陽平定，檢審相酬。

translations.literal: " The Emperor smiled and said: "For merit such as yours, it truly suits enfeoffment with the feudal altar; once Zheyang is pacified, We shall examine and review and requite accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor smiled and said: "Merit like yours truly merits a feudal estate; once Zheyang is pacified, we shall review and reward you accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」新野平，以顯宗為鎮南廣陽王嘉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was appointed Advisory Adjutant to the Pacifier-General of the South, Prince Guang of Yangjia.
translations.idiomatic: " After Xinye fell, Xianzong was appointed advisory adjutant to Pacifier-General of the South Prince Guang of Yangjia.

sentences.zh: 顯宗上表，頗自矜伐，訴前征勳。

translations.literal: Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather self-praising and boastful, pleading his merits from the earlier campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong submitted a memorial in which he rather self-aggrandizingly pressed his claims for earlier campaign merits.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「顯宗進退無檢，虧我清風，付尚書推列以聞。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Xianzong is unrestrained in advance and retreat, damaging Our pure style—hand over to the Ministry of State for investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Xianzong lacks restraint in word and deed and has compromised our standards of integrity—refer the matter to the Ministry of State for investigation and report.

sentences.zh: 」兼尚書張彝奏免顯宗官。

translations.literal: " Concurrent Minister Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Concurrent Minister Zhang Yi memorialized for Xianzong's removal from office.

sentences.zh: 詔以白衣守諮議，展其後效。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to serve as Advisory Adjutant in plain clothes, to display his later accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed him to retain his advisory post as a commoner, so that he might prove himself in future service.

sentences.zh: 顯宗既失意，遇信向洛，乃為五言詩贈御史中尉李彪，以申憤結。

translations.literal: Xianzong, having lost favor, upon a courier's journey toward Luoyang, then composed a five-character poem presented to the Censor-in-Chief Li Biao to express his pent-up frustration.
translations.idiomatic: Disheartened, Xianzong happened to be traveling toward Luoyang on official business and wrote a five-character poem for the Censor-in-Chief Li Biao to vent his resentment.

sentences.zh: 二十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year.

sentences.zh: 顯宗撰馮氏《燕志》、《孝友傳》各十卷。

translations.literal: Xianzong authored the Feng clan's *Records of Yan* and *Biographies of Filial Friendship*, each in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong compiled the Feng clan's *Records of Yan* and *Biographies of Filial Friendship*, ten scrolls each.

sentences.zh: 景明初，追赭陽勳，賜爵章武男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming reign, his Zheyang merit was posthumously recognized, and he was granted the title Baron of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era, his merit at Zheyang was recognized posthumously and he was granted the title Baron of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 子伯華襲。

translations.literal: His son Bohua inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bohua inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 程逡，字驎駒，本廣平曲安人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Qun, style Linju, was originally of Qu'an in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jun, courtesy name Linju, was a native of Qu'an in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 六世祖良，晉都水使者，坐事流涼州。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Liang, Jin Director of Waterways, was exiled to Liangzhou for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Liang, a Jin Director of Waterways, was banished to Liangzhou for a crime.

sentences.zh: 祖父肇，呂光人部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Minister of the Interior under Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao served as Minister of Personnel under Lü Guang.
