sentences.zh: 駿少孤貧，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: Jun, orphaned young and poor, was famed for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early and poor, Jun was known for filial devotion during mourning.

sentences.zh: 師事劉延明，性機敏好學，晝夜無倦。

translations.literal: He studied under Liu Yanming; by nature quick-witted and fond of learning, day and night without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Yanming. Quick-witted and devoted to learning, he studied day and night without tiring.

sentences.zh: 延明謂門人曰：「舉一隅而以三隅反者，此子亞之也。

translations.literal: Yanming said to his disciples: "One who, shown one corner, returns with three others—this lad ranks next to such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming told his disciples: "When shown one corner of a subject, this boy can infer the other three—among you he ranks next to such a student.

sentences.zh: 」駿白延明曰：「今名教之儒，咸謂老莊其言虛誕，不切實要，不可以經世。

translations.literal: " Jun addressed Yanming, saying: "Today's Confucian scholars of orthodox teaching all say that Laozi and Zhuangzi speak empty and extravagant words, not cutting to practical essentials, and cannot govern the world.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun said to Yanming: "Confucian scholars today all say that Laozi and Zhuangzi speak empty, fantastic words with no practical bearing and unsuited to governing the world.

sentences.zh: 駿為不然。

translations.literal: Jun did not think so.
translations.idiomatic: Jun disagreed.

sentences.zh: 夫老子著抱一之言，莊生申性本之旨，若斯者，可謂至順矣。

translations.literal: Laozi composed words of embracing the One; Master Zhuang expounded the principle of the native nature—such as these may be called utterly accordant.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi taught the doctrine of holding to the One; Zhuangzi expounded the principle of innate nature—teachings such as these may be called perfectly in accord with the Way.

sentences.zh: 人若乖一，則煩偽生；

translations.literal: If people depart from the One, then troublesomeness and falsity arise;
translations.idiomatic: When people depart from unity, artifice and disorder arise;

sentences.zh: 爽性，則沖真喪。

translations.literal: if nature is violated, then pure truth is lost.
translations.idiomatic: when nature is violated, pure genuineness is lost.

sentences.zh: 」延明曰：「卿年尚幼，言若老成，美哉。

translations.literal: " Yanming said: "You are still young in years, yet your words are like those of a mature man—how fine.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanming said: "You are still young, yet you speak like a mature scholar—how admirable.

sentences.zh: 」由是聲譽益播。

translations.literal: " From this his reputation spread all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " His reputation spread all the more after this.

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍擢為東宮侍講。

translations.literal: Juqu Mujian promoted him to Eastern Palace lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mujian appointed him lecturer in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太延五年，涼州平，遷于京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiyan, Liangzhou was pacified, and he was moved to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiyan, after Liangzhou was pacified, he was relocated to the capital.

sentences.zh: 為司徒崔浩所知。

translations.literal: He came to be known by Grand Minister Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the attention of Grand Minister Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 文成踐阼，為著作郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, he was appointed Gentleman of the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, he was appointed historiographer.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，除高密太守。

translations.literal: During Huangxing, he was appointed Administrator of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangxing era, he was appointed administrator of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 尚書李敷奏駿實史才，方申直筆，請留之。

translations.literal: Minister Li Fu memorialized that Jun truly had historian's talent and was just then wielding an upright brush—requesting he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Fu memorialized that Jun truly possessed historian's talent and was in the midst of honest historical writing, and requested that he be kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 書奏，從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 獻文屢引駿與論《易》、《老》義，顧謂群臣曰：「朕與此人言，意甚開暢。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen repeatedly summoned Jun to discuss the meanings of the *Changes* and the *Laozi*, and turning to the ministers said: "When I speak with this man, my mind is very open and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen repeatedly had Jun discuss the meanings of the *Book of Changes* and the *Laozi*, and turning to the assembled ministers said: "When I talk with this man, my mind feels remarkably clear and at ease.

sentences.zh: 」問駿年，對曰：「六十一。

translations.literal: " He asked Jun's age; he replied: "Sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked Jun's age. Jun replied: "Sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「昔太公老而遭文王，卿今遇朕，豈非早也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "In the past Taigong, old, met King Wen—you now meet Us, is this not early?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Long ago the Grand Duke, already old, met King Wen—you meet me at sixty-one; is that not still early?

sentences.zh: 」駿曰：「臣雖才謝呂望，陛下尊過西伯。

translations.literal: " Jun said: "Your servant's talent falls short of Lü Wang, yet Your Majesty's honor surpasses the Western Duke.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun said: "My talent cannot compare with Jiang Ziya's, but Your Majesty's eminence surpasses that of the Western Duke.

sentences.zh: 覬天假餘年，竭《六韜》之效。」

translations.literal: I hope Heaven grants remaining years, to exhaust the effect of the *Six Secret Teachings*."
translations.idiomatic: I only hope Heaven grants me more years, that I may give all the service described in the *Six Secret Teachings*."

sentences.zh: 延興末，高麗王璉求納女於掖庭，假駿散騎常侍，賜爵安豐男，持節如高麗迎女。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanxing, the King of Goguryeo Rian sought to send a daughter into the palace; Jun was provisionally made Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry, granted the title Baron of Anfeng, and sent with credentials to Goguryeo to welcome the girl.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yanxing era, King Rian of Goguryeo requested to send his daughter to the imperial harem. Jun was appointed acting Regular Palace Attendant, granted the title Baron of Anfeng, and sent with imperial credentials to Goguryeo to escort the princess.

sentences.zh: 駿至平壤城。

translations.literal: Jun reached Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reached the city of Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 或勸璉曰：「魏昔與燕婚，既而伐之，由行人具其夷險故也。

translations.literal: Someone advised Rian, saying: "Wei formerly allied by marriage with Yan, then attacked it—because the envoy thoroughly knew its routes and defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Rian: "Wei once allied with Yan by marriage and then attacked it—because their envoy had learned its terrain and defenses in detail.

sentences.zh: 今若送女，恐不異于馮氏。

translations.literal: If you now send your daughter, I fear it will be no different from Lady Feng.
translations.idiomatic: If you send your daughter now, I fear the same thing will happen as with the Feng clan marriage.

sentences.zh: 」璉遂謬言女喪。

translations.literal: " Rian then falsely claimed the girl had died.
translations.idiomatic: " Rian then falsely claimed that the princess had died.

sentences.zh: 駿與璉往復經年，責璉以義方。

translations.literal: Jun and Rian went back and forth for a year, Jun reproving Rian with righteous teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Rian exchanged messages for a full year, Jun upbraiding Rian on grounds of righteousness and propriety.

sentences.zh: 璉不勝其忿，遂斷駿從者酒食，欲逼辱之，憚而不敢害。

translations.literal: Rian, unable to bear his anger, then cut off wine and food for Jun's attendants, wishing to force humiliation on him, yet feared and did not dare to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Rian, unable to contain his rage, cut off food and drink for Jun's attendants in an attempt to humiliate him, but fear held him back from doing Jun harm.

sentences.zh: 會獻文崩，乃還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen died, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen died, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 拜秘書令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 初，遷神主於太廟，有司奏：舊事，廟中執事官例皆賜爵，今宜依舊。

translations.literal: At first, when the spirit tablets were moved to the Grand Ancestral Temple, the responsible officials memorialized: by precedent, officials serving in the temple were all granted noble ranks—now it should follow the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial spirit tablets were first moved to the Grand Ancestral Temple, the responsible officials memorialized that by precedent all temple officiants received noble titles, and proposed following that practice.

sentences.zh: 詔百寮評議，群臣咸以為宜依舊事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to deliberate; the ministers all considered it appropriate to follow the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the full court to discuss the matter, and all the ministers agreed that the old practice should be followed.

sentences.zh: 駿獨以為不可，表曰：「臣聞名器為帝王所貴，山河為區夏之重，是以漢祖有約，非功不侯。

translations.literal: Jun alone considered it unacceptable and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant hears that titles and honors are prized by emperors, and mountains and rivers are the weight of the realm—thus Han's founder made a covenant: without merit, no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Jun alone objected, submitting a memorial: "I have heard that titles and honors are treasures of the emperor and that territory is the foundation of the realm. The founder of Han established the rule that there should be no enfeoffment without merit.

sentences.zh: 未見預事於宗廟，而獲賞於疆土。

translations.literal: One has not seen those who merely participated in ancestral temple affairs rewarded with territory.
translations.idiomatic: I have never seen men rewarded with territorial lordships merely for participating in ancestral temple rituals.

sentences.zh: 雖復帝王制作，弗相沿襲。

translations.literal: Though the institutions of emperors and kings need not be inherited in succession,
translations.idiomatic: Though each emperor may make institutions of his own and need not follow precedent,

sentences.zh: 然一時恩澤，豈足為長世之軌乎。

translations.literal: yet a momentary act of favor—can it suffice as a guideline for generations?
translations.idiomatic: can a one-time act of grace really serve as a model for generations to come?

sentences.zh: 」書奏，從之。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted and the court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 文明太后謂群臣曰：「言事，固當正直而准古典；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming said to the ministers: "In memorializing on affairs, one should indeed be upright and accord with classical antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming told the ministers: "Memorials should be upright and grounded in classical precedent;

sentences.zh: 安可依附暫時舊事乎！

translations.literal: how can one rely on temporary old practices!
translations.idiomatic: how can one simply cling to a temporary precedent from the past!

sentences.zh: 」賜駿衣一襲，帛二百匹。

translations.literal: " She granted Jun one suit of garments and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " She rewarded Jun with one suit of clothes and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「駿曆官清慎，言事每愜。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Jun through his offices has been pure and cautious; his memorials ever satisfy.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "Jun has served with integrity and discretion in every office, and his memorials always hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 門無挾貨之賓，室有懷道之士。

translations.literal: At his gate no guests bearing goods; in his hall scholars who cherish the Way.
translations.idiomatic: No briber crossed his threshold, and men devoted to the Way gathered in his home.

sentences.zh: 可賜帛六百匹，旌其儉德。

translations.literal: He may be granted six hundred bolts of silk, to honor his frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him six hundred bolts of silk in recognition of his frugal integrity.

sentences.zh: 」駿悉散之親舊。

translations.literal: " Jun distributed it all among relatives and friends.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun gave it all away among relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 性介直，不競時榮。

translations.literal: By nature upright and direct, he did not compete for worldly glory.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and forthright by nature, he did not chase after worldly fame.

sentences.zh: 太和九年正月病篤，遺命曰：「吾存尚儉薄，豈可沒為奢厚哉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Taihe, gravely ill, his testament said: "While I live I still esteem frugality—how can I in death be extravagant and lavish!
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of Taihe, gravely ill, he left testament instructions: "In life I have practiced thrift—how can I in death be laid out in lavish splendor!

sentences.zh: 昔王孫裸葬，有感而然；

translations.literal: In the past Wangsun was buried naked—moved by this he acted accordingly;
translations.idiomatic: Wangsun was buried unclothed in antiquity, and I am moved to follow his example;

sentences.zh: 士安籧篨，頗亦矯厲。

translations.literal: Shi An's rush mat also was quite a deliberate austerity.
translations.idiomatic: and Xi Kang's rush mat was likewise an admirable austerity.

sentences.zh: 可斂以時服，明器從古。

translations.literal: May I be enshrouded in seasonal garments; mingqi may follow ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: Let me be laid out in garments suited to the season, and let funerary objects follow ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 」初駿病甚，孝文、文明太后遣使者更問其疾，敕侍御師徐謇診視，賜以湯藥。

translations.literal: " When Cheng Jun first fell gravely ill, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent emissaries repeatedly to inquire after his illness, ordered the palace physician Xu Jian to examine him, and granted him decoctions and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Jun first grew seriously ill, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent messengers again and again to ask after him, ordered the palace physician Xu Jian to diagnose and treat him, and bestowed medicinal decoctions.

sentences.zh: 臨終，詔以小子公稱為中散，從子靈虯為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At his end, an edict appointed his young son Gongcheng as Secretariat Attendant and his nephew Lingqiu as Assistant in the Bureau of Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: At his deathbed, an edict appointed his youngest son Gongcheng as Secretariat Attendant and his nephew Lingqiu as assistant in the Bureau of Historiography.

sentences.zh: 及卒，孝文、文明太后傷惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming mourned him with deep regret.

sentences.zh: 賜東園秘器、朝服一稱、帛三百匹，贈兗州刺史、曲安侯，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: They granted him the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, and three hundred bolts of silk, and posthumously conferred Inspector of Yan Province and Marquis of Qu'an, with the posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the Eastern Garden funeral regalia, one set of court dress, and three hundred bolts of silk, and posthumously appointed him Inspector of Yan Province and Marquis of Qu'an, with the posthumous epithet Xian, meaning Discerning.

sentences.zh: 所作文章，自有集錄。

translations.literal: The essays he wrote have their own collected record.
translations.idiomatic: The writings he composed survive in a collected record of their own.

sentences.zh: 李彪，字道固，頓丘衛國人也，孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: Li Biao, courtesy name Daogu, was a man of Dunqiu in the Wei Principality; Emperor Xiaowen bestowed this name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao, styled Daogu, was a native of Dunqiu in the Wei Principality; Emperor Xiaowen granted him the name Biao.

sentences.zh: 家寒微，少孤貧，有大志，好學不倦。

translations.literal: His family was poor and humble; orphaned young, he was destitute, yet harbored great ambition and studied tirelessly without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and humble. Orphaned in youth and left in want, he nevertheless nursed great ambitions and studied tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 初受業于長樂監伯陽，伯陽稱美之。

translations.literal: At first he received instruction from Boyang, Supervisor of Changle, who praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied under Boyang, Supervisor of Changle, who spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 晚與漁陽高悅、北平陽尼等將隱名山，不果而罷。

translations.literal: Later, together with Gaoyue of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, and others, he intended to retire to a famous mountain, but the plan came to nothing and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with Gaoyue of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, and others, he planned to withdraw to a famous mountain, but the plan never came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 悅兄閭博學高才，家富典籍，彪遂於悅家手抄口誦，不暇寢食。

translations.literal: Gaoyue's elder brother Lu was erudite and highly gifted, with a household rich in classics; Biao therefore at Gaoyue's home copied by hand and recited aloud, having no leisure even for sleep or meals.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyue's elder brother Lu was learned and gifted, with a household rich in books. Biao therefore copied texts by hand and recited them aloud at Gaoyue's home, scarcely pausing even to sleep or eat.

sentences.zh: 既而還鄉里。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned home.

sentences.zh: 平原王陸睿年將弱冠，雅有志業。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingyuan Lu Rui was nearing twenty and already had refined aspirations and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingyuan Lu Rui was nearing twenty and already possessed refined aspirations and serious purpose.

sentences.zh: 娶東徐州刺史博陵崔鑒女，路由冀、相，聞彪名而詣之。

translations.literal: He took to wife the daughter of Cui Jian, Inspector of Eastern Xu Province, of Boling; passing through Ji and Xiang on his route, he heard Biao's reputation and went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to marry the daughter of Cui Jian, Inspector of Eastern Xu Province, of Boling, he passed through Ji and Xiang, heard of Biao's reputation, and went to call on him.

sentences.zh: 修師友之禮，稱之州郡遂。

translations.literal: He observed the rites between teacher and friend, praising him throughout the province and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He observed the courtesies due between teacher and friend and praised him throughout the province and commandery.

sentences.zh: 遂舉孝廉，至京師，館而受業焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Biao was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, went to the capital, and was lodged there while receiving instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was then recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, went to the capital, and was given lodging there while pursuing his studies.

sentences.zh: 高閭稱之朝貴，李沖禮之其厚，彪深宗附之。

translations.literal: Gao Lu commended him to the court nobility, and Li Chong treated him with great courtesy; Biao deeply attached himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu commended him to the court nobility, and Li Chong treated him with exceptional courtesy; Biao became deeply devoted to them.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，為中書教學博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he served as Doctor of Instruction in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he served as Doctor of Instruction in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後假散騎常侍、衛國子，使于齊。

translations.literal: Later he was acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Duke of Weiguo, sent as envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Duke of Weiguo on a mission to Qi.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞，參著作事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretary Assistant and took part in editorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretary Assistant and took part in historiographical work.

sentences.zh: 自成帝已來，至於太和，崔浩、高允著述國書，編年序錄為《春秋》體，遺落時事。

translations.literal: From Emperor Chengdi onward down to Taihe, Cui Hao and Gao Yun compiled the national history, arranging annals and records in Spring and Autumn format, omitting current events.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Chengdi down through the Taihe era, Cui Hao and Gao Yun compiled the national history in annalistic form after the model of the Spring and Autumn Annals, leaving out contemporary events.

sentences.zh: 彪與秘書令高祐始奏從遷、固體，創為紀、傳、表、志之目焉。

translations.literal: Biao and Secretary Director Gao You first memorialized to follow the Sima Qian and Ban Gu format, establishing the categories of Annals, Biographies, Tables, and Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Biao and Secretary Director Gao You were the first to memorialize for adopting the format of Sima Qian and Ban Gu and establishing the categories of Annals, Biographies, Tables, and Treatises.

sentences.zh: 彪又表上封事七條，曰：

translations.literal: Biao also submitted a sealed memorial of seven items, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Biao also submitted a sealed memorial in seven sections, saying:

sentences.zh: 古先哲王之為制也，自天子以至公卿，下及抱關擊柝，其宮室車服，各有差品。

translations.literal: When the sage kings of antiquity established institutions, from the Son of Heaven down to high ministers, and on to gatekeepers and watchmen, their palaces, carriages, and vestments each had distinct ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage kings of antiquity established institutions, from the Son of Heaven down to high ministers and on to gatekeepers and night watchmen, palaces, carriages, and vestments each had their proper rank.

sentences.zh: 小不得僭大，賤不得逾貴。

translations.literal: The lowly might not usurp the lofty, nor the base exceed the noble.
translations.idiomatic: The humble might not encroach upon the great, nor the lowly exceed the noble.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故上下序而人志定。

translations.literal: Only thus were upper and lower ordered and men's aspirations settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus were high and low set in order and men's hearts at rest.

sentences.zh: 今時浮華相競，情無常守；

translations.literal: In the present age people vie in display and extravagance, with no constancy in their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: In the present age people compete in display and extravagance, with no constancy in their hearts;

sentences.zh: 大為消功之物，巨制費力之事，豈不謬哉。

translations.literal: To pursue things that squander labor and grand undertakings that drain strength—is this not absurd?
translations.idiomatic: yet they pursue things that squander labor and grand undertakings that drain strength—is this not absurd?

sentences.zh: 夫消功者，錦繡雕文是也；

translations.literal: What squanders labor is brocades and carved ornament;
translations.idiomatic: What squanders labor is brocade and carved ornament;

sentences.zh: 費力者，廣宅高宇，壯制麗飾是也。

translations.literal: What drains strength is vast estates and towering halls, imposing scale and gorgeous adornment.
translations.idiomatic: what drains strength is vast estates and towering halls, imposing scale and gorgeous adornment.

sentences.zh: 其妨男業害女工者，可勝言哉！

translations.literal: The harm done to men's work and women's handicraft—can it even be fully stated!
translations.idiomatic: The harm they do to men's labor and women's handicraft—can it even be fully told!

sentences.zh: 漢文時，賈誼上疏，雲今之王政可為長太息者六，此即是其一也。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Han, Jia Yi submitted a memorial saying that of the six matters in royal government today worth long sighs, this is one of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Han, Jia Yi submitted a memorial saying that among the six matters in governance today worth long sighs, this is one.

sentences.zh: 夫上之所好，下必從之。

translations.literal: What those above cherish, those below are sure to follow.
translations.idiomatic: What those above cherish, those below are sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 故越王好勇而士多輕死；

translations.literal: Thus the King of Yue loved valor and his gentlemen were many who lightly faced death;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the King of Yue loved valor, and his gentlemen were many who lightly faced death;

sentences.zh: 楚王好瘠而國有饑人。

translations.literal: The King of Chu loved thin waists and his state had starving men.
translations.idiomatic: the King of Chu loved slender waists, and his state had starving men.

sentences.zh: 今二聖躬行儉素，詔令殷勤，而百姓之奢猶未革者，豈楚、越之人易變如彼，大魏之士難化如此？

translations.literal: Now the Two Sages personally practice thrift and simplicity, with edicts earnest and repeated, yet the people's extravagance is still unreformed—can it be that men of Chu and Yue change easily like that, while gentlemen of Great Wei are so hard to transform?
translations.idiomatic: Now the Two Sages personally practice thrift and simplicity, and their edicts are earnest and repeated, yet the people's extravagance remains unreformed—can it be that men of Chu and Yue change easily like that, while the people of Great Wei are so hard to transform?

sentences.zh: 此蓋朝制不宣，人未見德使之然耳。

translations.literal: This is surely because court regulations are not proclaimed and people have not witnessed virtue—this is what makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely because court regulations have not been proclaimed and the people have not witnessed virtue in action.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為第宅車服，自百官以下至於庶人，宜為其等制。

translations.literal: Your humble servant considers that for residences, carriages, and vestments, from all officials down to common people, graded standards ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant considers that for residences, carriages, and vestments, from all officials down to commoners, graded standards ought to be established.

sentences.zh: 使貴不逼賤，卑不僭高，不可以稱其侈意，用違經典。

translations.literal: So that the noble may not press upon the base, nor the low usurp the high; none may indulge extravagance to suit their whim, violating the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the noble would not press upon the base, nor the lowly usurp the high; none could indulge extravagance to suit whim and violate the classics.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second item says:
translations.idiomatic: The second section reads:

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：「主器者莫若長子。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "He who holds the vessels of the state—none is fitter than the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "He who holds the vessels of the state—none is fitter than the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 」《傳》曰：「太子奉塚嫡之粢盛。

translations.literal: " The Classic of Filial Piety says: "The heir apparent presents the sacrificial grain of the lineage heir.
translations.idiomatic: " The Classic of Filial Piety says, "The heir apparent presents the sacrificial grain of the lineage heir.

sentences.zh: 」然則祭無主則宗廟無所饗，塚嫡廢則神器無所傳。

translations.literal: " Thus if sacrifice has no master the ancestral temple has no one to receive offerings, and if the lineage heir is set aside the sacred vessel has no one to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus if sacrifice has no master, the ancestral temple has no one to receive offerings; if the lineage heir is set aside, the sacred regalia has no one to inherit it.

sentences.zh: 聖賢知其如此，故垂誥以為長世之法。

translations.literal: The sages knew this to be so, and therefore left instructions as a law for enduring generations.
translations.idiomatic: The sages knew this to be so, and therefore left instructions as a law for enduring generations.

sentences.zh: 昔姬王得斯道也，故恢崇儒術以訓世嫡。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Zhou kings obtained this Way, and thus broadly honored Confucian doctrine to instruct the lineage heirs.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Zhou kings grasped this Way and therefore broadly honored Confucian doctrine to instruct the lineage heirs.

sentences.zh: 世嫡於是乎習成懿德，用大協于黎蒸。

translations.literal: The lineage heirs thereby cultivated excellent virtue and greatly harmonized with the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: The lineage heirs thereby cultivated excellent virtue and greatly harmonized with the people.

sentences.zh: 是以世統黎元，載祀八百。

translations.literal: Thus the succession passed among the people and the sacrifices lasted eight hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the succession passed among the people, and their sacrifices endured eight hundred years.

sentences.zh: 逮嬴氏之君于秦也，弗以義方教厥塚子，塚子於是習成凶德，肆虐以臨黔首。

translations.literal: When the lords of Qin came to power, they did not instruct their heirs in righteousness; the heirs thus cultivated cruel virtue and tyrannized the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When the lords of Qin came to power, they did not instruct their heirs in righteousness; the heirs therefore cultivated cruel virtue and tyrannized the common people.

sentences.zh: 是以饗年不永，二世而亡。

translations.literal: Thus their feast of years was not long—they perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus their years of enjoyment were brief, and they perished in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 亡之與興，道在於師傅。

translations.literal: Whether a state perishes or rises depends on the tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state perishes or rises depends on the tutors.

sentences.zh: 故《禮》云：「塚子生，因舉以禮，使士負之，有司齊肅端冕，見於南郊。

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Rites says: "When the lineage heir is born, rites are performed for him; a gentleman carries him, officials with reverent bearing and proper caps receive him and present him at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Rites says, "When the lineage heir is born, rites are performed for him; a gentleman carries him, and officials with reverent bearing and proper caps present him at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 」明塚嫡之重，見乎天也。

translations.literal: " This shows the weight of the lineage heir—it is visible before Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " This shows the weight of the lineage heir—it is made visible before Heaven.

sentences.zh: 「過闕則下，過廟則趨，」明孝敬之道也。

translations.literal: "When passing the gate-tower he descends; when passing the temple he quickens his pace"—this shows the way of filial reverence.
translations.idiomatic: "When passing the gate-tower he descends; when passing the temple he quickens his pace"—this shows the way of filial reverence.

sentences.zh: 然古之太子，自為赤子而教固以行矣。

translations.literal: Yet the crown princes of antiquity, from infancy as suckling babes, were already instructed and truly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown princes of antiquity, from the time they were infants, were already instructed and truly put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 此則遠世之鏡也。

translations.literal: This is a mirror from distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: This is a mirror from distant ages.

sentences.zh: 高宗文成皇帝慨少時師不勤教，嘗謂群臣曰：「朕始學之日，年尚幼沖，情未能專。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, the Cultured Emperor, lamented that in his youth his teachers had not diligently instructed him; he once told the assembled ministers: "When I first began my studies, I was still very young and could not concentrate my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong, the Cultured Emperor, lamented that in youth his teachers had not instructed him diligently; he once told the assembled ministers, "When I first began my studies, I was still very young and could not fix my mind.

sentences.zh: 既臨萬機，不遑溫習。

translations.literal: Once I assumed the myriad affairs of state, I had no leisure for warm review.
translations.idiomatic: Once I assumed the myriad affairs of state, I had no leisure to review what I had learned.

sentences.zh: 今而思之，豈非唯予之咎，抑亦師傅之不勤。

translations.literal: Reflecting on it now—is this not my fault alone, but also the tutors' failure to be diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on it now—is this not my fault alone, but also the tutors' failure to be diligent?

sentences.zh: 」尚書李䐶免冠而謝。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works Li Chong removed his cap and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Chong removed his cap and apologized.

sentences.zh: 此則近日之可鑒也。

translations.literal: This is a recent mirror one may consult.
translations.idiomatic: This is a recent example one may take as a warning.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太皇太后翼贊高宗，訓成顯祖，使巍巍之功，邈乎前王。

translations.literal: I reverently consider that the Grand Empress Dowager aided Emperor Gaozong and instructed Emperor Xianzu, enabling towering achievements far surpassing earlier kings.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently consider that the Grand Empress Dowager aided Emperor Gaozong and instructed Emperor Xianzu, enabling towering achievements far surpassing the kings of old.

sentences.zh: 陛下幼蒙鞠誨，聖敬日躋，及儲宮誕育，復親撫誥，日省月課，實勞神慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, from youth nurtured in instruction, grows daily in sacred reverence; and when the Heir Apparent was born, you personally nurtured and instructed him, examining daily and reviewing monthly—truly this has taxed your mind and care.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, nurtured in instruction from youth, grows daily in sacred reverence; and when the Heir Apparent was born, you personally nurtured and instructed him, examining him daily and reviewing his progress monthly—truly this has taxed your mind and care.

sentences.zh: 今誠宜准古立師傅，以詔導太子。

translations.literal: Now it is truly fitting to establish tutors according to antiquity, to instruct and guide the Crown Prince by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is truly fitting to establish tutors according to antiquity and instruct and guide the Crown Prince by edict.

sentences.zh: 詔導正則太子正，太子正則皇家慶，皇家慶則人事幸甚矣。

translations.literal: When instruction by edict is upright, the Crown Prince is upright; when the Crown Prince is upright, the imperial house is blessed; when the imperial house is blessed, the affairs of men are exceedingly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: When instruction by edict is upright, the Crown Prince is upright; when the Crown Prince is upright, the imperial house is blessed; when the imperial house is blessed, the affairs of the realm are exceedingly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：

translations.literal: The third item says:
translations.idiomatic: The third section reads:

sentences.zh: 《記》云：國無三年之儲，謂國非其國。

translations.literal: The Record says: A state without three years' stores of grain cannot be called a state.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, "A state without three years' stores of grain cannot be called a state."

sentences.zh: 光武以一畝不實，罪及牧守。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu, for a single mu that failed to yield, punished the prefects and governors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu punished prefects and governors when even a single mu failed to yield.

sentences.zh: 聖人之憂世重谷，殷勤如彼；

translations.literal: The sages' concern for the world and esteem for grain was as earnest as that;
translations.idiomatic: The sages' concern for the world and esteem for grain was as earnest as that;

sentences.zh: 明君之恤人勸農，相切若此。

translations.literal: A bright ruler's care for the people and encouragement of farming was as pressing as this.
translations.idiomatic: a bright ruler's care for the people and encouragement of farming was as pressing as this.

sentences.zh: 頃年山東饑，去歲京師儉，內外人庶，出入就豐。

translations.literal: In recent years the east of the mountains suffered famine; last year the capital region was lean; within and without, officials and commoners went out to seek abundance elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the region east of the mountains suffered famine; last year the capital region was lean; officials and commoners within and without the court went out to seek plenty elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 既廢營產，疲困乃加，又於國體，實有虛損。

translations.literal: Abandoning their farms and property, exhaustion was added to exhaustion; to the body politic as well there was real depletion.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning their farms and property, they added exhaustion to exhaustion; the body politic as well suffered real depletion.

sentences.zh: 若先多積穀，安而給之，豈有驅督老弱，糊口千里之外。

translations.literal: If grain had first been accumulated in abundance and distributed in peace, how could there have been driving and pressing of the aged and weak to scrape a living a thousand li away?
translations.idiomatic: If grain had first been accumulated in abundance and distributed in peace, how could the aged and weak have been driven and pressed to scrape a living a thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 以今況古，誠可懼也。

translations.literal: Weighing the present against antiquity, this is truly something to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the present against antiquity, this is truly something to fear.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜析州郡常調九分之二，京都度支歲用之餘，各立官司。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that two-ninths of the regular levies from provinces and commanderies, and the surplus of the capital's annual expenditures, should each be placed under dedicated offices.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that two-ninths of the regular levies from provinces and commanderies, together with the surplus of the capital's annual expenditures, should each be placed under dedicated offices.

sentences.zh: 年豐糴積于倉，時儉則加私之二，糶之於人。

translations.literal: In years of plenty grain should be purchased and stored in granaries; in lean seasons add a two-tenths premium and sell to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In years of plenty grain should be purchased and stored in granaries; in lean seasons a two-tenths premium should be added and grain sold to the people.

sentences.zh: 如此，人必事田以買官絹，又務貯財以取官粟。

translations.literal: Thus people will surely cultivate fields to buy official silk, and also strive to store wealth to obtain official grain.
translations.idiomatic: Thus people will surely cultivate fields to buy official silk and also strive to store wealth to obtain official grain.

sentences.zh: 年登則常積，歲凶則直給。

translations.literal: In prosperous years stores will be regularly accumulated; in famine years they will be directly distributed.
translations.idiomatic: In prosperous years stores will be regularly accumulated; in famine years they will be directly distributed.

sentences.zh: 又別立農官，取州郡戶十分之一以為屯人。

translations.literal: Also establish separate agricultural offices, taking one-tenth of households from each province and commandery as colonists.
translations.idiomatic: Separate agricultural offices should also be established, taking one-tenth of households from each province and commandery as colonists.

sentences.zh: 相水陸之宜，料頃畝之數，以贓贖雜物余財市牛科給，令其肆力。

translations.literal: According with the suitability of land and water, calculating the number of mu, use fines and miscellaneous revenues and surplus funds to purchase cattle and assign by quota, ordering them to exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: According with the suitability of land and water and calculating the number of mu, fines, miscellaneous revenues, and surplus funds should be used to purchase cattle and assign them by quota, ordering the colonists to exert their strength.

sentences.zh: 一夫之田，歲責六十斛，甄其正課並征戍雜役。

translations.literal: For each man's field, sixty hu per year is required; assess the regular tax together with frontier garrison and miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Each man's field would be assessed at sixty hu per year, together with the regular tax, frontier garrison duty, and miscellaneous corvée.

sentences.zh: 行此二事，數年之中，則穀積而人足，雖災不害。

translations.literal: Implementing these two measures, within a few years grain will accumulate and the people will be provided for—even disaster will not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Implementing these two measures, within a few years grain will accumulate and the people will be provided for—even disaster will not harm them.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞前代明王皆務懷遠人，禮賢引滯。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that enlightened kings of former ages all devoted themselves to cherishing distant people and honoring the worthy, drawing in those left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that enlightened kings of former ages all devoted themselves to cherishing distant peoples, honoring the worthy, and drawing in those who had been overlooked.

sentences.zh: 故漢高過趙，求樂毅之胄；

translations.literal: Thus Emperor Gaozu of Han, passing through Zhao, sought descendants of Yue Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Gaozu of Han, passing through Zhao, sought descendants of Yue Yi;

sentences.zh: 晉武廓定，旌吳、蜀之彥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin, upon pacifying the realm, honored the eminent men of Wu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin, upon pacifying the realm, honored the eminent men of Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜於河表七州人中，擢其門才，引令赴闕，依中州官比，隨能序之。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that among the people of the seven provinces south of the Yellow River, their local talent should be selected and summoned to court, ranked according to Central Region office equivalents, ordered by ability.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that among the people of the seven provinces south of the Yellow River, local talent should be selected and summoned to court, ranked according to Central Region office equivalents and ordered by ability.

sentences.zh: 一可以廣聖朝均新舊之義，二可以懷江、漢歸有道之情。

translations.literal: First, this can broaden the sacred court's principle of treating old and new equally; second, it can win the hearts of the Yangzi and Han toward the Way.
translations.idiomatic: First, this would broaden the sacred court's principle of treating old and new equally; second, it would win the hearts of the Yangzi and Han regions toward the Way.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：

translations.literal: The fourth item says:
translations.idiomatic: The fourth section reads:

sentences.zh: 漢制，舊斷獄報重盡季冬，至孝章時改盡十月，以育三微。

translations.literal: Under Han institutions, capital cases were traditionally concluded by the end of winter; in the reign of Emperor Xiaozhang this was changed to conclude by the tenth month, to nurture the Three Beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han institutions, capital cases were traditionally concluded by the end of winter; in the reign of Emperor Xiaozhang this was changed to conclude by the tenth month, to nurture the Three Beginnings.

sentences.zh: 後歲旱，論者以不十月斷獄，陰氣微，陽氣泄，以故致旱，事下公卿。

translations.literal: Later a drought year came; commentators held that not concluding cases in the tenth month caused yin to be slight and yang to leak—thus causing drought; the matter was referred to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Later a drought year came; commentators held that failing to conclude cases in the tenth month caused yin to be slight and yang to leak, thus bringing drought; the matter was referred to the ministers.

sentences.zh: 尚書陳寵曰：「冬至陽氣始萌，故十一月有射幹芸荔之應，周以為春。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Chong said: "At the winter solstice yang begins to sprout—thus in the eleventh month there is the response of arrow-root and artemisia; Zhou regarded this as spring.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Chong said, "At the winter solstice yang begins to sprout—thus in the eleventh month there is the response of arrow-root and artemisia; Zhou regarded this as spring.

sentences.zh: 十二月陽氣上通，雉雊雞乳，殷以為春。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month yang rises upward; pheasants call and hens brood; Yin regarded this as spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month yang rises upward; pheasants call and hens brood; Yin regarded this as spring.

sentences.zh: 十三月陽氣已至，蟄蟲皆震，夏以為春。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth month yang has fully arrived; hibernating insects all stir; Xia regarded this as spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth month yang has fully arrived; hibernating insects all stir; Xia regarded this as spring.

sentences.zh: 三微成著，以通三統。

translations.literal: When the Three Beginnings are established and manifest, the Three Successions are joined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Beginnings are established and manifest, the Three Successions are joined.

sentences.zh: 三統之月斷獄流血，是不稽天意也。

translations.literal: To execute capital punishments and shed blood in the months of the Three Successions is to fail to examine Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: To execute capital punishments and shed blood in the months of the Three Successions is to fail to examine Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 」章帝善其言，卒以十月斷。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhang approved his words and finally concluded cases in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang approved his words and finally concluded cases in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 今京都及四方斷獄報重，常竟季冬，不推三正以育三微。

translations.literal: Now in the capital and throughout the land, capital cases are regularly concluded only at year's end, without deferring to the Three Correct Starts to nurture the Three Beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the capital and throughout the land, capital cases are regularly concluded only at year's end, without deferring to the Three Correct Starts to nurture the Three Beginnings.

sentences.zh: 寬宥之情，每過於昔，遵之典憲，猶或闕然。

translations.literal: The spirit of clemency often exceeds that of old, yet observance of canonical statutes still falls short.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of clemency often exceeds that of old, yet observance of canonical statutes still falls short.

sentences.zh: 今豈所謂助陽發生，垂奉微之仁也？

translations.literal: Now can this be what is called aiding yang's birth and extending the benevolence of nurturing the Three Beginnings?
translations.idiomatic: Now can this be what is called aiding yang's birth and extending the benevolence of nurturing the Three Beginnings?

sentences.zh: 誠宜遠稽周典，近采漢制，天下斷獄起自初秋，盡于孟冬。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to examine the Zhou canon from afar and adopt Han institutions from near at hand; throughout the realm capital cases should begin from early autumn and conclude by mid-winter.
translations.idiomatic: It is truly fitting to examine the Zhou canon from afar and adopt Han institutions from near at hand: throughout the realm capital cases should begin from early autumn and conclude by mid-winter.

sentences.zh: 不於三統之春，行斬絞之刑。

translations.literal: During the spring of the Three Successions, execution and strangulation punishments should not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the spring of the Three Successions, execution and strangulation punishments should not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 如此則道協幽顯，仁垂後昆矣。

translations.literal: Thus the Way would harmonize the hidden and manifest, and benevolence extend to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the Way would harmonize the seen and unseen realms, and benevolence would reach down through generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 其五曰：

translations.literal: The fifth says:
translations.idiomatic: The fifth recommendation:

sentences.zh: 古者大臣有坐不廉而廢者，不謂之不廉，乃曰簠簋不飾。

translations.literal: In antiquity when great ministers were dismissed for the crime of dishonesty, they did not call it dishonesty but said, "The ritual vessels are not properly adorned."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a great minister was removed for corruption, no one called it corruption outright—they would say only that his sacrificial vessels were not properly maintained.

sentences.zh: 此君之所以禮貴臣，不明言其過也。

translations.literal: This is how the ruler, in honoring eminent ministers, did not speak plainly of their faults.
translations.idiomatic: This was how a ruler showed honor to his high ministers while avoiding blunt disclosure of their faults.

sentences.zh: 臣有大譴，則白冠氂纓盤水加劍，造室而請死，此臣之所以知罪而不敢逃刑也。

translations.literal: When a minister bore grave culpability, he would put on a white cap with yak-tail tassel, place a basin of water with a sword upon it, go to his chamber and request death—this is how the minister knew his guilt and dared not flee punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister incurred grave blame, he would don the white cap with yak-tail tassel, set out a basin of water with a sword laid upon it, and go to his chamber to beg for death—thus acknowledging guilt and accepting punishment rather than fleeing it.

sentences.zh: 聖朝賓遇大臣，禮崇古典，自太和降，有負罪當陷大辟者，多得歸第自盡。

translations.literal: The sagely court treats ministers as honored guests and venerates the ancient rites; from the Taihe era downward, those bearing guilt deserving death have mostly been permitted to return home and end their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage court receives ministers as honored guests and holds to the ancient rites; since the Taihe era, ministers who have incurred guilt warranting capital punishment have for the most part been allowed to return home and take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 遣之日，深垂隱湣，言發淒淚，百官莫不見，四海莫不聞，誠足以感將死之心，慰戚屬之情。

translations.literal: On the day of their dismissal, the court deeply showed concealed compassion; words issued in bitter tears—all the hundred officials saw it, all within the four seas heard it—truly sufficient to move the hearts of those about to die and comfort the grief of their kin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day they were sent away, the throne showed deep, restrained compassion, its words breaking in tears of sorrow—every official witnessed it, and the whole realm heard of it—enough truly to touch the hearts of men facing death and console the grief of their families.

sentences.zh: 然恩發於衷，未著永制，此愚臣所以敢陳末見。

translations.literal: Yet the grace issued from the heart and was not established as a permanent institution—this is why this foolish minister dares to present these humble views.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this grace has issued from the heart alone and has not been enshrined as permanent law—hence this unworthy minister ventures to offer his humble views.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文時，人有告丞相勃謀反者，逮系長安獄，頓辱之與皁隸同。

translations.literal: Formerly in the time of Emperor Wen of Han, someone reported that Chancellor Bo was plotting rebellion; he was arrested and imprisoned in Chang'an, harshly humiliated together with common jailers' servants.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, someone accused Chancellor Bo of plotting rebellion. Bo was arrested and imprisoned in Chang'an, humiliated and degraded alongside the lowest jail servants.

sentences.zh: 賈誼乃上書，極陳君臣之義，不宜如是。

translations.literal: Jia Yi thereupon submitted a memorial, fully setting forth the principles between ruler and minister—it should not be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi submitted a memorial arguing at length that the bonds between ruler and minister should never be handled in such a fashion.

sentences.zh: 夫貴臣者，天子為其改容而體貌之，吏人為共俯伏而敬貴之。

translations.literal: As for eminent ministers—the Son of Heaven changed his countenance and showed them personal regard; officials and clerks together prostrated themselves in respect and honored them as noble.
translations.idiomatic: An eminent minister was one for whom the Son of Heaven would soften his bearing and show personal regard, and whose subordinates would bow low in reverence.

sentences.zh: 其有罪過，廢之可也，賜之死可也；

translations.literal: If they had guilt, one might dismiss them, or grant them death;
translations.idiomatic: If guilty, he might be dismissed—or granted the grace of death;

sentences.zh: 若束縛之，輸之司寇，搒笞之，小吏詈罵之，殆非所以令眾庶見也。

translations.literal: But to bind them, hand them to the judicial officer, beat and flog them, have petty clerks revile and abuse them—this is scarcely what should be shown to the common masses.
translations.idiomatic: But to bind him, turn him over to the judicial officer, beat and flog him, and let petty clerks revile and abuse him—this is scarcely the sort of spectacle the people should witness.

sentences.zh: 及將刑也，臣則北面再拜，跪而自裁。

translations.literal: When the time came for execution, the minister would face north, bow twice, kneel and take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When execution was at hand, the minister would face north, bow twice, kneel, and take his own life.

sentences.zh: 天子曰：「子大夫自有過耳，吾遇子有禮矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "You, sir and grandee, have your own faults—I have treated you with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven said, "You, sir, have your own faults—but I have treated you with due ceremony.

sentences.zh: 上不使人抑而刑之也。

translations.literal: The ruler does not have men restrain and punish you."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler does not have men bind and punish you."

sentences.zh: 」孝文深納其言。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deeply accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen accepted his counsel wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 是後大臣有罪，皆自殺不受刑。

translations.literal: After this, ministers who committed crimes all killed themselves rather than submit to judicial punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After this, ministers who committed crimes all took their own lives rather than submit to judicial punishment.

sentences.zh: 至孝武時，稍復下獄。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wu, they were again gradually imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Wu, ministers were once again gradually thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 良由孝文行之當時，不為永制故耳。

translations.literal: This was truly because Emperor Xiaowen practiced it only for his own time and did not make it a permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: This was precisely because Emperor Wen had practiced it only in his own day and had not made it a permanent institution.

sentences.zh: 今天下有道，庶人不議之時，安可陳瞽言於朝？

translations.literal: Today when the realm has the Way and the common people offer no criticism, how can one dare present blind counsel at court?
translations.idiomatic: Today, when the realm is well governed and the common people offer no criticism, how can one dare offer blind counsel at court?

sentences.zh: 且恐萬世之後，繼體之主有若漢武之事。

translations.literal: Moreover I fear that ten thousand generations hence, succeeding sovereigns may act as Emperor Wu did.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I fear that ten thousand generations hence, succeeding sovereigns may act as Emperor Wu did.

sentences.zh: 焉得行恩當時，不著長世之制乎。

translations.literal: How can one exercise grace only for the present moment and not establish institutions lasting through the ages?
translations.idiomatic: How can grace be exercised only for the present moment, without establishing institutions to endure through the ages?

sentences.zh: 其六曰：

translations.literal: The sixth says:
translations.idiomatic: The sixth recommendation:

sentences.zh: 《孝經》稱父子之道天性，蓋明一體而同氣，可共而不右離者也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says the way between father and son is by nature—making clear they are one body sharing one breath, that may dwell together and cannot be parted.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says that the bond between father and son is innate—making clear that they are one body sharing one breath, that may dwell together and cannot be torn apart.

sentences.zh: 及其有罪不相及者，乃君上之厚恩也。

translations.literal: That when a crime does not implicate others is the sovereign's great grace.
translations.idiomatic: That guilt does not extend to one's kin is the sovereign's great grace.

sentences.zh: 而無情之人，父兄系獄，子弟無慘惕之容；

translations.literal: Yet the heartless—when father or elder brother is imprisoned, sons and younger brothers show no countenance of grief and apprehension;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heartless—when a father or elder brother is imprisoned, sons and younger brothers show no trace of grief or apprehension;

sentences.zh: 子弟即刑，父兄無愧恧之色。

translations.literal: When sons and younger brothers face execution, fathers and elder brothers show no color of shame.
translations.idiomatic: when sons and younger brothers face execution, fathers and elder brothers show no sign of shame.

sentences.zh: 宴安榮位，游從自若，軍馬仍華，衣冠猶飾。

translations.literal: They feast in ease, hold honored posts, associate and move about as before, their mounts still splendid, their dress still adorned.
translations.idiomatic: They feast in ease, hold honored posts, and go about their companions as before—their mounts still splendid, their dress still adorned.

sentences.zh: 寧是同體共氣，分憂均戚之理也？

translations.literal: Can this be the principle of sharing one body and one breath, dividing worry and sharing grief?
translations.idiomatic: Can this be the principle of sharing one body and one breath, dividing worry and sharing grief alike?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為父兄有犯，宜令子弟素服肉袒，詣闕請罪；

translations.literal: This foolish minister holds that when fathers or elder brothers offend, sons and younger brothers should wear plain white and bare the upper body, go to the palace gate and request punishment;
translations.idiomatic: This unworthy minister holds that when a father or elder brother offends, sons and younger brothers should wear plain white and bare the upper body, go to the palace gate, and beg for punishment;

sentences.zh: 子弟有坐，宜令父兄露板引咎，乞解所司。

translations.literal: When sons and younger brothers are implicated, fathers and elder brothers should post a placard confessing guilt and beg to be relieved of their posts.
translations.idiomatic: when sons and younger brothers are implicated, fathers and elder brothers should post a public confession of guilt and beg to be relieved of their offices.

sentences.zh: 若職任必要，不宜許者，慰勉留之。

translations.literal: If the office is indispensable and dismissal is not appropriate, they should be comforted and encouraged to remain.
translations.idiomatic: If the office is indispensable and dismissal is not appropriate, they should be comforted and encouraged to remain at their posts.

sentences.zh: 如此，足以敦厲凡薄，使人知有所恥矣。

translations.literal: In this way it would be sufficient to strengthen the vulgar and insipid and make people know shame.
translations.idiomatic: In this way it would be enough to strengthen the shallow and insipid and teach people to know shame.

sentences.zh: 其七曰：

translations.literal: The seventh says:
translations.idiomatic: The seventh recommendation:

sentences.zh: 《禮》云：臣有大喪，君三年不呼其門。

translations.literal: The Rites say: when a minister has a major bereavement, the ruler for three years does not summon at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: when a minister suffers a major bereavement, the ruler for three years does not summon him at his gate.

sentences.zh: 此聖人緣情制禮，以終孝子之情也。

translations.literal: This is the sage regulating rites according to feeling, to complete the filial son's sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sage regulating rites according to human feeling, to fulfill the filial son's devotion.

sentences.zh: 周季陵夷，喪禮稍亡，是以要糸至即戎，素冠作刺。

translations.literal: When Zhou's late age declined, mourning rites gradually perished; hence when the hemmed mourning sash arrived one took up arms, and "The Plain Cap" became a satire.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's late age declined, mourning rites gradually died out; hence when the hemmed mourning sash arrived one went straight to war, and "The Plain Cap" became a satirical lament.

sentences.zh: 逮乎虐秦，殆皆泯矣。

translations.literal: By the time of tyrannical Qin, they were nearly all extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of tyrannical Qin, they were nearly all extinguished.

sentences.zh: 漢初，軍旅屢興，未能遵古。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, armies were repeatedly raised and the ancients could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, armies were repeatedly raised and the ancient rites could not be followed.

sentences.zh: 至宣帝時，人當從軍屯者，遭大父母、父母死，未滿三月，皆弗徭役。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xuan, those who should have gone to frontier garrison duty—when grandparents or parents died, within three months none were levied for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Xuan, those due for frontier garrison duty who lost a grandparent or parent were exempt from corvée labor for three months.

sentences.zh: 其朝臣喪制，未有定聞。

translations.literal: As for mourning regulations for court ministers, nothing fixed was heard of.
translations.idiomatic: As for mourning regulations for court ministers, no fixed rule was yet established.

sentences.zh: 至後漢元初中，大臣有重憂，始得去官終服。

translations.literal: By the early Yuanchu era of Later Han, ministers with heavy bereavement could first leave office and complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: By the early Yuanchu era of Later Han, ministers who suffered a major bereavement were at last permitted to leave office and complete their mourning.

sentences.zh: 暨魏武、孫、劉之世，日尋干戈，前世禮制，復廢不行。

translations.literal: Through the eras of Cao Wei, Sun Wu, and Liu Han, as warfare pursued day by day, the ritual systems of former ages were again abandoned and not practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Through the eras of Cao Wei, Sun Wu, and Liu Han, as warfare raged day after day, the ritual systems of former ages were again abandoned and left unpracticed.

sentences.zh: 晉時鴻臚鄭默喪親，固請終服，武帝感其孝誠，遂著令以為常。

translations.literal: In Jin times Honglu Secretary Zheng Mo, bereaved of a parent, firmly requested to complete mourning; Emperor Wu was moved by his filial sincerity and thereupon issued an ordinance making it the regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times, when Honglu Secretary Zheng Mo lost a parent and firmly requested to complete his mourning, Emperor Wu was moved by his filial sincerity and issued an ordinance making it the regular rule.

sentences.zh: 聖魏之初，撥亂反正，未遑建終喪之制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the sacred Wei, in setting chaos aright, there was no leisure to establish regulations for complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of sacred Wei, in setting chaos aright, there was no leisure to establish regulations for complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 今四方無虞，百姓安逸，誠是孝慈道洽，禮教興行之日也。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are untroubled and the common people are at ease—truly this is the day when filial piety and compassion permeate and ritual instruction flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four quarters are untroubled and the common people live in ease—truly this is the day when filial piety and compassion permeate the realm and ritual instruction flourishes.

sentences.zh: 然愚臣所懷，竊有未盡。

translations.literal: Yet what this foolish minister harbors in his heart still has something incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what this unworthy minister harbors in his heart still falls short of completion.

sentences.zh: 伏見朝臣丁大憂者，假滿赴職，衣錦乘軒，從效廟之祀；

translations.literal: I humbly observe that court ministers who have completed the mourning leave period return to office, dressed in brocade and riding in curtained carriages, attending ancestral temple sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that court ministers who have completed their mourning leave return to office dressed in brocade and riding in curtained carriages, attending ancestral temple sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 鳴玉垂緌，同節慶之宴。

translations.literal: With jade pendants sounding and trailing tassels, joining festive banquets.
translations.idiomatic: jade pendants sounding at their belts, trailing tassels, joining festive banquets.

sentences.zh: 傷人子之道，虧天地之經。

translations.literal: This wounds the way of a son and falls short of Heaven and Earth's constant principle.
translations.idiomatic: This wounds the way of a son and falls short of Heaven and Earth's constant principle.

sentences.zh: 愚謂如有遭父母喪者，皆得終服。

translations.literal: This fool holds that those who encounter the death of parents should all be allowed to complete full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that those who lose a parent should all be permitted to complete full mourning.

sentences.zh: 若無其人有曠官者，則優旨慰喻，起令視事。

translations.literal: If no one is available and the office would go vacant, then with gracious edicts comfort and instruct, and raise them to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: If no substitute is available and the office would go vacant, then with gracious edicts comfort and instruct them, and summon them back to resume their duties.

sentences.zh: 但綜理所司，出納敷奏而已，國之吉慶，一令無預。

translations.literal: Only managing the affairs of their office, receiving documents and presenting reports—that is all; they should have no part whatever in the state's joyous celebrations.
translations.idiomatic: They should manage only the routine affairs of their office—receiving documents and presenting reports—and have no part whatever in the state's joyous celebrations.

sentences.zh: 其軍戎之警，墨縗從役，雖愆於禮，事所宜行也。

translations.literal: When there is military alarm, serving in black-clad mourning—though a lapse from ritual—is something circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: When military alarm arises, serving in black-clad mourning—though a lapse from ritual—is something circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之，尋皆施行。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and approved; soon all was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and approved it; soon all of it was put into practice.

sentences.zh: 彪稍見禮遇。

translations.literal: Biao gradually received courteous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Biao gradually came to receive courteous treatment at court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「彪雖宿非清第，代闕華資，然識性嚴聰，學博墳籍，剛辯之才，頗堪時用。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Although Biao by origin was not of a distinguished lineage and in his generation lacked illustrious credentials, yet his nature is severe and intelligent, his learning broad in the classics, and his talent for bold debate quite suited to the needs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Although Biao by origin was not of distinguished lineage and in his generation lacked illustrious credentials, yet his nature is keen and intelligent, his learning broad in the classics, and his talent for bold debate quite suited to the needs of the age.

sentences.zh: 兼優吏職，載宣朝美，若不賞庸敘績，將何以勸獎勤能。

translations.literal: He excels moreover in administrative office and has spread the court's excellence abroad—if we do not reward merit and record achievement, with what shall we encourage diligence and ability?
translations.idiomatic: He excels moreover in administrative office and has spread the court's excellence abroad—if we do not reward merit and record achievement, with what shall we encourage diligence and ability?

sentences.zh: 特遷秘書令。

translations.literal: He is specially promoted to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He is specially promoted to Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 以參議律令之勤，賜帛五百匹，馬一匹、牛二頭。

translations.literal: For his diligence in deliberating on statutes and ordinances, five hundred bolts of silk are granted, one horse, and two head of cattle.
translations.idiomatic: For his diligence in deliberating on statutes and ordinances, he is granted five hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and two head of cattle.

sentences.zh: 」其年，加員外散騎常侍，使于齊。

translations.literal: That same year he was additionally appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent as envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was additionally appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent as envoy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊遣其主客郎劉繪接對，並設宴樂。

translations.literal: Qi sent its Master of Guests Attendant Liu Hui to receive him and also set out a banquet with music.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent its Master of Guests Attendant Liu Hui to receive him and also laid out a banquet with music.

sentences.zh: 彪辭樂。

translations.literal: Biao declined the music.
translations.idiomatic: Biao declined the music.

sentences.zh: 及坐，彪曰：「向辭樂者，卿或未相體。

translations.literal: When seated, Biao said, "As for my declining the music just now—you perhaps did not fully understand my meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When they were seated, Biao said, "As for my declining the music just now—you perhaps did not fully grasp my meaning.

sentences.zh: 我皇孝性自天，追慕罔極，故有今者喪除之議。

translations.literal: Our Emperor's filial nature is heaven-sent, his longing boundless; hence there is now the discussion of ending mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor's filial nature is heaven-sent and his longing boundless; hence the present discussion of ending mourning.

sentences.zh: 去三月晦，朝臣始除縗裳，猶以素服從事。

translations.literal: Last month at month's end the court ministers first removed their hemp mourning garments, yet still wear plain dress while attending to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the third month the court ministers first removed their hemp mourning garments, yet still wear plain dress while attending to affairs.

sentences.zh: 裴、謝在北，固應具此。

translations.literal: Pei and Xie in the north should naturally have the same.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and Xie in the north should naturally observe the same.

sentences.zh: 今辭樂，想卿無怪。

translations.literal: In declining music now, I trust you will not be surprised.
translations.idiomatic: In declining music now, I trust you will not take offense.

sentences.zh: 」繪答言：「請問魏朝喪禮竟何所依？

translations.literal: Hui replied, "May I ask what the Wei court's mourning rites are ultimately based on?
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "May I ask what the Wei court's mourning rites are ultimately based on?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「高宗三年，孝文逾月。

translations.literal: Biao said, "Gaozong mourned three years; Emperor Xiaowen exceeded one month.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "Gaozong mourned three years; Emperor Wen of Han exceeded one month.

sentences.zh: 今聖上追鞠育之深恩，感慈訓之厚德，報于殷、漢之間，可謂得禮之變。

translations.literal: Now His Majesty responds to the deep grace of nurture and cherishes the great virtue of maternal instruction, requiting between Yin and Han—it may be called obtaining the ritual variation.
translations.idiomatic: Now His Majesty responds to the deep grace of nurture and cherishes the great virtue of maternal instruction, requiting it between the standards of Yin and Han—it may be called a proper variation of ritual.

sentences.zh: 」繪復問：「若欲遵古，何不終三年？

translations.literal: Hui asked again, "If you wish to follow antiquity, why not complete three years?
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked again, "If you wish to follow antiquity, why not complete three years?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「萬機不可久曠，故割至慕，俯從群議。

translations.literal: Biao said, "The myriad affairs of state cannot long go unattended; hence cutting short utmost longing, he humbly follows the counsel of the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "The myriad affairs of state cannot long go unattended; hence, setting aside his deepest grief, he humbly follows the counsel of the assembly.

sentences.zh: 服變不異三年，而限同一期，可謂失禮？

translations.literal: The outward change of dress is no different from three years, yet the term equals one cycle—can this be called a breach of ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: The outward change of dress is no different from three years, yet the term equals one full cycle—can this be called a breach of ritual?"

sentences.zh: 」繪言：「汰哉叔氏，專以禮許人。

translations.literal: Hui said, "How lax, Uncle! You use ritual solely to excuse people."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "How lax, Uncle! You use ritual solely to make excuses for people."

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「聖朝自為曠代之制，何關許人。

translations.literal: Biao said, "The sage court establishes its own institutions for an age apart—what has that to do with excusing anyone?"
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "The sage court establishes its own institutions for an age apart—what has that to do with making excuses for anyone?"

sentences.zh: 」繪言：「百官總己聽於塚宰，萬機何慮於曠？

translations.literal: Hui said, "When the hundred officials concentrate affairs upon themselves and obey the Chief Minister, why worry that the myriad affairs would lie idle?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "When the hundred officials concentrate affairs upon themselves and obey the Chief Minister, why worry that the myriad affairs of state would lie idle?"

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「五帝之臣，臣不若君，故君親攬其事。

translations.literal: Biao said, "Under the Five Emperors, ministers were not the equal of their lords, hence the lord personally handled affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "Under the Five Emperors, ministers were not the equal of their lords, hence the lord personally handled affairs.

sentences.zh: 三王君臣智等，故共理機務。

translations.literal: Under the Three Kings ruler and minister were equal in wisdom, hence they jointly managed affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Three Kings, ruler and minister were equal in wisdom, hence they jointly managed affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 主上親攬，蓋遠軌軒、唐。

translations.literal: Our sovereign personally handles affairs—surely treading the distant tracks of Xuanyuan and Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign personally handles affairs—surely treading the distant tracks of Xuanyuan and Tang."

sentences.zh: 」彪將還，齊主親謂彪曰：「卿前使還日，賦阮詩云：'但願長閒暇，後歲復來遊。

translations.literal: When Biao was about to return, the Qi sovereign personally said to him, "When you came as envoy before, you composed a Ruan poem saying, 'I only wish for long leisure—next year I'll come again to wander.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was about to return, the Qi sovereign personally said to him, "When you came as envoy before, you composed a Ruan poem saying, 'I only wish for long leisure—to come again and wander next year.

sentences.zh: '果如今日。

translations.literal: It has truly come to pass as today.
translations.idiomatic: It has truly come to pass as today.

sentences.zh: 卿此還也，復有來理否？

translations.literal: On this return of yours, is there again reason to come?
translations.idiomatic: On this return of yours, is there again reason to come?

sentences.zh: 」彪答：「請重賦阮詩曰：'宴衍清都中，一去永矣哉。

translations.literal: Biao replied, "Allow me to compose another Ruan poem: 'Feasting and roaming in the pure capital—once gone, forever gone.
translations.idiomatic: Biao replied, "Allow me to compose another Ruan poem: 'Feasting and roaming in the pure capital—once gone, forever gone.

sentences.zh: '」齊主惘然曰：「清都可爾，一去何事！

translations.literal: The Qi sovereign, dismayed, said, "The pure capital—that can be managed; but 'once gone'—what does that mean!
translations.idiomatic: The Qi sovereign, dismayed, said, "The pure capital—that can be managed; but 'once gone'—what does that mean!

sentences.zh: 觀卿此言，似成長闊。

translations.literal: Judging from your words, it seems a long separation is formed.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from your words, it seems a long separation is in store.

sentences.zh: 朕當以殊禮相送。

translations.literal: I shall send you off with extraordinary ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: I shall send you off with extraordinary ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」遂親至琅邪城，登山臨水，命群臣賦詩以送別。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally went to Langya city, climbed the mountain and looked over the water, and ordered the ministers to compose poems to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he personally went to Langya city, climbed the mountain and looked over the water, and ordered his ministers to compose poems to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: He was held in such esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was held in such esteem.

sentences.zh: 彪前後六度銜命，南人奇其謇博。

translations.literal: Biao on six occasions in succession bore imperial commission; southerners marveled at his forthrightness and erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Biao on six occasions in succession bore imperial commission; southerners marveled at his forthrightness and erudition.

sentences.zh: 後為御史中尉，領著作郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Censor-in-Chief and concurrently held the post of Director of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Censor-in-Chief and concurrently served as Director of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 彪既為孝文所寵，性又剛直，遂多劾糾，遠近畏之。

translations.literal: Biao, being favored by Emperor Xiaowen and by nature also upright and unyielding, thereupon impeached and investigated many; near and far feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, being favored by Emperor Wen and by nature upright and unyielding, thereupon impeached and investigated many; near and far feared him.

sentences.zh: 豪右屏氣。

translations.literal: Powerful local gentry held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful local gentry held their breath.

sentences.zh: 帝常呼為李生，從容謂群臣曰：「吾之有李生，猶漢之有汲黯。

translations.literal: The Emperor often called him Master Li, and at ease said to the ministers, "My having Master Li is like Han's having Ji An."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often called him Master Li, and at ease said to the ministers, "My having Master Li is like Han's having Ji An."

sentences.zh: 」後除散騎常侍，領御史中尉，解著作事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining the censorate, and relieved of the compilation post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining the censorate, and relieved of the compilation post.

sentences.zh: 帝宴群臣于流化池，謂僕射李沖曰：「崔光之博，李彪之直，是我國得賢之基。」

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted the ministers at the Flowing Transformation Pool and said to Director Li Chong, "Cui Guang's erudition and Li Biao's integrity are the foundation on which our state gains worthy men."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor feasted the ministers at the Flowing Transformation Pool and said to Director Li Chong, "Cui Guang's erudition and Li Biao's integrity are the foundation on which our state gains worthy men."

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，彪兼度支尚書，與僕射李沖、任城王澄等參理留台事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Biao concurrently served as Minister of Revenue and with Director Li Chong, Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, and others jointly managed affairs of the rear capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Biao concurrently served as Minister of Revenue and, with Director Li Chong, Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, and others, jointly managed affairs of the rear capital.

sentences.zh: 彪素性剛豪，與沖等意議乖異，遂形於聲色，殊無降下之心。

translations.literal: Biao's nature was by temperament bold and proud; his views differed from Chong and the others, and this showed in voice and countenance—entirely lacking any spirit of deference.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's nature was bold and proud; his views differed from Chong and the others, and this showed plainly in voice and countenance—entirely lacking any spirit of deference.

sentences.zh: 沖積其前後罪過，乃於尚書省禁止彪，上表曰：「案臣彪昔於凡品，特以才拔，等望清華，司文東觀，綢繆恩眷，繩直憲台，左加金璫，右珥蟬冕。

translations.literal: Chong accumulated his faults past and present, and thereupon at the Ministry of State Affairs detained Biao, submitting a memorial saying, "In review, your subject Biao formerly arose from common rank, specially raised for talent, matching in eminence the clear and splendid, overseeing texts at the Eastern Pavilion, bound close by imperial favor, straightening the rope at the censorate, on the left adding the golden earring, on the right wearing the cicada cap.
translations.idiomatic: Chong accumulated his faults past and present, and thereupon detained Biao at the Ministry of State Affairs, submitting a memorial saying, "In review, your subject Biao formerly arose from common rank, specially raised for talent, matching in eminence the clear and splendid, overseeing texts at the Eastern Pavilion, bound close by imperial favor, straightening the rope at the censorate, on the left adding the golden earring, on the right wearing the cicada cap.

sentences.zh: 東省。

translations.literal: Of the Eastern Department.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Eastern Department.

sentences.zh: 宜感恩厲節，忠以報德。

translations.literal: He ought to feel gratitude and strengthen his integrity, repaying virtue with loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He ought to have felt gratitude, strengthened his integrity, and repaid the state's favor with loyal service.

sentences.zh: 而竊名忝職，身為違傲，矜勢高亢，公行僭逸。
