translations.literal: Yet he steals renown and disgraces his post, his person acts in violation and pride, flaunts power and holds himself high, and openly practices usurpation and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he stole renown and disgraced his office, behaved with defiant arrogance, flaunted his power, and openly indulged in presumptuous excess.

sentences.zh: 坐與禁省，冒取官材，輒駕乘黃，無所憚懼。

translations.literal: He sits with the forbidden offices, presumptuously takes official timber, at will drives yellow carriage horses, without any fear or dread.
translations.idiomatic: He sat as an equal among the restricted ministries, seized official timber without authorization, drove imperial yellow horses at will, and feared nothing.

sentences.zh: 肆志傲然，愚聾視聽。

translations.literal: He indulges his will proudly, deaf and blind to sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged his whims with arrogant defiance and turned a deaf ear to all around him.

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，誰不可懷。

translations.literal: If this can be borne, who could not harbor resentment?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be tolerated, what outrage could not be borne?

sentences.zh: 臣今請以見事免彪所居職，付廷尉獄。

translations.literal: Your subject now requests that, on the basis of present matters, Biao be removed from the post he holds and handed over to the Court Commandant's prison.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject now requests that, on the basis of these facts, Biao be removed from office and handed over to the Court Commandant for trial.

sentences.zh: 」沖又表曰：

translations.literal: " Chong further submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Chong submitted a further memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣與彪相識以來，垂二十二載。

translations.literal: Since I became acquainted with Biao, nearly twenty-two years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: I have known Biao for nearly twenty-two years.

sentences.zh: 彪始南使之時，見其色厲辭辯，臣之愚識，謂是拔萃之一人。

translations.literal: When Biao first went south as envoy, I saw his stern countenance and eloquent speech; my dull understanding considered him one who stood out from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao first went south as envoy, I saw his stern bearing and sharp eloquence and, in my limited judgment, took him for a man who stood out from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 及彪官位升達，參與言宴，聞彪平章古今，商略人物。

translations.literal: When Biao's office rose to high rank and he took part in discussions and feasts, I heard Biao judge ancient and modern affairs and appraise people.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao rose to high office and took part in discussions and banquets, I heard him weigh ancient and modern affairs and appraise men of talent.

sentences.zh: 興言於侍筵之次，啟論于眾英之中；

translations.literal: He rose to speak beside the banquet table and opened discussion among the assembled worthies;
translations.idiomatic: He would rise to speak at the side of the imperial banquet and open debate among the assembled worthies;

sentences.zh: 賞忠識正，發言懇惻，惟直是語，辭無隱避。

translations.literal: praising loyalty and recognizing rectitude, speaking earnestly and sincerely, speaking only what is straight, his words without concealment or avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: praising loyalty, recognizing what was right, speaking with earnest sincerity, saying only what was straight, and never hiding or evading his meaning.

sentences.zh: 臣雖下愚，輒亦欽其正直。

translations.literal: Though I am low and dull, I too admired his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am a man of little wit, I too admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 及其始居司直，執志徑行，其所彈劾，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: When he first held the censorate directorship, he pursued his purpose straight and fast; those he impeached fell like targets at the release of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took up the censorate, he pursued his purpose without deviation; those he impeached fell as if struck the moment the bowstring was released.

sentences.zh: 赫赫之威，振于下國；

translations.literal: His brilliant authority shook the subordinate states;
translations.idiomatic: His formidable authority resounded through the provinces;

sentences.zh: 肅肅之稱，著自京師；

translations.literal: His solemn reputation was noted from the capital;
translations.idiomatic: his stern reputation was known throughout the capital;

sentences.zh: 天下改目，貪暴僉槠手。

translations.literal: All under Heaven changed their gaze; the greedy and violent together restrained their hands.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven took notice, and the greedy and violent alike held back their hands.

sentences.zh: 然時有私於臣雲其威暴者，臣以直繩之官，人所忌疾，風謗之際，易生音謠，心不承信。

translations.literal: Yet at times some privately told me he was violent in his authority; your subject, considering that the office of straightening the rope is what people hate and despise, and that at times of slanderous winds rumors easily arise, did not accept this in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some privately told me he was tyrannical in his authority. I considered that the censor's office is one people hate and that slander easily breeds rumor in such times, and so I did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 往年以河陽事，曾與彪在領軍府共太尉、司空及領軍諸卿等集閱廷尉所問囚徒。

translations.literal: In former years, on account of the Heyang affair, I was together with Biao at the General of the Garrison headquarters, together with the Grand Commandant, Minister of Works, and various ministers of the Garrison, assembling to review prisoners questioned by the Court Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In a former year, over the Heyang affair, I was with Biao at the Garrison General's headquarters, together with the Grand Commandant, Minister of Works, and other ministers of the Garrison, reviewing prisoners interrogated by the Court Commandant.

sentences.zh: 時有人訴枉者，二公及臣少欲聽采。

translations.literal: At the time someone appealed that he had been wronged; the two Excellencies and I slightly wished to hear and adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone appealed that he had been wronged, and the two Excellencies and I were inclined to hear him out.

sentences.zh: 語理未盡，彪便振怒，東坐攘袂揮赫，口稱賊奴，叱吒左右。

translations.literal: Before the words and reasoning were finished, Biao suddenly flared with anger, sat facing east flinging his sleeves and gesturing fiercely, his mouth calling them "traitor slaves," berating those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Before the argument was finished, Biao suddenly flared with rage, sat facing east with sleeves flung back, gestured violently, called them "traitor slaves," and berated his attendants.

sentences.zh: 高聲大呼曰：「南台中取我木手去，搭奴肋折！

translations.literal: He shouted loudly saying: "Go to the Southern Court and get my wooden cudgel—I will break the slave's ribs!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted loudly: "Send someone to the Southern Court to fetch my wooden cudgel—I'll break the wretch's ribs!"

sentences.zh: 」雖有此言，終竟不取。

translations.literal: " Although he said this, in the end he did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: " Although he said this, in the end he did not have the cudgel brought.

sentences.zh: 即言：「南台所問，唯恐枉活，終無枉死。

translations.literal: He then said: "What the Southern Court questions—I only fear letting the guilty live; never fearing wrong death."
translations.idiomatic: He then said: "When the Southern Court interrogates a case, I only fear letting the guilty go free—I never fear putting an innocent man to death."

sentences.zh: 」時諸人以所枉至重，有首實者多，又心難彪，遂各默爾。

translations.literal: " At the time the assembly, because the wrong suffered was very grave and many had confessed to the facts, and also because they were troubled at heart by Biao, thereupon each fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time the others, seeing how grave the injustice was and how many had already confessed, and being intimidated by Biao, each fell silent.

sentences.zh: 因緣此事，臣遂心疑有濫，知其威虐。

translations.literal: Because of this matter, your subject thereupon suspected in my heart there was abuse, and knew his ferocity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this incident, I began to suspect that abuses were occurring and came to know his tyrannical cruelty.

sentences.zh: 猶謂益多損少，故不以申徹，實失為臣知無不聞之義。

translations.literal: Still I judged that the gains outweighed the losses, and so did not report it fully—truly failing the duty of a minister who hears of nothing without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: Still I judged that his service did more good than harm, and so did not report it fully—a failure of the minister's duty to leave nothing unheard unreported.

sentences.zh: 及去年大駕南行以來，彪兼尚書，日夕共事，始乃知其言與行舛，是己非人，專恣無忌，尊身忽物。

translations.literal: Since last year when the Great Carriage went south, Biao concurrently served as Minister, working together day and night—only then did I learn that his words and conduct diverged, praising himself and blaming others, acting wilfully without restraint, honoring himself and neglecting others.
translations.idiomatic: Since last year, when the imperial procession went south and Biao concurrently served as Minister, working with him day and night, I came to see that his words and deeds diverged: he praised himself and blamed others, acted with unchecked wilfulness, and valued himself while disdaining everyone else.

sentences.zh: 臣與任城卑躬曲己，其所欲者無不屈從。

translations.literal: Your subject and the Prince of Rencheng bowed low and bent ourselves; whatever he desired, none failed to yield and follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng and I bowed and yielded to him; whatever he wanted, we never failed to comply.

sentences.zh: 依事求實，悉有成驗。

translations.literal: Seeking truth according to the facts, all had confirmatory proof.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating the facts, I found confirmatory proof for every charge.

sentences.zh: 如臣列得實，宜亟投彪於有北，以除奸矯之亂政；

translations.literal: If what your subject has listed is true, Biao should promptly be cast to the northern wastes, to remove the corrupt and perverse disorder of government;
translations.idiomatic: If what I have listed is true, Biao should promptly be cast into the northern wilds to remove this corrupt and perverse misrule;

sentences.zh: 如臣列無證，宜放臣於四裔，以息青蠅之白黑。

translations.literal: If what your subject has listed has no proof, your subject should be sent to the four borderlands, to still the blue flies' black-and-white slander.
translations.idiomatic: if what I have listed lacks proof, I should be sent to the four borderlands to still the buzzing of slander.

sentences.zh: 帝在懸瓠，覽表歎愕曰：「何意留京如此也！

translations.literal: The Emperor was at Xuanhu; reading the memorial he sighed in astonishment and said: "Who would have thought that staying in the capital he was like this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was at Xuanhu. Reading the memorial, he sighed in astonishment and said: "Who would have thought he behaved like this while left in the capital!"

sentences.zh: 」有司處彪大辟；

translations.literal: " The responsible office sentenced Biao to death;
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible office sentenced Biao to death;

sentences.zh: 帝恕之，除名而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned him, merely removing his name from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned him and merely struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 彪尋歸本鄉。

translations.literal: Biao soon returned to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Biao soon returned to his native place.

sentences.zh: 帝北幸鄴，彪野服稱草茅臣，拜迎鄴南。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went north to Ye, Biao in common clothes called himself a humble grass-thatched subject and bowed in welcome south of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor traveled north to Ye, Biao came in plain clothes, calling himself a humble commoner, and bowed in welcome south of the city.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕以卿為已死。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I thought you were already dead."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I thought you were already dead."

sentences.zh: 」彪對曰：「子在，回何敢死。

translations.literal: " Biao replied: "While the Master lives, how dare Hui die?"
translations.idiomatic: " Biao replied: "While the Master lives, how dare Hui die?"

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，因謂曰：「朕期卿每以貞松為志，歲寒為心，卿應報國，盡心為用，近見彈文，殊乖所以。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was pleased, and thereupon said: "I expected you always to take the steadfast pine as your aspiration and the cold of winter as your heart; you should repay the state and serve with all your heart. Recently reading the impeachment papers, it greatly deviates from what I intended."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased and then said: "I expected you always to take the steadfast pine as your ideal and the cold of winter as your test of character. You should serve the state with all your heart. Reading the impeachment papers recently, I find they greatly miss the point."

sentences.zh: 卿罹此譴，為朕與卿？

translations.literal: Did you suffer this reprimand for Me and you?
translations.idiomatic: Did you suffer this punishment because of you and me?

sentences.zh: 為宰事？

translations.literal: For the chief minister's affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Because of the chief minister?

sentences.zh: 為卿自取？

translations.literal: Or did you bring it upon yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Or did you bring it on yourself?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「臣愆由己至，罪自身招，實非陛下橫與臣罪，又非宰事無辜濫臣。

translations.literal: " Biao said: "Your subject's fault came from myself; the crime was drawn by my own person. Truly it was not that Your Majesty wrongly imposed guilt on me, nor that the chief minister without cause wrongly accused me."
translations.idiomatic: " Biao said: "The fault was mine alone; I brought the punishment on myself. It was not that Your Majesty wrongly condemned me, nor that the chief minister falsely accused me without cause."

sentences.zh: 臣罪既如此，宜伏東皋之下，不應遠點屬車之清塵。

translations.literal: Since my guilt is such as this, I should prostrate myself beneath the eastern mulberry; I ought not from afar touch the clear dust of the imperial retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Since my guilt is such as this, I ought to lie prostrate beneath the eastern mulberry and have no business coming from afar to touch the dust of Your Majesty's retinue.

sentences.zh: 但伏承聖躬不豫，臣肝膽塗地，是以敢至，非謝罪而來。

translations.literal: But humbly I heard that the Sacred Person was unwell; my liver and gall would be smeared on the ground—therefore I dared to come; not to come to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: But I humbly heard that Your Majesty was unwell, and my heart was torn with concern—therefore I dared to come, not to offer an apology.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕欲用卿，憶李僕射不得。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I wish to employ you, but remembering Director Li, I cannot."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "I wish to employ you again, but when I think of Director Li, I cannot."

sentences.zh: 」帝尋納宋弁之言，將復採用。

translations.literal: " Soon the Emperor accepted Song Bian's words and was about to employ him again.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the Emperor accepted Song Bian's advice and was about to employ him again.

sentences.zh: 會留台表至，言彪與御史賈尚往窮庶人恂事，理有誣抑，奏請收彪。

translations.literal: Just then a memorial arrived from the Rear Capital, saying Biao and Censor Jia Shang had gone to investigate the commoner Xun case, and the case involved false suppression; it requested that Biao be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a memorial arrived from the Rear Capital saying that Biao and Censor Jia Shang had investigated the case of the commoner Xun and that the proceedings involved wrongful suppression; it requested Biao's arrest.

sentences.zh: 彪自言事枉，帝明彪無此，遣左右慰勉之。

translations.literal: Biao himself said the matter was wrongful; the Emperor knew Biao had not done this and sent attendants to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao declared that the case was wrongful. The Emperor knew Biao had done no such thing and sent attendants to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 聽以牛車散載，送之洛陽。

translations.literal: He was permitted to go in an ox-cart with scattered baggage, and was sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to travel by ox-cart with his belongings scattered about and was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會赦得免。

translations.literal: He happened to receive an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was then issued and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 宣武踐阼，彪自托于王肅，又與郭祚、崔光、劉芳、甄琛、邢巒等詩書往來，迭相稱重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Biao attached himself to Wang Su, and also exchanged poems and letters with Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, Liu Fang, Zhen Chen, Xing Luan, and others, each in turn praising one another's weight.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Biao attached himself to Wang Su and exchanged poems and letters with Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, Liu Fang, Zhen Chen, Xing Luan, and others, each praising the other's eminence in turn.

sentences.zh: 因論求復舊職，修史官之事，肅等許為左右。

translations.literal: Thereupon they discussed seeking restoration to his former post and the matter of repairing the historiographic office; Su and the others promised to assist on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: They then discussed seeking restoration to his former post and reviving the historiographic office, and Su and the others promised to support him.

sentences.zh: 彪乃表曰：

translations.literal: Biao thereupon submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Biao thereupon submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 惟我皇魏之奄有中華也，歲越百齡，年幾十紀，史官敘錄，未充其盛。

translations.literal: Only consider that our august Wei in embracing all of China—years surpass a century, ages nearly ten decades—yet the historians' narrative has not matched that greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Consider that our august Wei has held all of China for more than a century, nearly ten decades, yet the historians' record has not matched that greatness.

sentences.zh: 加以東觀中圮，冊勳有闕，美隨日落，善因月稀。

translations.literal: Moreover the Eastern Pavilion collapsed midway; meritorious deeds in the annals have gaps; virtues faded with the setting sun, good deeds grew sparse with the waning moon.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Eastern Pavilion fell into ruin midway through, meritorious deeds went unrecorded in the annals, and fine achievements faded like the setting sun while good deeds grew scarce as the waning moon.

sentences.zh: 故諺曰：「一日不書，百事荒蕪。

translations.literal: Hence the proverb says: "One day without writing—a hundred affairs lie waste."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the proverb says: "One day without writing, and a hundred affairs fall into ruin."

sentences.zh: 」至於太和之十一年，先帝，先後召名儒博達之士，以充麟閣之選。

translations.literal: " As for the eleventh year of Taihe, the Former Emperor, former and later, summoned renowned scholars and broadly learned men to fill the selections at the Qilin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: " As for the eleventh year of Taihe, the Former Emperor summoned renowned scholars and broadly learned men to fill the posts at the Qilin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 于時忘臣眾短，采臣片志，令臣出納，授臣丞職，猥屬斯事，無所與讓。

translations.literal: At that time forgetting your subject's many shortcomings, adopting your subject's partial aspiration, ordering your subject to enter and exit the archives, granting your subject the assistant post, unworthily entrusted with this affair, without anything to yield to others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, overlooking my many shortcomings and taking note of my limited ambition, he ordered me to serve in the archives, granted me the assistant post, and unworthily entrusted me with this work, which I did not yield to anyone else.

sentences.zh: 高祖時詔臣曰：「平爾雅志，正爾筆端，書而不法，後世何觀。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time an edict told your subject: "Level your lofty aspiration, straighten your brush-tip; if what you write is not according to law, what will later ages look upon?"
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozu's time an edict told me: "Set your lofty ambition straight and keep your brush true. If what you write is not according to proper standards, what will later ages have to look upon?"

sentences.zh: 」臣奉以周旋，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: " Your subject received this and carried it through, not daring to let it fall away.
translations.idiomatic: " I received this charge and carried it out, not daring to let it slip.

sentences.zh: 伏惟孝文皇帝承天地之寶，崇祖宗之業，景功未就，奄焉崩殂，凡百黎萌，若無天地。

translations.literal: Humbly consider Emperor Xiaowen received the treasure of Heaven and Earth, exalted the enterprise of ancestors; his brilliant achievement was not yet complete when suddenly he perished; all the common folk were as if without Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly consider that Emperor Xiaowen received the treasure of Heaven and Earth and exalted the enterprise of his ancestors, yet his great achievement was not yet complete when he suddenly perished, and all the common people were as if left without Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 賴遇陛下體明睿之真，應保合之量，恢大明以燭物，履靜恭以和邦。

translations.literal: Fortunately meeting Your Majesty embodying enlightened wisdom in truth, responding with the capacity to preserve and harmonize, broadly extending great brilliance to illuminate all things, treading in quiet reverence to harmonize the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately we now have Your Majesty, who embodies true enlightened wisdom, possesses the capacity to preserve and harmonize, broadly extends great brilliance to illuminate all things, and treads in quiet reverence to bring harmony to the realm.

sentences.zh: 天清其氣，地樂其靜，可謂重明疊聖，元首康哉。

translations.literal: Heaven clears its qi, earth delights in its stillness—it may be called redoubled brightness upon sages; the Head, how at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven clears its air and earth rejoices in its stillness—it may truly be called an age of redoubled sage-kings; the sovereign is secure indeed!

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「善跡者欲人繼其行，善歌者欲人繼其聲。

translations.literal: The Record says: "He who leaves good tracks wishes people to continue his path; he who sings well wishes people to continue his sound."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "He who leaves good tracks wishes others to follow in his path; he who sings well wishes others to carry on his song."

sentences.zh: 」故《傳》曰：「文王基之，周公成之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the Tradition says: "King Wen laid the foundation; the Duke of Zhou completed it."
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore the Tradition says: "King Wen laid the foundation; the Duke of Zhou completed it."

sentences.zh: 」然先皇之茂勳聖達，今王之懿美洞鑒，准之前代，其德靡悔也。

translations.literal: " Yet the Former Emperor's lush merit and sagely attainment, the present King's fine beauty and penetrating insight—measured against former ages, his virtue has nothing to regret.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet the Former Emperor's abundant merit and sagely attainment, and the present King's fine virtue and penetrating insight—measured against former ages, leave nothing to regret.

sentences.zh: 時哉時哉，可不光昭哉！

translations.literal: The time! The time! How could it not shine brightly!
translations.idiomatic: What a time! What a time! How could it not shine forth in glory!

sentences.zh: 合德二儀者，先皇之陶鈞也。

translations.literal: He who matched the virtue of the Two Principles—that was the Former Emperor's potter's wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Matching the virtue of Heaven and Earth—that was the Former Emperor shaping the realm on his potter's wheel.

sentences.zh: 齊明日月者，先皇之洞照也。

translations.literal: Equal in brightness to sun and moon—that was the Former Emperor's penetrating illumination.
translations.idiomatic: Equal in brilliance to the sun and moon—that was the Former Emperor's penetrating illumination.

sentences.zh: 慮周四時者，先皇之茂功也。

translations.literal: Thought encompassing the four seasons—that was the Former Emperor's lush achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Thought encompassing all four seasons—that was the Former Emperor's abundant achievement.

sentences.zh: 合契鬼神者，先皇之玄燭也。

translations.literal: In accord with the tally of spirits and gods—that was the Former Emperor's mysterious torch.
translations.idiomatic: In accord with the will of spirits and gods—that was the Former Emperor's mysterious illumination.

sentences.zh: 遷都改邑者，先皇之達也。

translations.literal: Moving the capital and changing the city—that was the Former Emperor's far-reaching wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Moving the capital and changing the seat of government—that was the Former Emperor's far-reaching wisdom.

sentences.zh: 變是協和者，先皇之鑒也。

translations.literal: Changing what was wrong and harmonizing—that was the Former Emperor's mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting what was wrong and bringing harmony—that was the Former Emperor's discerning judgment.

sentences.zh: 思同書軌者，先皇之遠也。

translations.literal: Thought identical to unified script and cart tracks—that was the Former Emperor's far vision.
translations.idiomatic: Aspiring to unify script and cart tracks—that was the Former Emperor's far-reaching vision.

sentences.zh: 守在四夷者，先皇之略也。

translations.literal: Defense stationed among the four barbarians—that was the Former Emperor's strategic design.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping defense at the four frontiers—that was the Former Emperor's strategic design.

sentences.zh: 海外有截者，先皇之威也。

translations.literal: Beyond the seas there was order—that was the Former Emperor's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Order established even beyond the seas—that was the Former Emperor's authority.

sentences.zh: 禮由岐陽者，先皇之義也。

translations.literal: Rites originating from Qiyang—that was the Former Emperor's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Rites originating from Qiyang—that was the Former Emperor's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 張樂岱郊者，先皇之仁也。

translations.literal: Spreading music at the foot of Mount Tai—that was the Former Emperor's benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Spreading music at the foot of Mount Tai—that was the Former Emperor's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 鑾幸幽漠者，先皇之智也。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage journeying to the dark desert—that was the Former Emperor's wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial procession journeying to the northern desert—that was the Former Emperor's wisdom.

sentences.zh: 燮伐南荊者，先皇之禮也。

translations.literal: Harmonizing and chastising southern Jing—that was the Former Emperor's ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing relations while chastising southern Jing—that was the Former Emperor's ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 升中告成者，先皇之肅也。

translations.literal: Ascending the summit to report completion—that was the Former Emperor's solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending the central peak to report completion—that was the Former Emperor's solemn reverence.

sentences.zh: 親虔宗社者，先皇之敬也。

translations.literal: Personally reverent toward the altars of state—that was the Former Emperor's reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Personally reverent toward the altars of state—that was the Former Emperor's devotion.

sentences.zh: 兗實無闕者，先皇之德也。

translations.literal: Yan's grain stores without shortfall—that was the Former Emperor's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's granaries filled without shortfall—that was the Former Emperor's virtue.

sentences.zh: 開物成務者，先皇之貞也。

translations.literal: Opening things and completing affairs—that was the Former Emperor's steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: Opening new possibilities and completing great undertakings—that was the Former Emperor's steadfast resolve.

sentences.zh: 觀乎人文者，先皇之蘊也。

translations.literal: Observing the patterns of culture—that was the Former Emperor's deep store.
translations.idiomatic: Contemplating the patterns of civilization—that was the Former Emperor's deep cultivation.

sentences.zh: 革弊創新者，先皇之志也。

translations.literal: Reforming abuses and creating the new—that was the Former Emperor's aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Reforming abuses and creating the new—that was the Former Emperor's aspiration.

sentences.zh: 孝慈道洽者，先皇之衷也。

translations.literal: Filial piety and compassion pervading the Way—that was the Former Emperor's inner heart.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety and compassion pervading the realm—that was the Former Emperor's innermost heart.

sentences.zh: 先皇有大功二十，加以謙尊而光，為而弗有者，可謂四三皇而六五帝矣。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor had twenty great achievements; adding to this humble honor yet radiant, acting yet not claiming possession—he may be called one who matched three of the Three Sovereigns and six of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor had twenty great achievements; added to this, he was humble yet radiant, accomplished yet claiming nothing for himself—he may be said to have matched three of the Three Sovereigns and six of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 誠宜功書於竹素，聲播于金石。

translations.literal: Truly his achievements should be written on bamboo and silk, his fame spread through bronze and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Truly his achievements ought to be written on bamboo and silk and his fame inscribed in bronze and stone.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂史官之達者，大則與日月齊其明，小則與四時並其茂，故能聲流無窮，義昭來裔。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that when historiographers attain mastery, in greatness they match sun and moon in brilliance, in small matters they match the four seasons in flourishing—thus their fame flows without end, their meaning shines for coming generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to say that when historiographers attain mastery, in great matters they match the sun and moon in brilliance, in small matters they match the four seasons in flourishing—thus their fame flows without end and their meaning shines for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 是以金石可滅，而風流不泯者，其唯載籍乎。

translations.literal: Therefore though bronze and stone may perish, yet elegant reputation does not die—is this not solely through written records?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, though bronze and stone may perish, elegant reputation endures—is this not solely through the written record?

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「相門有相，將門有將。

translations.literal: The proverb says: "A minister's gate has ministers; a general's gate has generals."
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says: "A minister's house produces ministers; a general's house produces generals."

sentences.zh: 」斯不唯其性，蓋言習之所得也。

translations.literal: " This is not only their nature—it largely speaks of what habit and training acquire.
translations.idiomatic: " This depends not on nature alone—it speaks rather of what training and habit can achieve.

sentences.zh: 竊謂天文之官，太史之職，如有其人，宜其世矣。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that the office of heavenly observances, the post of Grand Historian—if there is such a man, how fitting for his generation!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to say that for the office of heavenly observances and the post of Grand Historian, if there is a man suited to the task, how fitting he would be for this age!

sentences.zh: 是以談、遷世事而功立，彪、固世事而名成，此乃前鑒之軌轍，後鏡之蓍龜也。

translations.literal: Therefore Tan and Qian finished worldly affairs and established achievement; Biao and Gu completed worldly affairs and achieved fame—this is the track of a former mirror, the oracle tortoise of a later looking-glass.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Tan and Qian completed their worldly tasks and established lasting achievement; Biao and Gu completed theirs and won enduring fame—this is the track of a mirror for those who came before and an oracle for those who come after.

sentences.zh: 然前代史官之不終業者，皆陵遲之世，不能容善。

translations.literal: Yet those historiographers of former ages who did not finish their work—all were in declining ages that could not tolerate goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those historiographers of former ages who did not finish their work all lived in declining times that could not tolerate excellence.

sentences.zh: 是以平子去史而成賦，伯喈違閣而就志。

translations.literal: Therefore Pingzi left the history office and completed his rhapsody; Boyong abandoned the pavilion and pursued his record.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhang Heng left the history office and completed his rhapsody, and Cai Yong abandoned the pavilion and pursued his own chronicle.

sentences.zh: 近僭晉之世，有佐郎王隱，為著作虞預所毀，亡官在家。

translations.literal: In the recent usurping Jin age, there was Assistant Gentleman Wang Yin, destroyed by Compiler Yu Yu, stripped of office and living at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent Jin usurpation era, there was Assistant Gentleman Wang Yin, ruined by Compiler Yu Yu, who lost his office and lived at home.

sentences.zh: 晝則樵薪供爨，夜則觀文屬綴，集成《晉書》，存一代之事。

translations.literal: By day he gathered firewood to supply the cooking; by night he read texts and joined passages together, compiling the *History of Jin* and preserving the affairs of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: By day he gathered firewood for the hearth; by night he read texts and stitched passages together, compiling the *History of Jin* and preserving the affairs of an entire age.

sentences.zh: 司馬紹敕尚書唯給筆劄而已。

translations.literal: Sima Shao ordered the Ministry of State Affairs to supply only writing slips.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shao ordered the Ministry of State Affairs to supply him with nothing but writing materials.

sentences.zh: 國之大籍，成於私家，末世之弊，乃至如此。

translations.literal: The great records of the state were completed in a private household—the abuses of a declining age reached even to this.
translations.idiomatic: The great records of the state were completed in a private household—the abuses of a declining age had sunk to this.

sentences.zh: 此史官之不遇時也。

translations.literal: This was historiographers failing to meet their time.
translations.idiomatic: This was what it meant for historiographers to be out of step with their age.

sentences.zh: 今大魏之史，職則身貴，祿則親榮，優哉遊哉，式穀令爾休矣！

translations.literal: Now the historians of great Wei—the post itself is personally honored, the salary brings familial glory; easy and at leisure, may goodness make you prosper!
translations.idiomatic: Now the historians of great Wei hold honored posts and salaries that bring glory to their families—how easy and pleasant their lot! May goodness make them prosper!

sentences.zh: 而典謨弗恢者，其有以也。

translations.literal: Yet that the canonical records are not fully restored—there are reasons for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the canonical records remain incomplete—and there are reasons for it.

sentences.zh: 而故著作漁陽傅毗、北平陽尼、河間邢產、廣平宋弁、昌黎韓顯宗並以文才見舉，注述是同，並登年不永，弗終茂績。

translations.literal: Former compilers Fu Pi of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, Xing Chan of Hejian, Song Bian of Guangping, and Han Xianzong of Changli were all recommended for literary talent and shared the same task of annotation and composition, yet all died before their years were full and did not finish their lush achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Former compilers Fu Pi of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, Xing Chan of Hejian, Song Bian of Guangping, and Han Xianzong of Changli were all recommended for literary talent and shared the same historiographic work, yet all died young and failed to complete their great undertakings.

sentences.zh: 前著作程靈虯同時應舉，共掌此務，今徙他職，官非所司。

translations.literal: Former compiler Cheng Lingqiu was recommended at the same time and jointly managed this task; now transferred to another post, his office is no longer what he oversees.
translations.idiomatic: Former compiler Cheng Lingqiu was recommended at the same time and jointly managed this work, but has now been transferred to another post and no longer oversees historiography.

sentences.zh: 唯著作崔光一人，雖不移任，然侍官兩兼，故載述致闕。

translations.literal: Only Compiler Cui Guang alone, though not transferred from his post, yet holding two concurrent court offices, therefore caused gaps in the narrative record.
translations.idiomatic: Only Compiler Cui Guang, though not transferred from his post, held two concurrent court offices and therefore left gaps in the historical record.

sentences.zh: 臣聞載籍之興，由於大業；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the rise of written records comes from great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that written records arise from great enterprise;

sentences.zh: 雅頌垂薦，起於德美。

translations.literal: the Odes and Hymns handed down in recommendation spring from virtue and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: and that the Odes and Hymns handed down for praise spring from virtue and excellence.

sentences.zh: 昔史談誡其子遷曰：「當世有美而不書，汝之罪也。

translations.literal: Formerly Shi Tan admonished his son Qian saying: "When the age has beauty yet you do not write it—that is your crime."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shi Tan admonished his son Qian, saying: "If the age has excellence and you fail to record it, that is your crime."

sentences.zh: 」是以久而見美。

translations.literal: " Therefore over time beauty is seen.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore excellence becomes visible over time.

sentences.zh: 孔明在蜀，不以史官留意，是以久而受譏。

translations.literal: Kongming in Shu did not pay attention to the historiographic office, and therefore over time received ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Kongming in Shu paid no attention to the historiographic office, and therefore over time came to be ridiculed for it.

sentences.zh: 《書》稱「無曠庶官，」《詩》有「職思其憂」，臣雖今非所司，然昔忝斯任，故不以草茅自疏，敢言及於此。

translations.literal: The *Documents* say "Let no common office stand idle," the *Odes* have "In office, think of its cares"—your subject though not now in charge of this, yet formerly unworthily held this post, therefore do not hold myself aloof as a humble commoner, and dare to speak of this.
translations.idiomatic: The *Documents* say, "Let no common office stand idle," and the *Odes* have, "In office, think of its cares." Though I no longer hold this post, I once unworthily did, and so I do not hold myself aloof as a humble commoner but dare to speak of this matter.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「患為之者不必知，知之者不得為。

translations.literal: A saying goes: "The trouble is that those who would do it need not know how; those who know how may not do it."
translations.idiomatic: A saying goes: "The trouble is that those who would do the work need not know how, while those who know how may not do it."

sentences.zh: 」臣誠不知，強欲為之耳。

translations.literal: " Your subject truly does not know, yet strongly wishes to do it—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " I truly do not know enough, yet I strongly wish to do it all the same.

sentences.zh: 竊尋先朝賜臣名彪者，遠則擬《漢史》之叔皮，近則准《晉史》之紹統，推名求義，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: Your subject privately considers that the Former Court granted your subject the name Biao—distantly comparing to Shupi of the *History of Han*, recently matching Shaotong of the *History of Jin*—weighing the name to seek its meaning, wishing to stop yet unable.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject privately considers that when the Former Court granted me the name Biao, it was distantly comparing me to Ban Shupi of the *History of Han* and recently to Zhang Shaotong of the *History of Jin*. Weighing the name for its meaning, I wish to stop yet cannot.

sentences.zh: 今求都下乞一靜處，綜理國籍，以終前志。

translations.literal: Now I request in the capital a quiet place, to organize the national records and finish my former aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Now I request a quiet place in the capital where I may organize the national records and fulfill my former aspiration.

sentences.zh: 官給事力，以充所須。

translations.literal: The office should supply laborers to meet what is needed.
translations.idiomatic: The office should supply clerks and attendants to meet my needs.

sentences.zh: 雖不能光啟大錄，庶不為飽食終日耳。

translations.literal: Though I cannot brilliantly open the great record, I hope at least not to end my days with a full belly and nothing done.
translations.idiomatic: Though I cannot brilliantly open the great historical record, I hope at least not to end my days with a full belly and nothing accomplished.

sentences.zh: 近則期月可就，遠則三年有成，正本蘊之麟閣，副貳藏之名山。

translations.literal: Near term, it may be completed within a month; far term, within three years there will be achievement—the original stored in the Qilin Pavilion, the duplicate kept on the famous mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the near term it may be completed within a month; at most within three years it will be done—the original stored in the Qilin Pavilion, a duplicate kept on the sacred mountain.

sentences.zh: 時司空北海王詳、尚書令王肅許之。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Works Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang and Director Wang Su approved it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Works Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang and Director Wang Su approved the request.

sentences.zh: 肅以其無祿，頗相賑餉。

translations.literal: Su, because he had no salary, considerably aided and supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Biao had no salary, Su considerably aided and supplied him.

sentences.zh: 遂在秘書省，同王隱故事，白衣修史。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the Secretariat, following Wang Yin's precedent, he compiled history as a commoner in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he worked in the Secretariat, following Wang Yin's precedent, compiling history as a commoner in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 宣武親政，崔光表曰：「臣昔為彪所致，與之同業積年，其志力貞強，考述無倦。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power, Cui Guang submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject was formerly recruited by Biao and worked in the same field with him for many years; his will and strength are steadfast and strong, his investigation and composition without weariness."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power, Cui Guang submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject was formerly recruited by Biao and worked with him in the same field for many years. His will and strength are steadfast, and his research and writing know no weariness."

sentences.zh: 頃來契闊，多所廢離，近蒙收起，還綜厥事。

translations.literal: Recently we have been parted, much abandoned and separated; recently he was mercifully taken back in and has resumed organizing this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Recently we have been parted and much of our work abandoned; recently he was mercifully taken back in and has resumed organizing this project.

sentences.zh: 老而彌厲，史才日新。

translations.literal: Old yet ever more vigorous, his historiographic talent renews day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Growing old yet ever more vigorous, his historiographic talent improves day by day.

sentences.zh: 若克復舊職，專功不殆，必能昭明《春秋》，闡成皇籍。

translations.literal: If he can recover his former post and devote himself without slackening, he will surely be able to illuminate the *Spring and Autumn Annals* and complete the imperial records.
translations.idiomatic: If he can recover his former post and devote himself without slackening, he will surely illuminate the *Spring and Autumn Annals* and complete the imperial historical record.

sentences.zh: 既先帝厚委，宿曆高班，纖負微愆，應從滌洗。

translations.literal: Since the Former Emperor heavily entrusted him and he long held high rank, a slight fault should be washed away.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Former Emperor heavily entrusted him and he long held high rank, a slight fault ought to be washed away.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜申以常伯，正綰著作。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say he should be appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and properly put in charge of compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to say he should be appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and properly put in charge of the historiographic office.

sentences.zh: 」宣武不許。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanwu did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu did not approve.

sentences.zh: 詔彪兼通直散騎常侍、行汾州事，非彪好也，固請不行。

translations.literal: An edict made Biao concurrently Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service and acting administrator of Fenzhou affairs—not to Biao's liking; he firmly requested not to go.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Biao concurrently Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service and acting administrator of Fenzhou—not to Biao's liking; he firmly requested not to go.

sentences.zh: 卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: He died in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 始彪為中尉，號為嚴酷。

translations.literal: When Biao first served as Censor-in-Chief, he was known as severe and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao first served as Censor-in-Chief, he was known for severity and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 以奸款難得，乃為木手擊其脅腋，氣絕而復屬者時有焉。

translations.literal: Because confessions of guilt were hard to obtain, he had a wooden cudgel strike their ribs and armpits; there were times when breath ceased and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Because confessions were hard to obtain, he had prisoners struck in the ribs and armpits with a wooden cudgel; sometimes they lost consciousness and were revived.

sentences.zh: 又慰喻汾州叛胡，得其凶渠，皆鞭面殺之。

translations.literal: He also comforted and persuaded the rebel Hu of Fenzhou; obtaining their ringleaders, he whipped their faces and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He also pacified the rebel Hu of Fenzhou; capturing their ringleaders, he whipped their faces and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 及彪病，體上往往瘡潰，痛毒備極。

translations.literal: When Biao fell ill, on his body sores often ulcerated, pain and poison reaching the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao fell ill, sores often ulcerated across his body, and the pain was extreme.

sentences.zh: 贈汾州刺史，諡曰剛憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Inspector of Fenzhou; his posthumous title was Gangxian (Steadfast and Lawful).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Inspector of Fenzhou with the posthumous title Gangxian, Steadfast and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 彪在秘書歲餘，史業竟未及就，然區分書體，皆彪之功。

translations.literal: Biao was in the Secretariat for more than a year; the historiographic work in the end was not completed, yet the classification of writing styles—all were Biao's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Biao spent more than a year in the Secretariat; the historiographic work was never completed, yet the classification of writing styles was entirely his achievement.

sentences.zh: 述《春秋三傳》，合成十卷。

translations.literal: He expounded the Three Commentaries on the *Spring and Autumn*, compiling them into ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He expounded the Three Commentaries on the *Spring and Autumn*, compiling them into ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其餘著詩頌賦誄章表別有集。

translations.literal: His other compositions—poems, eulogies, rhapsodies, dirges, memorials—are collected separately.
translations.idiomatic: His other works—poems, eulogies, rhapsodies, dirges, and memorials—were collected separately.

sentences.zh: 彪雖與宋弁結管、鮑交，弁為大中正，與孝文私議，猶以寒地處之，殊不欲微相優假。

translations.literal: Though Biao formed a Guan-Zhong and Bao-Shuya friendship with Song Bian, when Bian served as Grand Rectifier and privately discussed with Emperor Xiaowen, he still treated him as from a cold district, utterly unwilling to show the slightest favor.
translations.idiomatic: Though Biao formed a deep friendship with Song Bian like Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya, when Bian served as Grand Rectifier and privately discussed the matter with Emperor Wen, he still treated Biao as a man of humble origin and was utterly unwilling to show him the slightest favor.

sentences.zh: 彪亦知之，不以為恨。

translations.literal: Biao also knew this and did not take it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Biao knew this and bore no resentment.

sentences.zh: 弁卒，彪痛之無已，為之哀誄，備盡辛酸。

translations.literal: When Bian died, Biao grieved for him without end, composing a mournful dirge for him, fully expressing bitterness and grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian died, Biao grieved for him without end and composed a mournful dirge that fully expressed his bitterness and sorrow.

sentences.zh: 郭祚為吏部，彪為子志求官，祚乃以舊第處之。

translations.literal: When Guo Zuo was Minister of Personnel, Biao sought an office for his son Zhi; Zuo thereupon placed him according to his old rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zuo was Minister of Personnel, Biao sought an office for his son Zhi, and Zuo assigned him according to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 彪以位經常伯，又兼尚書，謂祚應以貴遊拔之，深用忿怨，形於言色。

translations.literal: Biao, whose rank had passed through Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and who had also concurrently served as Minister, considered that Zuo ought to have promoted him as a noble associate; deeply resentful, this showed in his words and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, who had held the rank of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and had also concurrently served as Minister, felt Zuo ought to have promoted his son as a noble associate. Deeply resentful, he showed it plainly in word and countenance.

sentences.zh: 時論以此非祚。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion criticized Zuo for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion criticized Zuo for this.

sentences.zh: 祚每曰：「爾與義和至友，豈能饒爾而怨我乎。

translations.literal: Zuo often said: "You and Yihe are the closest of friends—can you spare yourself yet blame me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuo often said: "You and Yihe are the closest of friends—can you spare yourself yet blame me for this?"

sentences.zh: 」任城王澄與彪先亦不穆，及為雍州，彪詣澄，為志求其府寮。

translations.literal: " Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng and Biao had formerly not been on good terms; when Cheng became governor of Yongzhou, Biao visited Cheng to seek a staff post for Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng and Biao had not been on good terms, but when Cheng became governor of Yongzhou, Biao visited him to seek a staff post for Zhi.

sentences.zh: 澄釋然為啟，得為列曹行參軍，時稱澄之美。

translations.literal: Cheng readily submitted a recommendation; Zhi obtained the post of Acting Staff Officer of the Various Bureaus, and at the time Cheng's magnanimity was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng readily submitted a recommendation, and Zhi obtained the post of Acting Staff Officer of the Various Bureaus. At the time Cheng's magnanimity was praised.

sentences.zh: 志字鴻道，博學有才幹，年十餘，便能屬文。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Hongdao, was broadly learned and capable; before he was even ten, he could compose writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Hongdao, was broadly learned and capable. Before he was even ten, he could compose literary works.

sentences.zh: 彪奇之，謂崔鴻曰：「子宜與鴻道為二鴻於洛陽。

translations.literal: Biao marveled at him and said to Cui Hong: "You ought to be two hong-birds with Hongdao in Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: Biao marveled at him and said to Cui Hong: "You and Hongdao ought to be the two great swans of Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 」鴻遂與交款往來。

translations.literal: " Hong thereupon formed a warm friendship and exchanged visits with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong thereupon formed a warm friendship with him and they exchanged visits.

sentences.zh: 彪有女，幼而聰令。

translations.literal: Biao had a daughter who from childhood was clever and gifted.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had a daughter who was clever and gifted from childhood.

sentences.zh: 彪每奇之，教之書學，讀誦經傳。

translations.literal: Biao always marveled at her, teaching her writing and learning, reading and reciting the classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Biao always marveled at her and taught her writing and learning, having her read and recite the classics and commentaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗竊謂所親曰：「此當興我家，卿曹容得其力。

translations.literal: He once privately told those close to him: "This one will surely raise our house; you all may perhaps receive her strength."
translations.idiomatic: He once privately told those close to him: "This girl will surely raise our house; you may all benefit from her someday."

sentences.zh: 」彪亡後，宣武聞其名，召為婕好。

translations.literal: " After Biao died, Emperor Xuanwu heard her name and summoned her as Lady of Handsome Fairness.
translations.idiomatic: " After Biao died, Emperor Xuanwu heard of her and summoned her as a palace lady.

sentences.zh: 在宮常教帝妹書，誦授經史。

translations.literal: In the palace she often taught the Emperor's younger sister writing, reciting and instructing in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace she often taught the Emperor's younger sister to write and instructed her in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 始彪奇志及婕妤，特加器愛。

translations.literal: At first Biao marveled at Zhi and the Lady, especially valuing and loving them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Biao especially valued and loved Zhi and his daughter the palace lady.

sentences.zh: 公私坐集，必自稱詠，由是為孝文所貴。

translations.literal: At public and private gatherings when seated together, he always himself recited and praised them, and thereby was valued by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: At public and private gatherings he always recited their works himself, and thereby came to be valued by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及彪亡後，婕妤果入掖廷，後宮咸師宗之。

translations.literal: After Biao died, the Lady indeed entered the Rear Palace; all the inner palace took her as teacher and model.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao died, his daughter indeed entered the inner palace, and all the women of the harem took her as their teacher and model.

sentences.zh: 宣武崩後，為比丘尼，通習經義，法座講說，諸僧歎重之。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanwu died, she became a Buddhist nun, thoroughly versed in scriptural meaning; from the dharma seat she lectured and expounded, and the monks sighed in admiration of her.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanwu died, she became a Buddhist nun, thoroughly versed in scriptural doctrine. From the dharma seat she lectured and expounded, and the monks admired her deeply.

sentences.zh: 志曆官所在著績。

translations.literal: Zhi in each office he held achieved notable results.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi achieved notable results in every office he held.

sentences.zh: 桓叔興外叛，南荊荒毀，領軍元叉舉其才任撫導，抉為南荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Huan Shuxing rebelled abroad, southern Jing lay waste and ruined; Garrison General Yuan Cha recommended his talent for pacification and guidance, and he was selected as Inspector of Southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Shuxing rebelled, southern Jing lay in ruins. Garrison General Yuan Cha recommended Zhi's talent for pacification and guidance, and he was appointed Inspector of Southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 建義初，叛入梁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he rebelled and entered Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, he rebelled and defected to Liang.

sentences.zh: 志弟游，有才行。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother You had talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother You had talent and ability.

sentences.zh: 隨兄志在南荊州，屬爾硃之亂，與志俱奔江左。

translations.literal: Following his elder brother Zhi in Southern Jingzhou, when the Erzhu rebellion occurred, he fled with Zhi to the lands east of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his elder brother Zhi to Southern Jingzhou; when the Erzhu rebellion broke out, he fled with Zhi to the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 子昶。

translations.literal: His son was Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶小名那。

translations.literal: Chang's childhood name was Na.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's childhood name was Na.

sentences.zh: 性峻急，不雜交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and impatient; he did not mix in social relations.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was stern and impatient, and he did not mix freely in social circles.

sentences.zh: 幼年已解屬文，有聲洛下。

translations.literal: From youth he already understood composition and had a reputation below Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he could already compose literary works and had a reputation in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽初置明堂，昶年十數歲，為《明堂賦》，雖優洽未足，才制可觀。

translations.literal: At the time Luoyang had just established the Bright Hall; Chang was in his teens and composed a *Rhapsody on the Bright Hall*—though its polish was not yet sufficient, its talent and structure were worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang had just established the Bright Hall, Chang, still in his teens, composed a *Rhapsody on the Bright Hall*. Though its polish was not yet complete, its talent and structure were impressive.

sentences.zh: 見者咸曰有家風也。

translations.literal: Those who saw it all said he had the family style.
translations.idiomatic: All who read it said he had inherited the family talent.

sentences.zh: 初謁周文，周文深奇之，厚加資給，令入太學。

translations.literal: When he first paid court to Emperor Wen of Zhou, Emperor Wen deeply marveled at him, generously supplied him, and ordered him to enter the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When he first paid court to Emperor Wen of Zhou, the Emperor deeply marveled at him, generously supported him, and ordered him to enter the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 周文每見學生，必問才行於昶。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wen of Zhou saw students, he always asked Chang about their talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Wen of Zhou saw students, he always asked Chang about their talent and character.

sentences.zh: 昶神情清悟，應對明辯，周文每稱歎之。

translations.literal: Chang's spirit and expression were clear and perceptive; in response he was bright and eloquent—Emperor Wen of Zhou always praised and sighed over him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's bearing was clear and perceptive, and his replies were bright and eloquent. Emperor Wen of Zhou always praised him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 綏德公陸通盛選僚采，請以昶為司馬，周文許之。

translations.literal: Duke of Suide Lu Tong carefully selected staff members and requested Chang as Marshal; Emperor Wen of Zhou approved.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Suide Lu Tong carefully selected staff members and requested Chang as his Marshal. Emperor Wen of Zhou approved.

sentences.zh: 昶雖年少，通特加接待，公私之事，咸取決焉。

translations.literal: Though Chang was young, Tong especially treated him with favor; public and private affairs all took their decisions from him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chang was young, Tong especially favored him, and all public and private affairs were decided by him.

sentences.zh: 又兼二千石郎中，典儀注。

translations.literal: He also concurrently served as Gentlemen of the Two Thousand Bushels, managing ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He also concurrently served as Gentleman of the Two Thousand Bushels, managing ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 累遷都官郎中、相州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Gentleman of the Palace Guard and Grand Rectifier of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Gentleman of the Palace Guard and Grand Rectifier of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 昶雖處郎官，周文恆欲以書記委之。

translations.literal: Though Chang held a gentleman post, Emperor Wen of Zhou always wished to entrust secretarial duties to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chang held a gentleman post, Emperor Wen of Zhou always wished to entrust secretarial duties to him.

sentences.zh: 於是以為丞相府記室參軍、著作郎、修國史，轉大行台郎中、中書侍郎，又轉黃門侍郎，對臨黃縣伯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made Staff Secretary of the Chancellor's Office, Compiler, and editor of the national history; transferred to Gentleman of the Grand Secretariat, Vice Director of the Secretariat; again transferred to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Baron of Huang in Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was made Staff Secretary of the Chancellor's Office, Compiler, and editor of the national history; then transferred to Gentleman of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Director of the Secretariat; then to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed as Baron of Huang in Lin.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂曰：「卿祖昔在中朝，為御史中尉；

translations.literal: He once said to him: "Your grandfather formerly in the Central Court served as Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: He once said to him: "Your grandfather formerly served in the Central Court as Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 卿操尚貞固，理應不墜家風。

translations.literal: your conduct and aspirations are steadfast and firm—you ought by rights not to let the family style fall.
translations.idiomatic: your conduct is steadfast and firm—you ought by rights to uphold the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 但孤以中尉彈劾之官，愛憎所在，故未即授卿耳。

translations.literal: But I, because the censorate is an office of impeachment where likes and dislikes hold sway, therefore have not immediately granted it to you.
translations.idiomatic: But because the censorate is an office of impeachment where personal likes and dislikes hold sway, I have not immediately granted it to you.

sentences.zh: 然此職久曠，無以易卿。

translations.literal: Yet this post has long stood vacant—there is no one to replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this post has long stood vacant, and there is no one better suited to it than you.

sentences.zh: 」乃奏昶為御史中尉，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he memorialized that Chang be made Censor-in-Chief and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he memorialized that Chang be made Censor-in-Chief and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜內史下大夫，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Inner Scribe and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Inner Scribe and advanced in rank to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，行禦伯中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, he acted as Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Earl.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, he served as acting Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Earl.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，除中外府司錄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, he was appointed Chief Recorder of the Inner and Outer Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng, he was appointed Chief Recorder of the Inner and Outer Offices.

sentences.zh: 保定初，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，轉禦正中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Trappings, and transferred to Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with Grand Master of the Third Rank privileges and transferred to Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 時以近侍清要，盛選國華，乃以昶及安昌西元則、中都公陸逞、臨淄公唐瑾等並為納言。

translations.literal: At the time, because close attendance was clear and essential, the finest talents of the state were lavishly selected; Chang and Anchang West Yuan Ze, Duke of Zhongdu Lu Cheng, Duke of Linzi Tang Jin, and others were all made Remonstrating Officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because close attendance at court was a clear and essential post, the finest talents of the state were lavishly selected; Chang, Yuan Ze of Anchang West, Duke of Zhongdu Lu Cheng, Duke of Linzi Tang Jin, and others were all made Remonstrating Officials.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced in rank to Duke.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為昌州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he went out as Inspector of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was appointed Inspector of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州遇疾，求入朝，詔許之。

translations.literal: While in the province he fell ill, requested to enter court, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the province he fell ill and requested permission to return to court; an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 未至京，卒，贈相、瀛二州刺史。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital, he died; posthumously granted Inspector of Xiang and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching the capital he died and was posthumously granted the posts of Inspector of Xiang and Ying.

sentences.zh: 昶，周文世已當樞要。

translations.literal: Chang, in Emperor Wen of Zhou's age, already held pivotal importance.
translations.idiomatic: Chang already held a pivotal position in Emperor Wen of Zhou's reign.

sentences.zh: 兵馬處分，專以委之；

translations.literal: Disposition of troops and horses was entirely entrusted to him;
translations.idiomatic: The disposition of troops and horses was entirely entrusted to him;

sentences.zh: 詔冊文筆，皆昶所作也。

translations.literal: Edicts, patents, and literary compositions—all were composed by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts, patents, and official documents were all composed by Chang.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護執政，委任如舊。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Yu Hu took power, his entrustment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yu Hu took power, Chang's responsibilities remained as before.

sentences.zh: 昶常曰：「文章之事，不足流於後世，經邦致化，庶及古人。

translations.literal: Chang often said: "The matter of literary composition is not enough to flow to later ages; governing the state and bringing transformation—perhaps one may reach the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Chang often said: "Literary composition alone is not enough to endure for posterity; governing the state and bringing transformation—there one may hope to match the ancients."

sentences.zh: 」故所作文筆，了無槁草，唯留心政事而已。

translations.literal: " Therefore the compositions he wrote had not a single draft—he attended only to governmental affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore he left behind almost no literary drafts, devoting himself solely to governmental affairs.

sentences.zh: 又以父在江南，身寓關右，自少及終，不飲酒聽樂。

translations.literal: Also because his father was in Jiangnan while he himself resided in Guanxi, from youth to the end he did not drink wine or listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father remained in the south while he himself lived in the northwest, from youth to the end of his life he neither drank wine nor listened to music.

sentences.zh: 時論以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 子丹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 高道悅，字文欣，遼東新昌人也。

translations.literal: Gao Daoyue, courtesy name Wenxin, was a native of Xinchang in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daoyue, courtesy name Wenxin, was a native of Xinchang in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖策，馮跋散騎常侍、新昌侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ce was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary to Feng Ba and Marquis of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ce served Feng Ba as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 祖育，馮弘建德令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Magistrate of Jiande under Feng Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu was Magistrate of Jiande under Feng Hong.

sentences.zh: 太武東討，率部歸命，授建忠將軍、齊郡建德二郡太守，賜爵肥如子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu marched east on campaign, he led his division to submit; he was granted General Who Establishes Loyalty and Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Qijun and Jiande, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu marched east on campaign, he led his division to submit. He was granted General Who Establishes Loyalty, appointed Grand Administrator of Qijun and Jiande, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Feiru.

sentences.zh: 父玄起，武邑太守，遂居勃海蓧縣。

translations.literal: His father Xuanqi was Grand Administrator of Wuyi and thereupon settled in Tiao County in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuanqi was Grand Administrator of Wuyi and settled in Tiao County in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 道悅少為中書學生、侍御主文中散。

translations.literal: Daoyue in youth was a student of the Secretariat and Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Daoyue was a student of the Secretariat and Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 後為諫議大夫，正色當官，不憚強禦。

translations.literal: Later he became Grand Master of Remonstrance, maintaining stern countenance in office and not fearing the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Grand Master of Remonstrance, maintaining a stern bearing in office and not fearing the powerful.

sentences.zh: 車駕南征，徵兵秦、雍，大期秋季閱集洛陽。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, troops were levied from Qin and Yong; the great deadline was autumn for review and assembly at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession marched south on campaign, troops were levied from Qin and Yong, with a deadline of autumn for review and assembly at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 道悅以使者書侍御史薛聰、侍御史主文中散元志等稽違期會，奏舉其罪。

translations.literal: Daoyue, because envoys' letters showed Attendant Censor Xue Cong, Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service in charge of documents Yuan Zhi, and others had delayed and violated the deadline, memorialized to impeach them for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyue memorialized to impeach Attendant Censor Xue Cong, Attendant Cavalier in Direct Service Yuan Zhi, and others for delaying and missing the deadline, as shown by the envoys' reports.

sentences.zh: 又奏兼左僕射、吏部尚書、任城王澄，位總朝右，任屬戎機，兵使會否，曾不檢奏。

translations.literal: He further memorialized that Concurrent Left Director, Minister of Personnel, and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, whose position commanded the right of court and whose duty belonged to military affairs, regarding whether troops and envoys met the deadline, had never inspected and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He further memorialized that Concurrent Left Director, Minister of Personnel, and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, who commanded the right flank of court and bore responsibility for military affairs, had never inspected or reported whether the troops and envoys met the deadline.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞公孫良職綰樞轄，蒙冒莫舉。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Ministry Gongsun Liang, whose duty held the pivot of control, covered up and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Gongsun Liang, whose duty controlled the pivot of administration, covered up the matter and failed to report it.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免澄、良等所居官。

translations.literal: He requested that on the basis of present matters Cheng, Liang, and the others be removed from the offices they held.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that Cheng, Liang, and the others be removed from office on the basis of these facts.

sentences.zh: 時道悅兄觀為外兵郎中，澄奏道悅有党兄之負，孝文詔責。

translations.literal: At the time Daoyue's elder brother Guan was Gentlemen of External Troops; Cheng memorialized that Daoyue bore the fault of favoring his elder brother, and Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Daoyue's elder brother Guan was Gentleman of External Troops. Cheng memorialized that Daoyue was guilty of favoring his brother, and Emperor Wen issued an edict rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 然以事經恩宥，遂寢而不論。

translations.literal: Yet because the matter had passed through imperial grace and pardon, it thereupon was shelved and not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the matter had received imperial grace and pardon, it was shelved and not pursued.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「道悅資性忠篤，稟操貞亮。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Daoyue's natural endowment is loyal and sincere; his received conduct is steadfast and bright."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Daoyue is by nature loyal and sincere, and his character is steadfast and upright."

sentences.zh: 居法樹平肅之規，處諫著必犯之節。

translations.literal: In upholding law he establishes rules of fairness and solemnity; in holding the remonstrance post he displays the integrity of one who must speak out.
translations.idiomatic: In upholding the law he establishes rules of fairness and solemnity; in holding the remonstrance post he displays the integrity of one who must speak out.

sentences.zh: 王公憚其風鯁，朕實嘉其一至，謇諤之誠，何愧黯、鮑也。

translations.literal: Princes and ministers fear his stern uprightness; We truly commend his single-minded devotion—his honest and forthright sincerity, how could it shame Ji An and Bao Shuya?
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers fear his stern uprightness; We truly commend his single-minded devotion. His honest and forthright sincerity would not shame Ji An or Bao Shuya.

sentences.zh: 其以為主爵下大夫，諫議如故。」

translations.literal: Let him be made Lower Grand Master of Ennoblement, retaining his remonstrance post as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be appointed Lower Grand Master of Ennoblement while retaining his remonstrance post as before."

sentences.zh: 車駕幸鄴，又兼御史中尉，留守洛京。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, he was also made Censor-in-Chief and remained to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession visited Ye, he was also appointed Censor-in-Chief and remained to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時宮闕初基，廟庫未構，車駕將水路幸鄴。

translations.literal: At the time the palace foundations were just laid and the ancestral temples and storehouses not yet built; the imperial carriage was about to travel to Ye by water route.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace foundations had just been laid and the ancestral temples and storehouses were not yet built. The imperial procession was about to travel to Ye by water.

sentences.zh: 已詔都水回營構之材，以造舟楫。

translations.literal: An edict had already ordered the Director of Waterways to divert construction materials to build boats and oars.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had already ordered the Director of Waterways to divert construction materials to build boats.

sentences.zh: 道悅表諫，以為闕居宇之功，作遊嬉之用，損耗殊倍。

translations.literal: Daoyue submitted a memorial remonstrating, considering that abandoning the work of dwelling construction for making pleasure craft, the waste was extraordinarily doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyue submitted a memorial of remonstrance, arguing that abandoning palace construction for pleasure craft would waste resources many times over.

sentences.zh: 又深薄之危，古今共慎。

translations.literal: Also the danger of deep waters—ancients and moderns alike have been cautious of it.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited the danger of deep waters, which ancients and moderns alike have always feared.

sentences.zh: 於是帝遂從陸路。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor thereupon took the land route.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Emperor took the land route instead.

sentences.zh: 轉道悅太子中庶子，正色立朝，嚴然難犯，宮官上下，咸畏憚之。

translations.literal: Daoyue was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Crown Prince; maintaining stern countenance at court, solemn and hard to violate, palace officials high and low all feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyue was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Crown Prince. Maintaining a stern bearing at court, he was solemn and formidable, and palace officials high and low all feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年秋，車駕幸中嶽，詔太子恂入居金墉。

translations.literal: In autumn of the twentieth year of Taihe, when the imperial carriage visited the Central Peak, an edict ordered Crown Prince Xun to enter and dwell at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the twentieth year of Taihe, when the imperial procession visited the Central Peak, an edict ordered Crown Prince Xun to take up residence at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 而恂潛謀還代，忿道悅前後規諫，遂於禁中殺之。

translations.literal: But Xun secretly plotted to return to Dai; resenting Daoyue's repeated admonitions before and after, he thereupon killed him within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: But Xun secretly plotted to return to Dai. Resenting Daoyue's repeated admonitions, he killed him within the palace precinct.

sentences.zh: 帝甚加悲惜，贈散騎常侍、營州刺史，並遣王人慰其妻子，又詔使者監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly added grief and regret, posthumously granting him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Inspector of Yingzhou, and sending a royal envoy to comfort his wife and children; an edict also ordered an envoy to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved deeply, posthumously granting him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Inspector of Yingzhou, sending a royal envoy to comfort his wife and children, and ordering an envoy to supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: 葬於舊塋，諡曰貞侯。

translations.literal: He was buried in the old tomb mound; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in the family tomb with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 宣武又追錄忠概，拜長子顯族給事中。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu further posthumously recorded his loyal spirit and appointed his eldest son Xianzu as Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu further honored his loyal spirit and appointed his eldest son Xianzu as Attendant Within the Gates.

sentences.zh: 顯族亦以忠厚見稱，卒于右軍將軍。

translations.literal: Xianzu was also praised for loyalty and honesty; he died as General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu was also praised for loyalty and honesty and died while serving as General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 顯族弟敬猷，有風度。

translations.literal: Xianzu's younger brother Jingyou had bearing and manner.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu's younger brother Jingyou had bearing and presence.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤西征，引為驃騎司馬。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin marched west on campaign, he recruited him as Marshal of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin marched west on campaign, he recruited Jingyou as Marshal of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤謀逆，敬猷與行台郎中封偉伯等潛圖義舉，謀泄見殺。

translations.literal: When Baoyin plotted rebellion, Jingyou with Mobile Secretariat Gentleman Feng Weibo and others secretly plotted a righteous rising; the plot leaked and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin plotted rebellion, Jingyou and Mobile Secretariat Gentleman Feng Weibo and others secretly plotted a righteous rising. The plot was discovered and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈滄州刺史，聽一子出身。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Inspector of Cangzhou; one son permitted to enter office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Inspector of Cangzhou, and one of his sons was permitted to enter office.

sentences.zh: 道悅長兄嵩，字昆侖，魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Daoyue's elder brother Song, courtesy name Kunlun, was Grand Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyue's elder brother Song, courtesy name Kunlun, was Grand Administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 嵩弟雙，清河太守。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Shuang was Grand Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Shuang was Grand Administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 坐黷貨，將刑於市，遇赦免。

translations.literal: Convicted of corrupt goods, about to be executed in the marketplace, he met an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of corruption and about to be executed in the marketplace, he was spared by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 時北海王詳為錄尚書事，雙多納金寶，除司空長史。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang was Recorder of Affairs of the Ministry of State Affairs; Shuang gave much gold and treasure and was appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang was Recorder of Affairs of the Ministry of State Affairs. Shuang gave him much gold and treasure and was appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 後為涼州刺史，專肆貪暴，以罪免。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Liangzhou, wantonly greedy and violent, and was removed from office for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Inspector of Liangzhou, where he was wantonly greedy and violent and was removed from office for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 後貨高肇，復起為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he bribed Gao Zhao and was restored as Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he bribed Gao Zhao and was restored as Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 以貪穢被劾，罪未判，遇赦復任。
