translations.literal: Impeached for greed and corruption, before judgment was passed he met an amnesty and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached for greed and corruption, he met an amnesty before judgment was passed and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 雙弟觀，尚書左外兵郎中、城陽王鸞司馬。

translations.literal: Shuang's younger brother Guan was Gentlemen of External Troops of the Left in the Ministry and Marshal to Prince of Chengyang Yuan Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's younger brother Guan was Gentleman of External Troops of the Left in the Ministry and Marshal to Prince of Chengyang Yuan Luan.

sentences.zh: 南征赭陽，先驅而歿，諡曰閔。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign against Zheyang, he died as vanguard; his posthumous title was Min.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign against Zheyang, he died while serving as vanguard. His posthumous title was Min.

sentences.zh: 甄琛，字思伯，中山毋極人，漢太保邯之後也。

translations.literal: Zhen Chen, courtesy name Sibo, was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen, courtesy name Sibo, was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan and a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Han.

sentences.zh: 父凝，州主簿。

translations.literal: His father Ning was Prefecture Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning was Prefecture Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 琛少敏悟。

translations.literal: Chen from youth was quick and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was quick and perceptive from youth.

sentences.zh: 閨門之內，兄弟戲狎，不以禮法自居。

translations.literal: Within the inner quarters, brothers played familiarly and did not hold themselves by ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Within the household, the brothers played familiarly among themselves and did not hold themselves to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 學覽經史，稱有刀筆。

translations.literal: In study he reviewed the classics and histories and was said to have skill with brush and knife.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics and histories and was said to have skill with the brush.

sentences.zh: 而形貌短陋，鮮風儀。

translations.literal: Yet his appearance was short and ugly, with little bearing and manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was short and plain in appearance, with little bearing or presence.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，入都積歲，頗以奕棋棄日，至乃通夜不止。

translations.literal: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he entered the capital and accumulated years, quite wasting days on chess, even continuing through the night without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he went to the capital and over the years wasted much time on chess, even playing through the night without stopping.

sentences.zh: 手下倉頭，常令執燭，或時睡頓，大加其杖，如此非一。

translations.literal: The household steward under his command he often ordered to hold the candle; if he sometimes dozed off, he greatly increased the beating—this happened more than once.
translations.idiomatic: He often ordered his household steward to hold the candle while he played. If the man dozed off, he beat him severely—more than once.

sentences.zh: 奴後不勝楚痛，乃曰：「郎君辭父母仕宦，若為讀書執燭，不敢辭罪，乃以圍棋，日夜不息，豈是向京之意？

translations.literal: The slave later could not bear the pain of the beating and said: "Master, leaving parents to take office—if it were to hold the candle for reading, I would not dare refuse the punishment; yet it is for go, day and night without rest—is this the intent of going to the capital?"
translations.idiomatic: The servant finally could not bear the beatings and said: "Master, you left your parents to take office. If you needed me to hold the candle while you read, I would not dare complain. But you play go day and night without rest—is this why you came to the capital?"

sentences.zh: 而賜加杖罰，不亦非理！

translations.literal: Yet you bestow increased beating and punishment—is this not also unreasonable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you beat me for it—is that not also unreasonable!

sentences.zh: 」琛悵然慚感。

translations.literal: " Chen was melancholy, ashamed, and moved.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen was moved to shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 遂從許赤彪假書研習，聞見日優。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Xu Chi and Li Biao he borrowed books to study and research; his knowledge and insight improved day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he borrowed books from Xu Chi and Li Biao to study, and his knowledge improved day by day.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜中書博士，遷諫議大夫，時有所陳，亦為孝文知賞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, he was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, transferred to Grand Master of Remonstrance; at times when he submitted proposals, he was also known and appreciated by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat and later transferred to Grand Master of Remonstrance. When he submitted proposals, Emperor Wen came to know and appreciate him.

sentences.zh: 宣武踐阼，以琛為中散大夫，兼御史中尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Chen was made Grand Master of Palace Attendance and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Chen was appointed Grand Master of Palace Attendance and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 琛表曰：

translations.literal: Chen submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 《月令》稱山林藪澤，有能取蔬食禽獸者，皆野虞教導之。

translations.literal: The *Monthly Ordinances* say that in mountains, forests, marshes, and lakes, those able to gather vegetables, food, birds, and beasts—all are instructed and guided by the wild-game wardens.
translations.idiomatic: The *Monthly Ordinances* say that in mountains, forests, marshes, and lakes, those able to gather vegetables, food, birds, and beasts are all instructed and guided by the wild-game wardens.

sentences.zh: 其迭相侵奪者，罪之無赦。

translations.literal: Those who repeatedly encroach and seize from one another—punish them without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who repeatedly encroach on one another are punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 此明導人而弗禁，通有無以相濟也。

translations.literal: This clearly means guiding people rather than forbidding them, opening what is lacking and what is abundant to aid one another.
translations.idiomatic: This clearly means guiding people rather than forbidding them, allowing what is abundant to aid what is lacking.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》雖有川澤之禁，正所以防其殘盡，必令取之有時。

translations.literal: Though the *Rites of Zhou* has prohibitions on rivers and marshes, this is precisely to guard against their complete exhaustion, necessarily ordering that taking be at proper times.
translations.idiomatic: Though the *Rites of Zhou* has prohibitions on rivers and marshes, this is precisely to guard against their complete exhaustion and to ensure that resources are taken only at proper times.

sentences.zh: 斯所謂鄣護在公，更所以為人守之耳。

translations.literal: This is what is called protective barriers held by the public—the purpose is for people to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called protective barriers held in the public trust—the purpose is for people to guard them on behalf of one another.

sentences.zh: 今者天為黔首生鹽，國為黔首鄣護。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has produced salt for the common people; the state protects it for the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has produced salt for the common people, and the state protects it on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 假獲其利，猶是富專口齗，不及四體也。

translations.literal: Even if one obtains its profit, it is still enriching only the mouth and teeth, not reaching the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one obtains its profit, it enriches only the mouth and teeth, not the whole body.

sentences.zh: 且天下夫婦，歲貢粟帛，四海之有，備奉一人；

translations.literal: Moreover, couples throughout the realm yearly tribute grain and silk; all that the four seas possess suffices to serve one person;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, couples throughout the realm yearly tribute grain and silk; all that the four seas possess suffices to serve one person;

sentences.zh: 軍國之資，取給百姓，天子亦何患乎貧，而苟禁一池？

translations.literal: resources for army and state are drawn from the common people—why should the Son of Heaven worry about poverty, yet grudgingly forbid one salt pond?
translations.idiomatic: the resources of army and state are drawn from the common people—why should the Son of Heaven worry about poverty, yet grudgingly forbid access to one salt pond?

sentences.zh: 臣每觀上古愛人之跡，時讀中葉驟稅之書，未嘗不歎彼遠大，惜此近狹。

translations.literal: Your subject whenever observes the traces of ancient love for people, and at times reads books of sudden taxation from the middle ages, has never failed to sigh at their far-reaching breadth and regret this near narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I observe how the ancients cared for the people, and read accounts of sudden taxation from the middle ages, I cannot help sighing at their far-reaching vision and regretting our present narrowness.

sentences.zh: 今偽弊相承，仍崇關廛之稅。

translations.literal: Now false abuses succeed one another, still honoring market-gate and stall taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Now false abuses succeed one another, and market-gate and stall taxes are still honored.

sentences.zh: 大魏宏博，唯受穀帛之輸。

translations.literal: Great Wei is vast and broad, accepting only the delivery of grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei is vast and broad, accepting only the delivery of grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 是使遠方聞者，莫不歌德。

translations.literal: This makes those who hear of it from afar none fail to sing of its virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This makes all who hear of it from afar sing of its virtue.

sentences.zh: 語稱出內之吝，有司之福；

translations.literal: A saying calls stinginess in disbursement the blessing of officials;
translations.idiomatic: A saying calls stinginess in disbursement the blessing of officials;

sentences.zh: 施惠之難，人君之禍。

translations.literal: the difficulty of bestowing favor the misfortune of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: and the difficulty of bestowing favor the misfortune of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 夫以府藏之物，猶以不施而為災，況府外之利，而可吝之於黔首？

translations.literal: For treasury goods, if not disbursed they still become disaster—how much more profits outside the treasury, that could be grudged to the common people?
translations.idiomatic: If goods in the treasury become a disaster when not disbursed, how much more profits outside the treasury—how can these be grudged to the common people?

sentences.zh: 願弛鹽禁，使沛然遠及。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to relax the salt prohibition, making it abundantly reach far.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes to relax the salt prohibition so that its benefits may flow abundantly to all.

sentences.zh: 依《周體》置川衡之法，使之監導而已。

translations.literal: Following the *Rites of Zhou*, establish the method of river wardens, having them oversee and guide—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Following the *Rites of Zhou*, establish river wardens to oversee and guide production—that is all.

sentences.zh: 詔付八坐議可否以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Eight Excellencies to deliberate whether it was feasible and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Eight Excellencies to deliberate on its feasibility and report back.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰、兼尚書邢巒等奏：

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, Concurrent Minister Xing Luan, and others submitted:
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, Concurrent Minister Xing Luan, and others submitted:

sentences.zh: 琛之所列，但恐坐談則理高，行之則事闕，是用遲回，未謂為可。

translations.literal: What Chen has listed—we only fear that seated discussion makes the principle lofty, but in execution affairs fall short; therefore we hesitate and do not consider it feasible.
translations.idiomatic: What Chen has proposed—we fear that in discussion the principle sounds lofty, but in execution it would fall short. Therefore we hesitate and do not consider it feasible.

sentences.zh: 竊惟大道既往，恩惠生焉，下奉上施，卑高理睦。

translations.literal: Your subjects privately consider that when the Great Way has passed, favor arises; the lower serves the upper and bestows, low and high are harmoniously ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects privately consider that when the Great Way has passed, favor arises; the lower serves the upper and bestows gifts, and low and high are harmoniously ordered.

sentences.zh: 恆恐財不賙國，澤不厚人，故多方以達其情，立法以行其志。

translations.literal: Always fearing that wealth cannot supply the state and bounty cannot enrich the people, therefore by many means to reach their sentiments, establishing laws to carry out their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Always fearing that wealth cannot supply the state and bounty cannot enrich the people, the rulers devised many means to understand the people's needs and established laws to carry out their purpose.

sentences.zh: 至乃取貨山澤，輕在人之貢；

translations.literal: Even to taking goods from mountains and marshes, lightening the people's tribute;
translations.idiomatic: They even took revenue from mountains and marshes, lightening the people's tribute;

sentences.zh: 立稅關市，裨十一之儲。

translations.literal: establishing taxes at passes and markets, supplementing the one-tenth store.
translations.idiomatic: established taxes at passes and markets, supplementing the state's reserves.

sentences.zh: 收此與彼，非利己也；

translations.literal: Collecting this and that—not for self-benefit;
translations.idiomatic: Collecting here and there was not for self-benefit;

sentences.zh: 回彼就此，非為身也。

translations.literal: turning that to this—not for the person.
translations.idiomatic: turning that to this was not for personal gain.

sentences.zh: 所謂集天地之產，惠天地之人，藉造物之富，賑造物之貧。

translations.literal: What is called gathering the produce of Heaven and Earth, favoring the people of Heaven and Earth, borrowing the wealth of creation, relieving the poverty of creation.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by gathering the produce of Heaven and Earth to benefit its people, borrowing the wealth of creation to relieve the poverty of creation.

sentences.zh: 禁此泉池，不專太官之禦；

translations.literal: Forbidding these springs and ponds—not solely for the Grand Steward's imperial supply;
translations.idiomatic: Forbidding these springs and ponds was not solely for the Grand Steward's imperial supply;

sentences.zh: 僉槠此匹帛，豈為後宮之資。

translations.literal: collecting together this cloth and silk—how could it be resources for the inner palace?
translations.idiomatic: collecting this cloth and silk was hardly resources for the inner palace alone.

sentences.zh: 既潤不在己，彼我理一，積而散之，將焉所吝。

translations.literal: Since the enrichment is not in oneself, other and self share one principle—accumulating and dispersing it, where would there be grudging?
translations.idiomatic: Since the enrichment is not for oneself alone, other and self share one principle—accumulating and dispersing wealth, where is there room for grudging?

sentences.zh: 然自行以來，典司多怠，出入之間，事不如法。

translations.literal: Yet since implementation began, those in charge have often been negligent; in the coming and going of goods, affairs have not accorded with law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since implementation began, those in charge have often been negligent, and in the handling of goods affairs have not accorded with law.

sentences.zh: 此乃用之者無方，非興之者有謬。

translations.literal: This is that those who use it have no method—not that those who established it were in error.
translations.idiomatic: This means those who administer it lack proper method—not that those who established the system were in error.

sentences.zh: 至使朝廷識者，聽營其間。

translations.literal: Even to the point that knowledgeable men at court were permitted to operate among them.
translations.idiomatic: Even knowledgeable men at court were permitted to operate among them.

sentences.zh: 今而罷之，懼失前旨。

translations.literal: Now to abolish it—we fear losing the former intent.
translations.idiomatic: To abolish it now would mean losing the original intent.

sentences.zh: 宜依前式。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the former model.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to follow the former model.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司鹽之稅，乃自古通典，然興制利人，亦世或不同。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The salt administration tax is an ancient universal institution, yet in establishing systems to benefit people, each age may differ."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The salt administration tax is an ancient universal institution, yet in establishing systems to benefit the people, each age may differ."

sentences.zh: 甄琛之表，實所謂助政毗俗者也。

translations.literal: Zhen Chen's memorial is truly what is called assisting government and harmonizing with custom.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen's memorial is truly what is meant by assisting government and harmonizing with custom.

sentences.zh: 可從其前計，尚書嚴為禁豪強之制也。」

translations.literal: His former plan may be followed; let the Ministry strictly enforce prohibitions against powerful local gentry."
translations.idiomatic: His former plan may be followed, and let the Ministry strictly enforce prohibitions against powerful local gentry."

sentences.zh: 詔琛參八坐議事，尋正中尉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chen to participate in the Eight Excellencies' deliberations; soon he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chen to participate in the Eight Excellencies' deliberations, and soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，領中尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant, retaining the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant while retaining the censorate.

sentences.zh: 琛俛眉畏避，不能繩糾貴遊，凡所劾者，率多下吏。

translations.literal: Chen lowered his brows in fear and avoidance, unable to straighten the rope and investigate noble associates; of those he impeached, most were lower officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chen lowered his brows in fear and avoidance, unable to investigate noble associates. Of those he impeached, most were lower officials.

sentences.zh: 于時趙修寵貴，琛傾身事之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Xiu was favored and honored; Chen devoted himself entirely to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Xiu was favored and honored, and Chen devoted himself entirely to serving him.

sentences.zh: 琛父凝為中散大夫，弟僧林為本州別駕，皆托修申達。

translations.literal: Chen's father Ning was Grand Master of Palace Attendance; his younger brother Senglin was Vice-Prefect of the native province—all entrusted Xiu to convey their requests.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's father Ning was Grand Master of Palace Attendance and his younger brother Senglin was Vice-Prefect of their native province—all entrusted Zhao Xiu to convey their requests.

sentences.zh: 至修奸詐事露，明當收考，今日乃舉其罪。

translations.literal: When Xiu's treacherous and deceitful affairs were exposed and it was clear he should be arrested and interrogated, only then did Chen today impeach him for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu's treacherous and deceitful affairs were exposed and it was clear he should be arrested and interrogated, only then did Chen impeach him.

sentences.zh: 及監決修鞭，猶相隱惻，然告人曰：「趙修小人，背如土牛，殊耐鞭杖。

translations.literal: When overseeing Xiu's execution by whipping, he still showed hidden sympathy, yet told others: "Zhao Xiu is a petty man; his back is like an earthen ox—extraordinarily able to endure the whip and staff."
translations.idiomatic: When overseeing Xiu's execution by whipping, he still showed hidden sympathy, yet told others: "Zhao Xiu is a petty man; his back is like an earthen ox and can endure the whip extraordinarily well."

sentences.zh: 」有識以此非之。

translations.literal: " Knowledgeable men criticized him for this.
translations.idiomatic: " Knowledgeable men criticized him for this.

sentences.zh: 修死之明日，琛與黃門郎李憑以朋黨被召詣尚書。

translations.literal: The day after Xiu died, Chen and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Ping were summoned to the Ministry on charges of faction.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xiu died, Chen and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Ping were summoned to the Ministry on charges of factionalism.

sentences.zh: 兼尚書元英、邢巒窮其阿附之狀。

translations.literal: Concurrent Ministers Yuan Ying and Xing Luan thoroughly investigated their fawning and attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Ministers Yuan Ying and Xing Luan thoroughly investigated their fawning attachment to Zhao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 琛曾拜官，諸賓悉集，巒乃晚至。

translations.literal: Chen once received an appointment; all guests had assembled, yet Luan arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen once received an appointment, all guests had assembled, yet Luan arrived late.

sentences.zh: 琛謂巒：「何處放蛆來，今晚始顧？

translations.literal: Chen said to Luan: "Where did you release the maggots from, that you only look in tonight?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen said to Luan: "Where did you release the maggots from, that you only show up tonight?"

sentences.zh: 」雖以言戲，巒變色銜忿。

translations.literal: " Though it was spoken in jest, Luan changed color and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " Though spoken in jest, Luan changed color and harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 及此，大相推窮。

translations.literal: At this time they greatly pressed and investigated each other.
translations.idiomatic: At this time they pressed the investigation against each other with great vigor.

sentences.zh: 司徒、錄尚書事、北海王詳等奏曰：

translations.literal: Minister of Education, Recorder of Affairs of the Ministry of State Affairs, Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang, and others submitted:
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education, Recorder of Affairs of the Ministry of State Affairs, Prince of Beihai Yuan Xiang, and others submitted:

sentences.zh: 謹案侍中、領御史中尉甄琛，身居直法，糾擿是司。

translations.literal: We respectfully report that Palace Attendant and Censor-in-Chief Zhen Chen, holding the post of straight law, has impeachment as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully report that Palace Attendant and Censor-in-Chief Zhen Chen, holding the post of upholding the law, has impeachment as his charge.

sentences.zh: 風邪響黷，猶宜劾糾，況趙修侵公害私，朝野切齒？

translations.literal: Wind and evil, sound and corruption—still ought to be impeached and investigated; how much more Zhao Xiu, who harmed the public for private gain, hated by court and countryside?
translations.idiomatic: Wind and corruption ought still to be impeached and investigated—how much more Zhao Xiu, who harmed the public for private gain and was hated by court and countryside alike?

sentences.zh: 而琛嘗不陳奏，方更往來，中外影響，致其談譽。

translations.literal: Yet Chen never submitted a memorial, but instead continued association; inside and outside echoed his influence, causing his reputation to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chen never submitted a memorial but instead continued to associate with him. Inside and outside court echoed his influence, enhancing Zhao Xiu's reputation.

sentences.zh: 令布衣之父，超登正四之官；

translations.literal: He caused a commoner's father to leap to a rank-four regular post;
translations.idiomatic: He caused a commoner's father to leap to a rank-four regular post;

sentences.zh: 七品之弟，越陟三階之祿。

translations.literal: a rank-seven younger brother to surpass three ranks in salary.
translations.idiomatic: and a rank-seven younger brother to surpass three ranks in salary.

sentences.zh: 虧先皇之選典，塵聖明之官人。

translations.literal: He damaged the Former Emperor's selection canon and sullied the sage and bright appointment of officials.
translations.idiomatic: He damaged the Former Emperor's selection standards and sullied the sage Emperor's appointment of officials.

sentences.zh: 又與黃門郎李憑，相為表裏。

translations.literal: Also with Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Ping, they were outer and inner to each other.
translations.idiomatic: He also acted in collusion with Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Ping.

sentences.zh: 憑兄叨封，知而不言。

translations.literal: Ping's elder brother presumptuously received enfeoffment; Chen knew yet did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's elder brother presumptuously received enfeoffment, and Chen knew yet did not speak.

sentences.zh: 及修釁彰，方加彈奏。

translations.literal: Only when Xiu's offense was manifest did he add impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Xiu's offense became manifest did he submit an impeachment.

sentences.zh: 生則附其形勢，死則就地排之。

translations.literal: While alive he attached to his power and influence; when dead he cast him aside on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao Xiu lived he attached himself to his power; when Xiu died he cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 竊天之功，以為己力，仰欺朝廷，俯罔百司。

translations.literal: Stealing Heaven's achievement as his own strength, looking up he deceived the court, looking down he misled the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: He stole credit that belonged to Heaven as his own strength, deceiving the court above and misleading the hundred offices below.

sentences.zh: 其為鄙詐，於茲甚矣。

translations.literal: His baseness and deceit—here it is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: His baseness and deceit reached an extreme here.

sentences.zh: 謹依律科從，請以職除。

translations.literal: Respectfully following the legal statutes, we request removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully following the legal statutes, we request his removal from office.

sentences.zh: 其父中散，實為叨越，雖皇族帝孫，未有此例。

translations.literal: His father's post as Grand Master of Palace Attendance was truly presumptuous overstepping; even for imperial clan and emperor's grandsons, there has been no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His father's post as Grand Master of Palace Attendance was truly presumptuous overstepping; even for imperial clansmen and the emperor's grandsons, there has been no such precedent.

sentences.zh: 既得不以倫，請下收奪。

translations.literal: Since it was obtained not according to proper order, we request it be seized and revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Since it was obtained improperly, we request that it be seized and revoked.

sentences.zh: 李憑朋附趙修，是親是仗，緇點皇風，塵鄙正化，此而不糾，將何以肅整阿諛，獎厲忠概？

translations.literal: Li Ping factionally attached to Zhao Xiu, relying on kinship and power, staining the imperial wind, sullying upright transformation—if this is not investigated, how will we sternly rectify flattery, reward and encourage loyal spirit?
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping factionally attached himself to Zhao Xiu, relying on kinship and power, staining the imperial style and sullying upright governance. If this is not investigated, how will we sternly rectify flattery and reward loyal spirit?

sentences.zh: 請免所居官以肅風軌。

translations.literal: We request removal from the offices they hold to solemnize conduct and standards.
translations.idiomatic: We request their removal from office to restore proper conduct and standards.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 琛遂免歸本郡。

translations.literal: Chen was thereupon removed and returned to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was thereupon removed from office and returned to his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 左右相連死黜者二十餘人。

translations.literal: More than twenty of his associates were connected in death or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty of his associates were connected in death or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 始琛以父母老，常求解官扶侍，故孝文授以本州長史。

translations.literal: At first Chen, because his parents were old, often requested release from office to support and attend them; therefore Emperor Xiaowen granted him Chief Clerk of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chen, because his parents were old, often requested release from office to support and attend them. Therefore Emperor Wen granted him Chief Clerk of his native province.

sentences.zh: 及貴達，不復請歸，至是乃還。

translations.literal: When he reached honor and advancement, he no longer requested return; only now did he go back.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached honor and advancement, he no longer requested to return home; only now did he go back.

sentences.zh: 供養數年，遭母憂。

translations.literal: He supported them for several years, then encountered his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He supported them for several years, then his mother died.

sentences.zh: 母钜鹿曹氏，有孝性。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Cao of Julu, who had filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Cao of Julu, a woman of filial nature.

sentences.zh: 夫氏去家，路逾百里，每得魚肉菜果珍美口實者，必令僮僕走奉其母，乃後食焉。

translations.literal: The husband's clan was far from home, the road more than a hundred li; whenever she obtained fish, meat, vegetables, fruit, or delicacies pleasing to the palate, she always ordered servants to run and present them to her mother-in-law, and only then ate herself.
translations.idiomatic: The husband's clan lived more than a hundred li away. Whenever she obtained fish, meat, vegetables, fruit, or other delicacies, she always sent servants to present them to her mother-in-law before eating herself.

sentences.zh: 琛母服未闋，復喪父。

translations.literal: Before Chen's mourning for his mother was complete, his father also died.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chen's mourning for his mother was complete, his father also died.

sentences.zh: 琛於塋兆內手種松柏，隆冬負掘水土。

translations.literal: Chen within the tomb precinct personally planted pines and cypresses; in deep winter he bore soil and water on his back to dig.
translations.idiomatic: Chen personally planted pines and cypresses within the tomb precinct, bearing soil and water on his back to dig even in deep winter.

sentences.zh: 鄉老哀之，咸助加力。

translations.literal: Village elders pitied him and all helped add their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Village elders pitied him and all came to help.

sentences.zh: 十餘年中，墳成木茂。

translations.literal: Within more than ten years, the tomb was complete and the trees lush.
translations.idiomatic: Within more than ten years, the tomb was complete and the trees flourished.

sentences.zh: 與弟僧林誓以同居沒齒，專事產業，躬親農圃，時以鷹犬馳逐自娛。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Senglin he vowed to live together to the end of their teeth, devoted solely to estate affairs, personally tending fields and gardens, at times amusing himself with hawks and hounds in the chase.
translations.idiomatic: With his younger brother Senglin he vowed to live together for life, devoting himself to estate affairs, personally tending fields and gardens, and at times amusing himself with hawking and hunting.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大事，猶上表陳情。

translations.literal: When the court had great affairs, he still submitted memorials stating his sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had great affairs, he still submitted memorials stating his views.

sentences.zh: 久之，復除散騎常侍，領給事黃門侍郎、定州大中正，大見親寵。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining Attendant Within the Gates Who Handles Affairs and Grand Rectifier of Dingzhou; he was greatly favored and cherished.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was again appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining Attendant Within the Gates Who Handles Affairs and Grand Rectifier of Dingzhou, and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 委以門下庶事，出參尚書，入廁帷幄。

translations.literal: Entrusted with miscellaneous affairs of the Secretariat, going out he participated in the Ministry, entering he attended within the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with miscellaneous affairs of the Secretariat, he participated in Ministry business when abroad and attended within the imperial curtain when at court.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，琛兼主客郎，迎送齊使彭城劉纘。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time, Chen concurrently served as Gentleman of Reception and saw off the Qi envoy Liu Zuan of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wen's time, Chen concurrently served as Gentleman of Reception and received and escorted the Qi envoy Liu Zuan of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 琛欽其器貌，常歎詠之。

translations.literal: Chen admired his talent and appearance and often sighed and praised him in verse.
translations.idiomatic: Chen admired his talent and appearance and often praised him in verse.

sentences.zh: 纘子昕為朐山戍主。

translations.literal: Zuan's son Xin was garrison commander of Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's son Xin was garrison commander of Qushan.

sentences.zh: 昕死，家屬入洛。

translations.literal: When Xin died, his family entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin died, his family entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 有女年未二十，琛乃納昕女為妻。

translations.literal: He had a daughter not yet twenty; Chen thereupon took Xin's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had a daughter not yet twenty, and Chen thereupon took her as his wife.

sentences.zh: 婚日，詔給廚費。

translations.literal: On the wedding day, an edict granted kitchen expenses.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding day, an edict granted kitchen expenses.

sentences.zh: 琛所好悅，宣武時調戲之。

translations.literal: The one Chen favored and delighted in—in Emperor Xuanwu's time he was teased about it.
translations.idiomatic: The woman Chen favored—in Emperor Xuanwu's time he was teased about it.

sentences.zh: 遷河南尹，黃門、中正如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Henan; Yellow Gate and Grand Rectifier posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Intendant of Henan while retaining his Yellow Gate and Grand Rectifier posts.

sentences.zh: 琛表曰：

translations.literal: Chen submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 國家居代，患多盜竊。

translations.literal: When the state dwelt in Dai, the affliction of theft was many.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was based in Dai, theft was rampant.

sentences.zh: 世祖太武皇帝親自發憤，廣置主司，裏宰皆以下代令長及五等散男有經略者乃得為之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu Taiwu personally roused himself in indignation, broadly establishing chief offices; ward chiefs were all drawn from lower-generation magistrates and district chiefs and fifth-rank scattered barons with strategic ability before they could hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu personally roused himself in indignation and broadly established chief offices. Ward chiefs were drawn only from lower-generation magistrates and fifth-rank scattered barons with strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 又多置吏士，為其羽翼。

translations.literal: He also broadly placed clerks and gentlemen as their wings.
translations.idiomatic: He also placed many clerks and gentlemen to serve as their support.

sentences.zh: 崇而重之，始得禁止。

translations.literal: Honoring and weighting them, only then could prohibition be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring and weighting these posts, only then could theft be stopped.

sentences.zh: 今遷都已來，天下轉廣；

translations.literal: Now since the capital was moved, the realm has grown broader;
translations.idiomatic: Now since the capital was moved, the realm has grown broader;

sentences.zh: 四遠赴會，事過代都。

translations.literal: the four directions far and near converge, affairs surpassing the capital of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: people converge from all four directions, and affairs surpass those of the old capital at Dai.

sentences.zh: 寇盜公行，劫害不絕。

translations.literal: Bandits and robbers walk openly; plunder and harm never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and robbers walk openly, and plunder never ceases.

sentences.zh: 此由諸坊混雜，厘比不精，主司闇弱，不堪檢察故也。

translations.literal: This is because the various wards are mixed and confused, household registration imprecise, chief offices dim and weak, unable to bear inspection—therefore.
translations.idiomatic: This is because the various wards are mixed and confused, household registration is imprecise, and the chief offices are weak and unable to conduct proper inspection.

sentences.zh: 今擇尹既非南金，裏尉鉛刀而割，欲望清肅都邑，不可得也。

translations.literal: Now the Intendant selected is not southern gold; ward wardens cut with lead knives—to desire clearing and solemnizing the capital city is unattainable.
translations.idiomatic: The Intendant selected is not the finest metal; ward wardens cut with lead knives—to expect the capital to be cleared and solemnized is impossible.

sentences.zh: 里正乃流外四品，職輕任碎，多是下才。

translations.literal: Ward chiefs are outside-the-flow rank four; their posts are light and duties fragmented, mostly men of lower talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ward chiefs are outside-the-flow rank four; their posts are light and duties fragmented, and most are men of lower talent.

sentences.zh: 人懷苟且，不能督察，故使盜得容奸，百賦失理。

translations.literal: People harbor perfunctory attitudes, unable to inspect and supervise, therefore allowing thieves to harbor wickedness and all taxes to lose order.
translations.idiomatic: People harbor perfunctory attitudes and cannot inspect or supervise properly, allowing thieves to operate and all taxes to fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 邊外小縣，所領不過百戶，而令長皆以將軍居之。

translations.literal: Small counties on the frontier administer no more than a hundred households, yet magistrates and chiefs all hold them as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Small frontier counties administer no more than a hundred households, yet their magistrates and chiefs all hold general ranks.

sentences.zh: 京邑諸坊，大者或千戶、五百戶，其中皆王公卿尹，貴勢姻戚，豪猾僕隸，廕養奸徒，高門邃宇，不可幹問。

translations.literal: Wards of the capital city, large ones perhaps a thousand or five hundred households—within them are all princes, dukes, ministers, and intendants, noble power and kin connections, fierce and cunning servants and slaves, sheltered and reared wicked men, high gates and deep halls—not to be approached and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Wards of the capital, some with a thousand or five hundred households, contain princes, dukes, ministers, and intendants, noble power and kin connections, fierce servants and slaves, sheltered criminals, and high gates and deep halls that cannot be approached or questioned.

sentences.zh: 比之邊縣，難易不同。

translations.literal: Compared with frontier counties, the difficulty and ease differ.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with frontier counties, the difficulty differs greatly.

sentences.zh: 今難彼易此，實為未愜。

translations.literal: Now making the difficult easy and the easy difficult—truly this is unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: To treat the difficult as easy and the easy as difficult is truly unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 王者立法，隨時從宜；

translations.literal: Kings establish laws, adapting to the times as fitting;
translations.idiomatic: Kings establish laws, adapting to the times as fitting;

sentences.zh: 先朝立品，不必即定。

translations.literal: the Former Court established ranks—not necessarily fixed immediately.
translations.idiomatic: the Former Court established ranks—not necessarily fixed immediately.

sentences.zh: 施而觀之，不便則改。

translations.literal: Implement and observe; if inconvenient, then change.
translations.idiomatic: Implement and observe; if inconvenient, then change.

sentences.zh: 今閑官靜任，猶聽長兼，況煩劇要務，不得簡能下領。

translations.literal: Now idle offices and quiet posts still permit long concurrent holding—how much more urgent and heavy essential affairs, which cannot be entrusted to selected talent of lower rank?
translations.idiomatic: Even idle offices and quiet posts still permit long concurrent holding—how much more urgent and essential affairs, which cannot be entrusted to lower-ranking men of talent?

sentences.zh: 請取武官中八品將軍以下幹用貞濟者，以本官俸恤領裏尉之任，各食其祿。

translations.literal: Your subject requests selecting from military officers of rank-eight generals and below those capable and steadfast in service, using their original office salary to hold ward warden posts, each eating their own stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject requests selecting from military officers of rank-eight generals and below those capable and steadfast in service to hold ward warden posts on their original salaries.

sentences.zh: 高者領六部尉，中者領經途尉，下者領里正。

translations.literal: Higher ones would lead the six-department wardens, middle ones the thoroughfare wardens, lower ones the ward chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Higher ones would lead the six-department wardens, middle ones the thoroughfare wardens, and lower ones the ward chiefs.

sentences.zh: 不爾，請少高裏尉之品，選下品中應遷者，進而為之。

translations.literal: If not, your subject requests slightly raising the rank of ward wardens, selecting from lower ranks those due for promotion, advancing them to hold the posts.
translations.idiomatic: If not, your subject requests slightly raising the rank of ward wardens and selecting from lower ranks those due for promotion to fill the posts.

sentences.zh: 則督責有所，輦轂可清。

translations.literal: Then supervision and responsibility would have a place, and the imperial carriage hub could be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Then supervision and responsibility would have a proper place, and the capital could be cleared of crime.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「里正可進至勳品、經途從九品、六部尉正九品諸職中簡取，何必須武人也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ward chiefs may be advanced to merit rank; thoroughfare wardens from rank nine; six-department wardens from rank nine regular posts—select from these. Why must they be military men?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Ward chiefs may be advanced to merit rank; thoroughfare wardens from rank nine; six-department wardens from rank nine regular posts—select from these. Why must they be military men?"

sentences.zh: 」琛又奏以羽林為游軍，于諸坊巷司察盜賊。

translations.literal: " Chen further memorialized to use the Feathered Forest as roaming troops, in the various wards and lanes inspecting and observing bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen further memorialized to use the Feathered Forest guards as roaming troops to inspect the various wards and lanes for bandits and thieves.

sentences.zh: 於是京邑清靜，後皆踵焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the capital city was cleared and quiet; later all followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the capital was cleared and quiet, and later all followed this model.

sentences.zh: 轉太子少保，黃門如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince; Yellow Gate remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince while retaining his Yellow Gate post.

sentences.zh: 及高肇死，琛以黨不宜復參朝政，出為營州刺史，遷涼州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao died, Chen, as a faction member, was deemed unfit to again participate in court politics; he went out as Inspector of Yingzhou, transferred to Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao died, Chen, as a faction member, was deemed unfit to participate in court politics again. He was sent out as Inspector of Yingzhou and later transferred to Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 猶以高氏之昵，不欲處之於內。

translations.literal: Still because of intimacy with the Gao clan, they did not wish to place him within.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his intimacy with the Gao clan, they still did not wish to place him within the capital.

sentences.zh: 久之，為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time, he became Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除定州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 固辭曰：「陛下在東宮，崔光為少傅，臣為少保，今光為車騎大將軍、儀同三司、開國公。

translations.literal: He firmly declined, saying: "When Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace, Cui Guang was Junior Tutor and your subject was Junior Guardian. Now Guang is General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the Third Rank, and Duke with an Established State."
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined, saying: "When Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace, Cui Guang was Junior Tutor and I was Junior Guardian. Now Guang is General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the Third Rank, and Duke with an Established State."

sentences.zh: 故僕射游肇時為侍中，與臣官階相似；

translations.literal: Former Director You Zhao at the time was Palace Attendant, similar in official rank to your subject;
translations.idiomatic: Former Director You Zhao at the time was Palace Attendant, similar in rank to me;

sentences.zh: 肇在省為僕射，死贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhao in the Ministry was Director; at death posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the Third Rank, and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao served in the Ministry as Director and at death was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the Third Rank, and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 臣今適為征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Your subject now happens to be General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: I now happen to be General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 生師保不如死遊肇。

translations.literal: Alive, tutor and guardian are not equal to dead You Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Alive, a tutor and guardian is worth less than the dead You Zhao.

sentences.zh: 」詔書慰遣之。

translations.literal: " An edict comforted and sent him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict comforted him and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 琛既至鄉，衣錦晝遊，大為稱滿；

translations.literal: When Chen reached his native place, clad in brocade he toured by day, greatly praised and satisfied;
translations.idiomatic: When Chen reached his native place, he toured in brocade by day to great acclaim;

sentences.zh: 政體嚴細，甚無聲譽。

translations.literal: his governance was strict and detailed, with very little reputation.
translations.idiomatic: but his governance was strict and detailed and won little reputation.

sentences.zh: 崔光辭司徒之授也，琛與光書，外相抑揚，內實附會。

translations.literal: When Cui Guang declined the grant of Minister of Education, Chen wrote to Guang—outwardly praising and disparaging in turn, inwardly truly attaching and aligning.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guang declined appointment as Minister of Education, Chen wrote to him—outwardly praising and disparaging in turn, but inwardly seeking to align himself with Guang.

sentences.zh: 光亦揣其意，復書以悅之。

translations.literal: Guang also gauged his intent and replied with a letter to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also gauged his intent and replied with a letter to please him.

sentences.zh: 徵為車騎將軍、特進，又拜侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Special Advance, and again appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Special Advance, and again appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以其衰老，詔賜禦府杖，朝直杖以出入。

translations.literal: Because of his old age, an edict granted him an imperial staff and a court-attendance staff for going in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his old age, an edict granted him an imperial staff and a court-attendance staff for going in and out.

sentences.zh: 卒，詔給東園秘器，贈司徒公、尚書左僕射，加後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: When he died, an edict granted Eastern Garden secret vessels; posthumously granted Duke Minister of Education and Left Director of the Ministry, with rear guard music added.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, an edict granted Eastern Garden secret vessels and posthumously granted him Duke Minister of Education and Left Director of the Ministry, with rear guard music added.

sentences.zh: 太常議諡文穆，吏部郎袁翻奏曰：

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Wenmu; Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Fan submitted:
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Wenmu; Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Fan submitted:

sentences.zh: 案禮，諡者行之跡也；

translations.literal: According to ritual, a posthumous title is the trace of conduct;
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, a posthumous title is the trace of conduct;

sentences.zh: 號者功之表也；

translations.literal: a style-name is the manifestation of achievement;
translations.idiomatic: a style-name is the manifestation of achievement;

sentences.zh: 車服者位之章也。

translations.literal: carriage and robes are the insignia of rank.
translations.idiomatic: carriage and robes are the insignia of rank.

sentences.zh: 是以大行受大名，細行受細名。

translations.literal: Therefore great conduct receives a great name, minor conduct receives a minor name.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore great conduct receives a great name and minor conduct receives a minor name.

sentences.zh: 行生於己，名生於人。

translations.literal: Conduct arises from oneself; name arises from others.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct arises from oneself; name arises from others.

sentences.zh: 故闔棺然後定諡，皆累其生時美惡，所以為將來勸戒；

translations.literal: Therefore only after the coffin is closed is the posthumous title fixed—all accumulating the good and bad of his living years, thereby serving as admonition for the future;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore only after the coffin is closed is the posthumous title fixed, accumulating the good and bad of his living years to serve as admonition for the future;

sentences.zh: 身雖死，使名常存也。

translations.literal: though the person dies, causing the name to endure.
translations.idiomatic: so that though the person dies, the name endures.

sentences.zh: 凡薨亡者，屬所即言大鴻臚，移本郡大中正。

translations.literal: For all who die in office, the responsible office immediately informs the Grand Herald, who transmits to the native commandery's Grand Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: For all who die in office, the responsible office immediately informs the Grand Herald, who transmits to the native commandery's Grand Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 條其行跡功過，承中正移，言公府，下太常部博士評議，為諡列上。

translations.literal: He lists conduct, achievements, and faults; receiving the Rectifier's transmission, reporting to the public offices, sending down to the Minister of Ceremonies' doctors for deliberation, fixing the posthumous title and submitting upward.
translations.idiomatic: He lists conduct, achievements, and faults; the report goes to the public offices, then to the Minister of Ceremonies' doctors for deliberation, who fix the posthumous title and submit it upward.

sentences.zh: 諡不應法者，博士坐如選舉不以實論。

translations.literal: If the posthumous title does not accord with law, the doctor is punished as for selection not according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: If the posthumous title does not accord with law, the doctor is punished as for selection not according to fact.

sentences.zh: 若行狀失實，中正坐如博士。

translations.literal: If the conduct report is untrue, the Rectifier is punished as the doctor.
translations.idiomatic: If the conduct report is untrue, the Rectifier is punished as the doctor.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，莫不殷勤重慎，以為褒貶之實也。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors and kings have all been earnest and careful, taking this as the substance of praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity emperors and kings have all been earnest and careful, taking this as the substance of praise and blame.

sentences.zh: 今之行狀，皆出自其家，任其臣子自言君父之行，無復是非之事。

translations.literal: Today's conduct reports all come from the family itself, allowing ministers and sons to speak of their lord and father's conduct themselves—no longer any matter of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Today's conduct reports all come from the family itself, allowing ministers and sons to speak of their lord and father's conduct themselves—with no regard for right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 臣子之欲光揚君父，但苦跡之不高，行之不美，是以極辭肆意，無復限量。

translations.literal: Ministers and sons wishing to glorify their lord and father, only troubled that the traces are not high and the conduct not beautiful, therefore use extreme words without restraint, no longer any limit.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and sons wishing to glorify their lord and father, troubled only that the traces are not lofty and the conduct not beautiful, use extreme words without restraint and without limit.

sentences.zh: 觀其狀也，則周、孔聯鏕，伊顏接衽。

translations.literal: Viewing their reports, then Zhou and Confucius walk side by side, Yi and Yan share the same robe.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing their reports, Zhou and Confucius walk side by side and Yi Yin and Yan Hui share the same robe.

sentences.zh: 論其諡也，雖窮文盡武，無或加焉。

translations.literal: Speaking of their posthumous titles, though exhausting literary and martial terms, none can be added.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of their posthumous titles, though literary and martial terms are exhausted, none can be added.

sentences.zh: 然今之博士與古不同，唯知依其行狀，又先問其家人之意；

translations.literal: Yet today's doctors differ from antiquity, knowing only to follow their conduct reports, and first asking the family's intent;
translations.idiomatic: Yet today's doctors differ from antiquity, knowing only to follow conduct reports and first asking the family's intent;

sentences.zh: 臣子所求，便為議上。

translations.literal: what ministers and sons request is immediately deliberated and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: whatever ministers and sons request is immediately deliberated and submitted.

sentences.zh: 都不復斟酌與奪，商量是非。

translations.literal: Entirely no longer weighing grant and denial, deliberating right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: No longer weighing grant and denial or deliberating right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 致號諡之加，與泛階莫異；

translations.literal: Causing the addition of style and posthumous title to differ not from general rank advancement;
translations.idiomatic: The addition of style and posthumous title differs not from general rank advancement;

sentences.zh: 專以極美為稱，無復貶降之名。

translations.literal: solely using utmost beauty as title, no longer any names of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: using only the most flattering titles, with no names of demotion.

sentences.zh: 禮官之失，一至於此。

translations.literal: The failure of ritual officers has reached even to this.
translations.idiomatic: The failure of ritual officers has reached this point.

sentences.zh: 案甄司徒行狀，至德與聖人齊蹤，鴻名共大賢比跡，文穆之諡，何足加焉。

translations.literal: In review of Minister of Education Zhen's conduct report—supreme virtue walks equal with sages, great name matches great worthies in trace—the posthumous title Wenmu, how could it be added to?
translations.idiomatic: In review of Minister of Education Zhen's conduct report—supreme virtue walks equal with sages and great name matches great worthies—the posthumous title Wenmu is more than sufficient.

sentences.zh: 但比來贈諡，於例普重，如甄之流，無不復諡。

translations.literal: But recently posthumous grants in precedent are universally heavy; men like Zhen, none fail to receive posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: But recently posthumous grants have been universally generous; men like Zhen invariably receive posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依諡法，慈惠愛人曰孝，宜諡曰孝穆公。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures that according to posthumous-title law, compassionate and benevolent love of people is called Xiao—it is fitting to posthumously title him Duke Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures that according to posthumous-title law, compassionate and benevolent love of people is called Xiao—it is fitting to posthumously title him Duke Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，明勒太常、司徒，有行狀如此，言辭流宕，無復節限者，悉請裁量，不聽為受。

translations.literal: From now onward, clearly instruct the Minister of Ceremonies and Minister of Education: when conduct reports are like this, words flowing unrestrained without limit, all please measure and cut—do not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: From now onward, clearly instruct the Minister of Ceremonies and Minister of Education: when conduct reports are like this, with words flowing unrestrained without limit, all such reports should be measured and cut—do not accept them.

sentences.zh: 仍踵前來之失者，皆付法司科罪。

translations.literal: Those who still follow the former failures—all hand over to the legal office for punishment according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Those who still follow the former failures should all be handed over to the legal office for punishment according to statute.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 琛祖載，明帝親送，降車就輿，吊服哭之，遣舍人慰其諸子。

translations.literal: When Chen's coffin was loaded, Emperor Ming personally escorted it, descending from his carriage to approach the bier, in mourning dress weeping for him, sending a palace attendant to comfort his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's coffin was loaded, Emperor Ming personally escorted it, descending from his carriage to approach the bier and weeping in mourning dress. He sent a palace attendant to comfort Chen's sons.

sentences.zh: 琛性輕簡，好嘲謔，故少風望。

translations.literal: Chen's nature was light and simple, fond of mockery and jest—therefore he had little reputation and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's nature was light and simple and fond of mockery and jest, and therefore he had little reputation and esteem.

sentences.zh: 然明解有幹具，在官清白。

translations.literal: Yet he was clear in understanding and capable in affairs; in office he was clean and honest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was clear in understanding and capable in affairs, and in office he was clean and honest.

sentences.zh: 自孝文、宣武，咸相知待。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaowen and Emperor Xuanwu, all knew and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wen and Emperor Xuanwu onward, all knew and treated him well.

sentences.zh: 明帝以師傅之義而加禮焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming because of the tutor's bond added ceremony toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming added ceremony toward him because of their bond as tutor and pupil.

sentences.zh: 所著文章，鄙碎無大體，時有理詣。

translations.literal: The writings he composed were vulgar and fragmented without great structure, yet at times had rational insight.
translations.idiomatic: The writings he composed were vulgar and fragmented without great structure, yet at times showed rational insight.

sentences.zh: 《磔四聲》、《姓族廢興》、《會通緇素三論》及《家晦》二十篇，《篤學文》一卷，頗行於世。

translations.literal: *Dissecting the Four Tones*, *Rise and Fall of Clans*, *Three Treatises on Harmonizing Black and White*, and twenty chapters of *Family Obscurity*, one scroll of *Essay on Earnest Study*—all circulated somewhat in the world.
translations.idiomatic: *Dissecting the Four Tones*, *Rise and Fall of Clans*, *Three Treatises on Harmonizing Black and White*, and twenty chapters of *Family Obscurity*, plus one scroll of *Essay on Earnest Study*, all circulated to some extent.

sentences.zh: 琛長子侃，字道正，位秘書郎。

translations.literal: Chen's eldest son Kan, courtesy name Daozheng, held the post of Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's eldest son Kan, courtesy name Daozheng, held the post of Secretary.

sentences.zh: 性險薄，多與盜劫交通。

translations.literal: His nature was treacherous and base; he often associated with bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was treacherous and base, and he often associated with bandits and robbers.

sentences.zh: 隨琛在京，以酒色夜宿洛水亭舍，毆擊主人。

translations.literal: Following Chen in the capital, because of wine and women he lodged overnight at a Luoyang River pavilion lodge and beat the host.
translations.idiomatic: Following Chen to the capital, he spent a night at a Luoyang River pavilion lodge indulging in wine and women and beat the host.

sentences.zh: 為司州所劾，淹在州獄。

translations.literal: Impeached by the Department of State Affairs, he lingered in the provincial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached by the Department of State Affairs, he lingered in the provincial prison.

sentences.zh: 琛大以慚慨。

translations.literal: Chen was greatly ashamed and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was greatly ashamed and indignant.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷為牧，與琛先不協，欲具案窮推。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai was governor; he and Chen had not been on good terms before and wished to fully investigate and press the case.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai was governor. He and Chen had not been on good terms and wished to fully investigate and press the case.

sentences.zh: 琛托左右以聞，宣武敕懷寬放。

translations.literal: Chen entrusted attendants to report it; Emperor Xuanwu ordered Huai to release him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Chen entrusted attendants to report the matter; Emperor Xuanwu ordered Huai to release Kan leniently.

sentences.zh: 懷固執之，久乃特旨出侃。

translations.literal: Huai firmly held to the case; only after a long time did a special edict release Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Huai firmly held to the case; only after a long time did a special edict release Kan.

sentences.zh: 自此沈廢，卒家。

translations.literal: From this he sank into disgrace and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: From this he sank into disgrace and died at home.

sentences.zh: 侃弟楷，字德方。

translations.literal: Kan's younger brother Kai, courtesy name Defang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's younger brother Kai, courtesy name Defang.

sentences.zh: 粗有文學，頗更吏事。

translations.literal: He had rough literary learning and considerable experience in clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had some literary learning and considerable experience in clerical affairs.

sentences.zh: 琛啟除秘書郎。

translations.literal: Chen memorialized for his appointment as Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Chen memorialized for his appointment as Secretary.

sentences.zh: 宣武崩，未葬，楷與河南尹丞張普惠等飲戲，免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, before burial Kai with Assistant Intendant of Henan Zhang Puhui and others drank and played games; he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, before burial Kai drank and played games with Assistant Intendant of Henan Zhang Puhui and others and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後稍遷尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Later he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of Ritual Affairs in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of Ritual Affairs in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He had the reputation of fulfilling his office.
translations.idiomatic: He had the reputation of fulfilling his office well.

sentences.zh: 明帝末，丁憂在鄉，定州刺史廣陽王深召楷兼長史，委以州任。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ming's reign, while in mourning in his native place, Inspector of Dingzhou Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen summoned Kai as concurrent Chief Clerk and entrusted him with provincial duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Ming's reign, while in mourning in his native place, Inspector of Dingzhou Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen summoned Kai as concurrent Chief Clerk and entrusted him with provincial duties.

sentences.zh: 尋屬鮮于修禮、毛普賢等率北鎮流人反於州西北之左人城，屠村掠野，引向州城。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Xianyu Xiuli, Mao Puxian, and others led displaced people from the northern garrisons to rebel at Zuoren City northwest of the province, slaughtering villages and plundering the countryside, advancing toward the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon thereafter Xianyu Xiuli, Mao Puxian, and others led displaced people from the northern garrisons to rebel at Zuoren City northwest of the province, slaughtering villages and plundering the countryside as they advanced toward the provincial city.

sentences.zh: 州城內先有燕、恆、雲三州避難戶，修禮等聲雲，欲將此輩共為舉動。

translations.literal: Within the provincial city there were beforehand refugee households from Yan, Heng, and Yun provinces; Xiuli and others spread word that they wished to take these people together in a rising.
translations.idiomatic: Within the provincial city there were refugee households from Yan, Heng, and Yun provinces. Xiuli and others spread word that they wished to take these people together in a rising.

sentences.zh: 楷見人情不安，慮有變起，乃走收三州人中粗暴者殺之，以威外賊。

translations.literal: Kai saw the people's sentiments unsettled and feared a mutiny would arise; he thereupon ran to seize and kill the rough and violent among the three provinces' people, to awe the external bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Kai saw the people's sentiments unsettled and feared a mutiny would arise. He seized and killed the rough and violent among the refugees from the three provinces to awe the external bandits.

sentences.zh: 及刺史元冏、大都督揚津等至，楷乃還家。

translations.literal: When Inspector Yuan Jiong, Grand Commander Yang Jin, and others arrived, Kai thereupon returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Yuan Jiong, Grand Commander Yang Jin, and others arrived, Kai returned home.

sentences.zh: 後修禮等忿楷屠害北人，遂掘其父墓，載棺巡城，示相報復。

translations.literal: Later Xiuli and others resented Kai's slaughter of northerners; they thereupon dug up his father's tomb, loaded the coffin and paraded it around the city, showing mutual retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiuli and others, resenting Kai's slaughter of northerners, dug up his father's tomb, loaded the coffin, and paraded it around the city to show retaliation.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，徵為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後齊文襄取為儀同府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Later Qi Wenxiang took him as Advisory Staff Officer of the Equally Ranked Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi Wenxiang took him as Advisory Staff Officer of the Equally Ranked Office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈驃騎將軍、秘書監、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died, posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, and Inspector of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, and Inspector of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 琛從父弟密，字叔雍。

translations.literal: Chen's paternal cousin Mi, courtesy name Shuyong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's paternal cousin Mi, courtesy name Shuyong.

sentences.zh: 清謹少嗜欲，頗涉書史。

translations.literal: Clear and careful with few desires, he considerably involved himself in books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and careful with few desires, he read widely in books and histories.

sentences.zh: 疾世俗貪競，乾沒榮寵，曾為《風賦》以見意。

translations.literal: He detested worldly greed and competition, seizing glory and favor; he once composed a *Rhapsody on Wind* to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He detested worldly greed and competition and seizing glory and favor; he once composed a *Rhapsody on Wind* to express his views.

sentences.zh: 後參中山王英軍事。

translations.literal: Later he participated in Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he participated in Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 英鐘離敗退，鄉人蘇良沒於賊中，密盡私財以贖之。

translations.literal: When Ying was defeated and retreated at Zhongli, his fellow townsman Su Liang was lost among the bandits; Mi exhausted his private wealth to ransom him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying was defeated and retreated at Zhongli, his fellow townsman Su Liang was captured by bandits. Mi exhausted his private wealth to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 良歸，傾資報密。

translations.literal: When Liang returned, he poured out his wealth to repay Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang returned, he poured out his wealth to repay Mi.

sentences.zh: 密一皆不受，曰：「濟君之日，本不求貨，豈相贖之意。

translations.literal: Mi refused every bit, saying: "The day I helped you, I originally sought no goods—how could this be the intent of mutual ransom?"
translations.idiomatic: Mi refused everything, saying: "The day I helped you, I sought no payment—this was not meant as a ransom."

sentences.zh: 」及葛榮侵擾河北，詔密為相州行台，援守鄴城。

translations.literal: " When Ge Rong harassed Hebei, an edict made Mi Mobile Secretariat of Xiangzhou to reinforce and defend Ye City.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ge Rong harassed Hebei, an edict appointed Mi Mobile Secretariat of Xiangzhou to reinforce and defend Ye City.

sentences.zh: 莊帝以密全鄴勳，賞安市縣子。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang because of Mi's merit in preserving Ye rewarded him as Viscount of Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang rewarded him as Viscount of Anshi for his merit in preserving Ye.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，為衛尉卿，在官有平直之譽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign, he became Commandant of the Guard; in office he had a reputation for fairness and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he became Commandant of the Guard and earned a reputation for fairness and uprightness in office.

sentences.zh: 出為北徐州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Northern Xuzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Inspector of Northern Xuzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎將軍、儀同三司、瀛州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Third Rank, and Inspector of Yingzhou; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Third Rank, and Inspector of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 琛同郡張纂，字伯業。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan of the same commandery as Chen, courtesy name Boye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan of the same commandery as Chen, courtesy name Boye.

sentences.zh: 祖珍，字文表，慕容寶度支尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen, courtesy name Wenbiao, was Minister of Revenue under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen, courtesy name Wenbiao, was Minister of Revenue under Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 道武平中山，入魏，卒于涼州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, he entered Wei and died as Inspector of Liangzhou; posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, he entered Wei and died while serving as Inspector of Liangzhou, with the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 纂頗涉經史，雅有氣尚，交結勝流。

translations.literal: Zuan considerably involved himself in classics and histories, elegantly had spirited character, and formed connections with eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan read widely in the classics and histories, had an elegant and spirited character, and formed connections with eminent men.

sentences.zh: 為樂陵太守，在郡多所受納。

translations.literal: He was Grand Administrator of Leling; in the commandery he accepted much in bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand Administrator of Leling and accepted many bribes while in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 聞御史至，棄郡逃走，於是除名，乃卒。

translations.literal: Hearing censors had arrived, he abandoned the commandery and fled; thereupon his name was struck from the rolls, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that censors had arrived, he abandoned the commandery and fled. His name was struck from the rolls, and he died.

sentences.zh: 天平初，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, posthumously granted Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was posthumously granted Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 纂叔感，字崇仁，有器業，不應州郡之命。

translations.literal: Zuan's uncle Gan, courtesy name Chongren, had talent and achievement and did not respond to provincial and commandery appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's uncle Gan, courtesy name Chongren, had talent and achievement and did not respond to provincial and commandery appointments.

sentences.zh: 子宣軌，少孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: His son Xuan Gui, orphaned in youth, was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan Gui, orphaned in youth, was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 累遷相州撫軍府司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Marshal of the Pacification Army headquarters of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Marshal of the Pacification Army headquarters of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣軌性通率，輕財好施。

translations.literal: Xuan Gui's nature was open and direct; he lightly valued wealth and liked to give.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Gui's nature was open and direct; he lightly valued wealth and liked to give.

sentences.zh: 屬葛榮圍城，與刺史李神有固守效，以功賜爵中山公。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong besieged the city, he with Inspector Li Shen had the effect of firm defense; for merit he was granted the title Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged the city, he and Inspector Li Shen held firm in defense and he was granted the title Duke of Zhongshan for his merit.

sentences.zh: 後坐事死鄴。

translations.literal: Later convicted of an offense, he was executed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Later convicted of an offense, he was executed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 纂從弟元賓，位奉朝請。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger paternal cousin Yuan Bin held the post of Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger paternal cousin Yuan Bin held the post of Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 及外生高昂貴達，啟贈瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: When his maternal nephew Gao Ang reached noble advancement, a memorial posthumously granted Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his maternal nephew Gao Ang reached noble advancement, a memorial posthumously granted him Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高聰，字僧智，本勃海人也。

translations.literal: Gao Cong, courtesy name Sengzhi, was originally a native of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cong, courtesy name Sengzhi, was originally a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖軌，隨慕容德徙青州，因居北海之劇縣。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gui followed Murong De in moving to Qingzhou and thereupon settled in Ju County in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui followed Murong De in moving to Qingzhou and settled in Ju County in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 父法昂，少隨其車騎將軍王玄謨征伐，以功至員外郎，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Fa'ang in youth followed General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Xuanmo on campaign; for merit he reached Vice-Director and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fa'ang in youth followed General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Xuanmo on campaign, reached Vice-Director for his merit, and died early.

sentences.zh: 聰生而喪母，祖母王撫育之。

translations.literal: Cong from birth lost his mother; his grandmother Wang raised and nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong lost his mother at birth and was raised by his grandmother Wang.

sentences.zh: 大軍攻克東陽，聰徙平城，與蔣少遊為雲中兵戶，窘困無所不為。

translations.literal: When the great army captured Dongyang, Cong was moved to Pingcheng; with Jiang Shaoyou he became a military household of Yunzhong, in dire straits doing everything.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army captured Dongyang, Cong was moved to Pingcheng. With Jiang Shaoyou he became a military household of Yunzhong and in dire straits did everything he could to survive.

sentences.zh: 族祖允視之若孫，大加賙給。

translations.literal: His clan elder Yun treated him as a grandson and greatly aided and supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: His clan elder Yun treated him as a grandson and greatly aided and supplied him.

sentences.zh: 聰涉獵經史，頗有文才。

translations.literal: Cong ranged through classics and histories and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Cong read widely in the classics and histories and had considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 允嘉之，數稱其美，言之朝廷，由是與少遊同拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Yun praised him, repeatedly commending his excellence and speaking of him at court; thereby he with Shaoyou were together appointed Doctors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yun praised him, repeatedly commended his excellence, and spoke of him at court. Thereby Cong and Shaoyou were together appointed Doctors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉侍郎，為高陽王雍傅，稍為孝文知賞。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Director, he became Tutor to Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and gradually came to be known and appreciated by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Vice Director, he became Tutor to Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and gradually came to be known and appreciated by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，兼員外散騎常侍，使于齊。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, concurrently Vice Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was envoy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he served concurrently as Vice Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and was envoy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 後兼太子左率。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Later he concurrently served as Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 聰微習弓馬，乃以將略自許。

translations.literal: Cong slightly studied bow and horse and thereupon prided himself on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had some training in archery and horsemanship and prided himself on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 孝文銳意南討，專訪王肅以軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was keen on southern campaign and specially consulted Wang Su on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was keen on a southern campaign and specially consulted Wang Su on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 聰托肅，願以偏裨自效。

translations.literal: Cong entrusted himself to Su, wishing to serve as a subordinate commander.
translations.idiomatic: Cong entrusted himself to Su, wishing to serve as a subordinate commander.

sentences.zh: 肅言於帝，故假聰輔國將軍，受肅節度，同援渦陽。

translations.literal: Su spoke to the Emperor; therefore Cong was temporarily made General Who Supports the State, subject to Su's command, jointly reinforcing Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: Su spoke to the Emperor, and Cong was temporarily made General Who Supports the State, subject to Su's command, to reinforce Woyang jointly.

sentences.zh: 聰躁怯少威重，及與賊交，望風退敗。

translations.literal: Cong was impetuous and timid with little authority and weight; when he engaged the bandits, at sight of them he retreated in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was impetuous and timid with little authority. When he engaged the enemy, he retreated in defeat at the first sign of danger.

sentences.zh: 孝文恕死，徙平州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen pardoned him from death and exiled him to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen pardoned him from death and exiled him to Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 行屆瀛州，刺史王質獲白兔，將獻，托聰為表。

translations.literal: Passing through Yingzhou, Inspector Wang Zhi obtained a white hare and was about to present it; he entrusted Cong to compose the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Yingzhou, Inspector Wang Zhi obtained a white hare and was about to present it. He entrusted Cong to compose the memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝見表，顧王肅曰：「在下那得有此才，令朕不知。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw the memorial and turned to Wang Su, saying: "How could there be such talent below, that We did not know?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw the memorial and turned to Wang Su, saying: "How could there be such talent below that We did not know of?"

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「比高聰北徙，或其所制。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Recently Gao Cong was moved north—perhaps he composed it."
translations.idiomatic: " Su said: "Recently Gao Cong was moved north—perhaps he composed it."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟曰：「必應然也。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor understood and said: "It must indeed be so."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor understood and said: "It must indeed be so."

sentences.zh: 宣武初，聰復竊還京師，說高肇廢六輔。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu's reign, Cong secretly returned to the capital again and persuaded Gao Zhao to abolish the Six Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, Cong secretly returned to the capital again and persuaded Gao Zhao to abolish the Six Assistants.

sentences.zh: 宣武親政，除給事黃門侍郎，後加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power, Cong was appointed Attendant Within the Gates Who Handles Affairs; later Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary was added.
