translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power, Cong was appointed Attendant Within the Gates Who Handles Affairs and later given the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及幸鄴還，於河內懷界，帝射矢一里五十餘步。

translations.literal: When returning from visiting Ye, at the border of Huai in Henei, the Emperor shot an arrow one li and more than fifty paces.
translations.idiomatic: When returning from visiting Ye, at the border of Huai in Henei, the Emperor shot an arrow more than a li and fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 侍中高顯等奏，盛事奇跡必宜表述，請勒銘射宮，永彰聖藝。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Gao Xian and others submitted that such a great event and wondrous feat must be expressed; they requested an inscription carved at the archery palace to eternally display the sage's skill.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Gao Xian and others submitted that such a great event and wondrous feat must be recorded. They requested an inscription carved at the archery palace to eternally display the Emperor's skill.

sentences.zh: 遂刊銘射所，聰為之詞。

translations.literal: Thereupon an inscription was carved at the archery site; Cong composed its words.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an inscription was carved at the archery site, and Cong composed its words.

sentences.zh: 趙修嬖境，聰深朋附。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu was a favored minion; Cong deeply attached himself as a faction ally.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu was a favored minion, and Cong deeply attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 及詔追贈修父，聰為碑文，出入同載，觀視碑石。

translations.literal: When an edict posthumously granted Xiu's father, Cong composed the stele inscription; going in and out they rode together, viewing the stele stone.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict posthumously honored Xiu's father, Cong composed the stele inscription. They rode together going in and out, viewing the stele.

sentences.zh: 聰每見修，迎送盡禮。

translations.literal: Whenever Cong saw Xiu, he welcomed and escorted him with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cong saw Xiu, he welcomed and escorted him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 聰又為修作表，陳當時便宜，教其自安之術，由是迭相親狎。

translations.literal: Cong also composed memorials for Xiu, stating present conveniences and teaching him methods of self-preservation; thereby they became mutually intimate in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Cong also composed memorials for Xiu, stating present conveniences and teaching him methods of self-preservation. Thereby they became mutually intimate.

sentences.zh: 修死，甄琛、李憑皆被黜落，聰深用危慮，而先以疏宗之情，曲事高肇，竟獲自免，肇之力也。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Zhen Chen and Li Ping were all dismissed; Cong was deeply anxious, yet earlier because of distant clan kinship he fawningly served Gao Zhao and in the end obtained self-preservation—Zhao's power.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu died, Zhen Chen and Li Ping were all dismissed. Cong was deeply anxious, but because of distant clan kinship he had fawningly served Gao Zhao and in the end escaped punishment—thanks to Zhao's power.

sentences.zh: 修之任勢，聰傾身事之；

translations.literal: While Xiu held power, Cong devoted himself entirely to serving him;
translations.idiomatic: While Xiu held power, Cong devoted himself entirely to serving him;

sentences.zh: 及死，言必毀惡。

translations.literal: when he died, his words were always to slander and revile.
translations.idiomatic: when he died, Cong always spoke to slander and revile him.

sentences.zh: 茹皓之寵，聰又媚附，每相招命，稱皓才識非修之儔。

translations.literal: When Ru Hao was favored, Cong again fawned and attached; whenever they summoned each other, he praised Hao's talent and insight as not Xiu's equal.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru Hao was favored, Cong again fawned and attached himself. Whenever they met, he praised Hao's talent and insight as far surpassing Xiu's.

sentences.zh: 乃因皓啟請田宅，皆被遂許。

translations.literal: Thereupon through Hao he memorialized requesting fields and houses—all were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon through Hao he memorialized requesting fields and houses, and all were granted.

sentences.zh: 及皓見罪戮，聰以為死之晚也。

translations.literal: When Hao was condemned and executed, Cong considered his death overdue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was condemned and executed, Cong considered his death overdue.

sentences.zh: 其薄於情義皆如此。

translations.literal: His thinness in sentiment and righteousness were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His thinness in sentiment and righteousness were all like this.

sentences.zh: 侍中高顯為護軍，聰代兼其任。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Gao Xian was Protector of the Army; Cong replaced him concurrently in the post.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Gao Xian was Protector of the Army, and Cong replaced him concurrently in the post.

sentences.zh: 顯與兄肇疑聰間構而求之。

translations.literal: Xian and his elder brother Zhao suspected Cong of intrigue and sought to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and his elder brother Zhao suspected Cong of intrigue and sought to remove him.

sentences.zh: 聰居兼十餘旬，出入機要，言即真，無遠慮，藉貴因權，耽於聲色，賄納之音，聞於遐邇。

translations.literal: Cong held the concurrent post for more than ten ten-day periods, entering and exiting crucial affairs; his words were immediately enacted, without far-sighted consideration; borrowing nobility and wielding power, he indulged in sound and color; reports of bribery and acceptance were heard near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Cong held the concurrent post for more than three months, entering and exiting crucial affairs. His words were immediately enacted without far-sighted consideration. Borrowing nobility and wielding power, he indulged in pleasure, and reports of bribery were heard near and far.

sentences.zh: 中尉崔亮知肇微恨，遂面陳聰罪，出為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang knew Zhao's slight resentment and thereupon face-to-face stated Cong's crimes; he was sent out as Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang knew Zhao's slight resentment and thereupon stated Cong's crimes to his face. Cong was sent out as Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 聰善於去就，知肇嫌之，側身承奉，肇遂待之如舊。

translations.literal: Cong was skilled at advancing and retreating; knowing Zhao resented him, he bent himself in service and Zhao thereupon treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was skilled at advancing and retreating. Knowing Zhao resented him, he bent himself in service, and Zhao thereupon treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 聰在并州數歲，多不率法，又與太原太守王椿有隙，再為大使御史舉奏。

translations.literal: Cong in Bingzhou for several years mostly did not follow law; also he had a rift with Grand Administrator of Taiyuan Wang Chun and was twice impeached by envoy censors.
translations.idiomatic: Cong spent several years in Bingzhou mostly failing to follow the law. He also had a rift with Grand Administrator of Taiyuan Wang Chun and was twice impeached by envoy censors.

sentences.zh: 肇每以宗私相援，事得寢緩。

translations.literal: Zhao each time aided him out of clan private interest; the matters were shelved and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao each time aided him out of clan loyalty, and the matters were shelved and delayed.

sentences.zh: 宣武末，拜散騎常侍、平北將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanwu's reign, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 明帝踐阼，以其素附高肇，出為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, because he had long attached to Gao Zhao, Cong was sent out as Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, because Cong had long attached himself to Gao Zhao, he was sent out as Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以高肇之党，與王世義、高綽、李憲、崔楷、蘭氛之為中尉元匡所彈，靈太后並特原之。

translations.literal: Soon as a member of Gao Zhao's faction, together with Wang Shiyi, Gao Chuo, Li Xian, Cui Kai, and Lan Fen he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang; Empress Dowager Ling specially pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as a member of Gao Zhao's faction, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang together with Wang Shiyi, Gao Chuo, Li Xian, Cui Kai, and Lan Fen. Empress Dowager Ling specially pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 聰遂廢於家，斷絕人事，唯修營園果，世稱高聰梨，以為珍異。

translations.literal: Cong thereupon was idle at home, cutting off human relations, only cultivating gardens and fruit—the world called them Gao Cong pears, considering them rare and exotic.
translations.idiomatic: Cong thereupon lived in retirement at home, cutting off human relations and cultivating gardens and fruit. The world called them Gao Cong pears and considered them rare delicacies.

sentences.zh: 又唯以聲色自娛。

translations.literal: Also he only amused himself with sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: He also amused himself only with music and women.

sentences.zh: 後拜光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and died.

sentences.zh: 靈太后聞其亡，嗟惋良久。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling heard of his death, she sighed and lamented for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling heard of his death, she sighed and lamented for a long time.

sentences.zh: 贈青州刺史，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Inspector of Qingzhou; posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Inspector of Qingzhou with the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 聰有妓十餘人，有子無子皆注籍為妾，以悅其情。

translations.literal: Cong had more than ten courtesans; whether they had sons or not, all were registered as concubines to please their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had more than ten courtesans. Whether they had sons or not, all were registered as concubines to please them.

sentences.zh: 及病，欲不適他人，並令燒指吞炭，出家為尼。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, wishing they not go to others, he had them all burn their fingers and swallow charcoal, leaving home to become nuns.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, wishing they not go to others, he had them all burn their fingers and swallow charcoal and become Buddhist nuns.

sentences.zh: 聰所作文筆二十卷。

translations.literal: Cong's literary compositions totaled twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's literary compositions totaled twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 長子雲，字彥鴻，位輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yun, courtesy name Yanhong, held the posts of General Who Supports the State and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yun, courtesy name Yanhong, held the posts of General Who Supports the State and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 河陰遇害，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He met harm at Heyin; posthumously granted Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin and was posthumously granted Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 論曰：韓麒麟由才器識用，遂見紀于齊士。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Han Qilin through talent, capacity, and recognized employment was thereupon recorded among the worthies of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Han Qilin, through talent, capacity, and recognized employment, was recorded among the worthies of Qi.

sentences.zh: 顯宗以文學自立，而時務屢陳；

translations.literal: Xianzong established himself through literary learning and repeatedly stated affairs of the time;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong established himself through literary learning and repeatedly addressed affairs of the time;

sentences.zh: 至於實錄之功，未之聞也。

translations.literal: as for achievement in true records, none has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: but achievement in true historical records has not been heard of.

sentences.zh: 子熙清尚自守，榮過其器。

translations.literal: Zi Xi was pure and elevated in self-preservation; honor exceeded his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xi was pure and elevated in self-preservation, but honor exceeded his capacity.

sentences.zh: 程駿才業見知，蓋當時之長策。

translations.literal: Cheng Jun's talent and achievement were recognized—probably the long strategy of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jun's talent and achievement were recognized—probably the best policy of the time.

sentences.zh: 李彪生自微族，見擢明世，輶軒驟指，聲駭江南，執筆立言，遂為良史。

translations.literal: Li Biao born from a humble clan was raised in a bright age; envoy carriages suddenly pointed south, his fame startling Jiangnan; holding the brush and establishing words, he thereupon became a good historian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao, born from a humble clan, was raised in a bright age. Envoy carriages suddenly pointed south and his fame startled the south. Holding the brush and establishing words, he became a good historian.

sentences.zh: 逮於直繩在手，厲氣明目，持堅無術，末路蹉跎。

translations.literal: When it came to the straight rope in hand, fierce spirit and bright eyes, holding firm without method—his final path was wasted and stumbling.
translations.idiomatic: When the straight rope was in his hand, he showed fierce spirit and bright eyes, but holding firm without method, his final path was wasted and stumbling.

sentences.zh: 行百里者半於九十，彪之謂也。

translations.literal: He who travels a hundred li is half done at ninety—this applies to Biao.
translations.idiomatic: He who travels a hundred li is half done at ninety—this applies to Biao.

sentences.zh: 高道悅謇直之風，見憚於世，醜正貽禍，有可悲乎！

translations.literal: Gao Daoyue's forthright and upright wind was feared by the world; uglifying the upright brings disaster—is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daoyue's forthright and upright character was feared by the world. Uglifying the upright brings disaster—is it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 甄琛以學尚刀筆，早樹聲名；

translations.literal: Zhen Chen through learning honoring brush and knife early established fame;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen, through learning and skill with the brush, early established fame;

sentences.zh: 受遇三朝，終至崇重。

translations.literal: favored through three reigns, in the end reaching honored weight.
translations.idiomatic: was favored through three reigns and in the end reached honored eminence.

sentences.zh: 高聰才尚見知，名位顯著。

translations.literal: Gao Cong's talent was recognized and known; name and rank were prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cong's talent was recognized; his name and rank were prominent.

sentences.zh: 而異軌同奔，咸經于危覆之轍，惜乎！

translations.literal: Yet different tracks ran the same course—all passed through the ruts of peril and overturn—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet though their paths differed, all ran the same course through the ruts of peril and ruin—alas!
